Unlike prior B/AH, unique coverage is not summed as independent benefit; unlike prior L, KL mismatch is the production law rather than a residual support penalty around proportional; unlike HRC, no outcome-selected capacity transition is introduced. The fitted amplitudes a_i=M q_i are nonnegative and their normalization recovers q.

title: Final shared-surrogate admissibility audit

title: Adversarial audit of the negative shared-surrogate decision
material_novelty: Introduces no fitted mechanism. It re-derives the negative decision from persisted source predictions rather than the synthesis prose, tests whether the primary exact-pair diagnostic rewards a shrunk phase response, establishes the observational status of a 300M two-phase advantage directly from the 238 exact contrasts and their trained single-phase counterparts, and checks each frozen disqualifier for protocol dependence and search-boundary artifacts.
evidence: Decision survives. The exact-pair diagnostic is sound: against a zero-delta null of 0.017990/0.036104, HPR scores 0.007850/0.016902 at amplitude ratio 0.881/0.800 and calibration slope 1.021/1.109, so it is not a shrunk predictor. Governing fact: 0/238 asymmetric policies beat the best tied policy on either target (0.951105 vs 0.955440; 0.982774 vs 0.988999), and the winning tied rows are physically trained singleavg runs, so HPR's near-tied optimum is correct rather than deficient. Phase benefit is monotone in aggregate suboptimality on both panels, Spearman -0.467/-0.497 (p 2.6e-14/2.8e-16) and +0.976 on WSD80, with best-decile splitting penalty +0.0119/+0.0310 (Wilcoxon p 1e-4, paired; the design has zero replicated coordinates). Two disqualifiers fail: the broad-text false gains are 0.029430/0.029460 under random folds but 0.003185/0.002973 under blocked folds, passing the frozen 0.005 threshold, and the late multiplier is pinned at its grid maximum in 6/6 folds under a grid inherited from the delphi_3e18 panel. Extending that grid to (1,2,4,8,16) halves the reported gap: all_rmse goes from +15.4%/+16.2% to +8.1%/+7.7% versus HPR and pair_rmse from +18.8%/+15.2% to +9.9%/+6.9%, so the frozen gate evidence overstated the deficit, though the 5% tolerance still fails. An intermediate claim that the multiplier saturates every bound offered, and is therefore unidentified, was tested and RETRACTED. Sweeping it at the selected shape shows an interior optimum near 8-16 on both targets, with 64 clearly worse than 8, and a confirmation fit with the ceiling raised to 64 selects 16 in 5/6 folds and 8 in the remaining fold, leaving the ceiling unused and reproducing the ceiling-16 metrics exactly. Closing the offset channel by tying E0 to the multiplier does not remove its gain but slightly enlarges it, -17.6%/-13.5% against -16.6%/-8.3%, so the multiplier is a real effect rather than a reparameterization: early exposure carries roughly eight to sixteen times less predictive weight than late exposure at 300M, estimable from endpoint data. NG-LK should therefore not be cited as requiring trajectories to identify the multiplier; the scalar is identified, and what a trajectory panel buys is separating retention, forgetting, repetition and optimizer-time evolution, which all collapse into it. The corner optimum is not a grid artifact: it persists and worsens to full degeneracy under the widest grid, phase TV 1.000000 and max bucket weight 1.000000 on uncheatable, against a maximum observed achievable gain of about 0.049 anywhere in the 238 exact contrasts. With the multiplier identified at an interior value the pathology cannot be attributed to a constrained search and is intrinsic to the form. The gate evidence string also overstates boundary pinning for retention and ridge, which are interior in 2/6 folds each.
reopen_condition: No promotion. The late multiplier is identified from endpoint data at an interior 8-16, so the trajectory panel must be justified by mechanism separation rather than multiplier identification: one scalar cannot distinguish retention, forgetting, within-window repetition and optimizer-time evolution. The ratio of achievable phase gain to the aggregate penalty it costs is 0.50-0.71 across 300M and 0.21-0.75 on WSD80 for a>=0.35, but 1.935 at WSD80 a=0.18, which is the entire observed two-phase advantage. Excess magnitude does not explain it (a=0.18 excess 0.0103 gives gain 0.0199; a=0.35 excess 0.0081 gives 0.0017); the direction of departure from the tied optimum does. A trajectory panel must vary phase-boundary placement at aggregates both below and above the tied optimum and measure that ratio directly, so that the late multiplier is identified by intermediate evaluations rather than absorbed at a search boundary.

title: Interference-limited evidence state
material_novelty: Bounded acquisition composed with composition-driven forgetting. Per bucket, a=1-exp(-rho*eps0), h=exp(-mu*beta1*(1-w1)), s=1-(1-h*a)*exp(-rho*eps1). The materially new element is the transition law h: phase-0 evidence for bucket i decays in proportion to the phase-1 token mass spent on other buckets, so forgetting depends on the composition of the later phase rather than its duration. SUR-060/061 decay unconditionally in time and therefore assign identical decay to two policies with equal exposure and equal phase lengths; this law does not. mu=0 gives s=1-exp(-rho*E_total) exactly, so the phase-weighted-dose null is nested exactly and is an exact ablation. No phase-local replay or repetition term is included, so the SUR-019 prohibition is respected; over-exposure enters only as the phase-blind D=max(0,E-1).
evidence: Absolute-interference law h=exp(-mu*beta1*(1-w1)) fails the preregistered non-identification stop on WSD80. Both nonlinear parameters pin at opposite grid boundaries in 29/29 metrics under both fold protocols and both fitting modes: rho=0.05 (grid minimum) and mu=32 (grid maximum). The degenerate limit rho->0, mu->inf reduces the state to rho*eps1, a pure last-phase-only recency model, which over-predicts the Programming-Languages two-phase gain 6.6x (0.06296 versus observed 0.009594), places the optimum 0.099 from (0.10,0.50), and predicts 0.0201/0.0205 BPB of phase gain on the C4 English and RefinedWeb negative controls. Interior OOF RMSE is 0.0283 versus repaired RPL 0.0076. Cause is diagnosed rather than assumed: the absolute law is not tied-neutral, so mu is identified from the curvature of the tied aggregate response and the phase prediction is inherited rather than fitted. The exact mu=0 ablation reproduces zero gain to 5e-10, so the phase-blind nesting itself is correct. CORRECTION after independent review: the boundary claim holds for joint full fits (29/29 both protocols) and for independent full fits at 27/29 random and 26/29 blocked, but the REGISTERED rule is a majority of folds. Under random folds it fires (29/29 joint, 27/29 independent); under blocked folds it does not (0/29 joint, 2/29 independent). The non-identification is therefore protocol-dependent, severe under random folds and largely absent under blocked ones. The eight-fiber profile adds a partial credit not visible in the scalar gates: this is the only law that reproduces the observed contrast sign change, predicting +0.359 at aggregate 0.18 against +0.400 observed, and it fails by extrapolating that rule to high aggregate where it invents a +0.196 BPB gain.
reopen_condition: Cheapest falsification: on the exact aggregate-matched 300M pairs and the WSD80 fixed-aggregate fibers, mu must select an interior value in a majority of inner folds and the predicted broad-text phase gain must stay at or below 0.005 BPB while code targets keep their observed gain. If mu selects 0 or the grid maximum in a majority of folds, report unidentified and do not extend the grid.

title: Multi-target shared-state identification
material_novelty: Estimates one shared nonlinear transition theta simultaneously from every metric measured on the same checkpoints under one weighted objective, with a small interpretable linear head per target. SUR-043 froze a shape selected on Programming Languages and then refitted heads, a sequential transfer; this is simultaneous identification, so metrics that individually cannot identify theta still contribute to pinning it. SUR-062 varied response resolution at frozen transition parameters and did not change how the transition is identified. Exact aggregates are derived rather than double counted: the Table-9 macro is reconstructed from 47 leaves plus one derived MMLU-bucket mean, and Uncheatable components and macro are never taken from the same row. Folds group all labels of a policy together.
evidence: The registered gate has now been evaluated properly, after the review showed the harness had bootstrapped RMSE rather than the registered selection and gain diagnostics. Paired bootstrap of Regret@1 and Regret@5 over interior rows, 4000 draws, identical draws across fitting modes. Four diagnostics improve beyond uncertainty, clearing the "at least two" bar, but every one sits on the ABSOLUTE law, which fails every representability gate in the round; every one is under random folds only; every one is on the two GitHub controls and never on the primary target, where the difference is exactly 0.000000; and k=1 and k=5 on one target are not independent diagnostics, so four cells are two targets. Under blocked folds the same law is significantly WORSE jointly on GitHub C++ (+0.018030, CI 0.001170 to 0.030883), as is share-drop (+0.169871, CI 0.034526 to 0.214896). For the recency law, the only tied-neutral two-sided mechanism, not one diagnostic improves and three are worse. The substantive result is the divergence: sharing improved out-of-fold RMSE on every code target for every law under blocked folds by 0.017 to 0.095 BPB with all intervals excluding zero, while leaving selection regret unchanged or significantly worse under those same folds. Prediction quality and policy choice move in opposite directions on this panel. The corrected information audit stands: the metrics carry about 3.46 effective independent labels, so sharing has real information to exploit; it just does not convert into better selection here.
reopen_condition: The identification question is answered for this panel and this model family: sharing helps prediction and not selection. Reopen only with a selection-aware estimator, one that shares the nonlinear shape under a loss targeting the optimum region rather than pooled squared error, or on a panel where prediction and selection do not diverge.

title: Share-drop interference evidence state
material_novelty: Replaces the SUR-084 retention law with h=exp(-mu*beta1*max(0, w0-w1)): a bucket loses stored evidence only in proportion to the fall in its own representation between the phases. The law is exactly one on every tied policy, so unlike SUR-084 the interference rate contributes nothing to the aggregate response and is identified from asymmetric policies alone. Unlike SUR-070 it needs no counterfactual tied late distribution, only the realized phase mixtures. Unlike SUR-060 the decay depends on composition rather than elapsed time. The repair is diagnosed from SUR-084 selection traces, not chosen from gate outcomes.
evidence: The structural claim is FALSIFIED AS STATED and holds only conditionally. A one-sided share-drop penalty cannot produce a fixed-aggregate gain only while every bucket net evidence coefficient stays non-negative. The head bounds family amplitudes below at zero but lets bucket departures range over [-50, 50], so the net can go negative and the subtraction becomes a gain. Across 58 metric-protocol cells, 4 reach a negative net coefficient; twitterAAE_HELM_fixed under blocked folds reaches net -0.0579 with a fixed-aggregate gain of +0.021627 BPB. On the primary Programming Languages target the net coefficients are [0.5011, 0.7261] and the fiber gain is exactly 0.000000, which is why the primary-target result still shows a tied optimum and a gain of -8.98e-06. Tied neutrality itself remains exact (0.00e+00). The eight-fiber profile independently confirms the law never produces a positive contrast on the primary target at any aggregate. The backbone finding is unaffected: interior OOF RMSE 0.0546 to 0.1268 against repaired RPL 0.0076 where the phase channel is inert.
reopen_condition: Any future use of a one-sided law must enforce non-negative NET evidence coefficients, for example by parameterizing departures as within-family contrasts bounded so the family level dominates. Without that the structural argument does not apply.

title: Two-sided recency-exposure evidence state
material_novelty: Third and final law in the family. kappa=exp(-mu*beta1*(w0-w1)) discounts a bucket-phase-0 exposure when its share falls between the phases and credits it when its share rises, and the state is s=1-exp(-rho*(kappa*eps0+eps1)). Acting on exposure rather than on acquired mass keeps s bounded in [0,1) without requiring kappa to be a probability, which is what forced SUR-086 to be one-sided. It is exactly the two-sided omission-and-reactivation transition that the SUR-023 reopen condition requires, and it is justified by a structural derivation rather than by residuals: on a simplex every share rise is another share fall, so a one-sided law can only subtract and can never produce a two-phase gain on a fixed-aggregate fiber. kappa is exactly 1 on tied policies, so mu cannot shape the aggregate response; mu=0 reduces the state to 1-exp(-rho*E_total) exactly.
evidence: The pre-run prediction was half right and the route fails anyway. The interference rate is genuinely interior (8.0 in two of three folds, 16.0 in the third, on a grid reaching 32.0), confirming that a tied-neutral two-sided law lets mu be identified from asymmetric policies alone. But the acquisition rate selects rho=5.0, the grid MAXIMUM, in 58/58 metric-mode cells, so the preregistered non-identification stop applies and the grid was not extended. On Programming Languages (random folds, joint): predicted gain 0.000109 against observed 0.009594; predicted optimum (0.050,0.045) at distance 0.4727 from (0.10,0.50); Regret@1 0.135778 against repaired RPL 0.002842; interior OOF RMSE 0.045296 against 0.007575. It is the only candidate that passes the broad-text negative-control gate (0.001955 and 0.002065 against the 0.005 limit, where repaired RPL predicts 0.0294), but it passes because its phase channel is nearly silent everywhere. The decisive diagnostic is the ablation: switching the phase channel off improves Regret@1 from 0.135778 to 0.006290, a factor of 21, while the paired bootstrap shows the phase channel improving interior OOF RMSE by 0.016181 BPB (95% CI -0.021244 to -0.010968, p=0.000). It fits better and selects far worse, which is verbatim a charter rejection condition.
reopen_condition: Same preregistered non-identification stop: if either nonlinear parameter pins at a grid boundary in a majority of metrics, report unidentified and do not extend the grid. If it passes WSD80 it must still clear the 300M core RMSE and Regret@1 gates against HPR on identical rows and folds.

title: Power-approach acquisition curve for the evidence state
material_novelty: Not a new mechanism: an exact nested generalization of the acquisition curve inside SUR-087, made because the exponential curve was measured to be the binding misspecification rather than assumed to be adequate. acquired(x)=1-(1+rho*x/nu)^-nu replaces 1-exp(-rho*x); nu=infinity is the exponential exactly and is inside the grid, so the extension can never fit worse. Power-law approach to saturation is the form the scaling-law literature supports and the form RPL already uses for its benefit term. Verified before fitting to preserve every algebraic property of SUR-087 at every grid value: mu=0 total-epoch nesting exact to 0.00e+00, tied mu-independence exact to 0.00e+00, state bounded, and nu=1e7 reproduces the exponential to 2.7e-08.
evidence: The registered prediction that interior RMSE falls substantially is confirmed on the aggregate backbone alone: fitted on the 20 tied WSD80 coordinates, where the phase channel is inert by construction, the power-approach curve reaches RMSE 0.007906 against the panel training-seed sigma 0.004633, about 1.7 seed sigma, where the exponential curve could not reach the tied response at any rate. The registered prediction that nu selects a finite interior value fails: the tied-only fit selects nu=0.25, the grid minimum, and the full nested fit selects rho=5.0, the grid maximum. The generalization is therefore a real and reusable repair of the aggregate backbone, not a promotable model, and no further link variant is licensed.
reopen_condition: Same non-identification stop applies to nu as to rho and mu. If the interior RMSE does not approach the repaired-RPL reference even with the extended curve, the conclusion is that this evidence-state family cannot represent the WSD80 aggregate response and no further link variant is licensed.

title: Two-timescale exposure response
material_novelty: Every law tested in SUR-084/086/087 modifies ONE exposure index, and a one-index model provably cannot beat the best tied policy: any two-phase policy shares its index value with some tied policy, so its loss is attainable on the diagonal. WSD80 measures a +0.009594 BPB gain over the ENTIRE tied class, which refutes the whole one-index family at once. This is the minimal escape: TWO exposure indices with different memory horizons. For timescale k in {slow, fast}, E_k,i = (1-phi_k)*w0_i + phi_k*w1_i, evidence s_k,i = 1-(1+rho*c_i*E_k,i/nu)^-nu, and L = b - sum_k sum_i alpha_k,i s_k,i + damage. The tied policy class is exactly the diagonal E_slow = E_fast = w, so an off-diagonal minimum is reachable and is what produces a gain no constant mixture can match. Mechanism: different capabilities integrate the data stream over different horizons, their optimal mixtures differ, and a two-phase schedule serves both at once. Unlike SUR-061 this is a static response with no ODE and no trajectory fitting, so the SUR-061 reopen condition about time-varying response calibration does not apply. phi_slow = phi_fast collapses it to a single index, which is exactly the phase-weighted-dose null, so the null is nested exactly.
evidence: By a wide margin the best candidate the project has produced, and still not promotable. The registered falsification did NOT fire: the horizons come out well separated (slow=0.55, fast=1.00) rather than collapsing to a single index, and the single-index collapse is verified exact at 0.00e+00. Interior OOF RMSE 0.008500 against repaired RPL 0.007575, versus 0.028-0.055 for the three one-index laws. The fiber profile is the reason to take it seriously: predicted contrast changes sign at exactly a=0.30, the measured tied optimum, and tracks the observed contrast within 0.052 on seven of eight fibers; predicted fiber GAINS track observed ones to a mean absolute error of 0.0064 across a range spanning 0.000 to 0.243. Three frozen gates still fail: global gain 0.016004 against observed 0.009594 (error 0.006410 > 0.004439), optimum distance 0.1180 > 0.05, Regret@1 0.006290 > 0.004842. The failure is localized: the model puts its optimum at aggregate 0.105 where the data says 0.18, so the residual error is in the AGGREGATE BACKBONE at low aggregate, not in the phase mechanism. Provenance caveat: the horizon grid was corrected post-outcome after slow pinned at an arbitrary 0.45 cap; under the original grid the gain gate passed (0.006615) and under the corrected grid it fails (0.016004), so the earlier pass was a grid artifact and is not claimed.
reopen_condition: The phase mechanism is not the blocker; the aggregate backbone at low aggregate is. Next step is to fit the two-timescale phase structure on top of an aggregate response validated independently on the tied diagonal, rather than fitting both jointly. Any promotion also needs the post-outcome grid correction confirmed on held evidence.

title: Superlinear over-exposure damage for the two-timescale response
material_novelty: Not a new mechanism: one shared exponent on the over-exposure term of SUR-089, added because the misfit was localized rather than assumed. With linear damage max(0, E-1) the tied response is a saturating benefit minus a term linear in epochs, which produces a broad bowl; measured backbone residuals over-predict loss at the tied optimum by +0.0109, +0.0111 and +0.0132 BPB at w=0.30, 0.35 and 0.40, that is 2.4 to 2.9 seed sigma, while being small elsewhere. Replacing the damage with max(0, E-1)^tau lets marginal damage grow with exposure and sharpens the minimum. Repetition hurting superlinearly is the standard reading and the incumbent RPL already carries damage_exponent=2.0, so this brings the family into line with the model it is being measured against rather than inventing anything. tau=1 recovers SUR-089 exactly and is inside the grid.
evidence: Half the registered signature fired and the decisive half did not. Superlinear damage does sharpen the bowl: tied RMSE improves from 0.007906 to 0.006198 (1.71 to 1.34 seed sigma) and the optimum-region residuals fall from +0.0109/+0.0111/+0.0132 to +0.0072/+0.0061/+0.0075, that is from 2.4-2.9 down to 1.3-1.6 seed sigma. But tau selects 3.0, the grid MAXIMUM, which is the registered boundary stop, and the residuals at w=0.30, 0.35 and 0.40 remain the SAME SIGN and above one seed sigma. A systematic same-sign residual across the whole optimum region is a shape error the family cannot absorb, not noise. Per the registered reopen condition this means the aggregate response family is wrong rather than mis-parameterized, and no further damage variant is licensed. The grid was not extended.
reopen_condition: Closed. The binding constraint is no longer the phase mechanism but the aggregate response family: a saturating benefit minus a power damage term cannot reproduce the observed tied bowl near its minimum. The next aggregate family must be identified independently, which is what WSD80-SUR-073 exists to do.

title: Inverse-power aggregate backbone carrying the two-timescale phase structure
material_novelty: Replaces the bounded evidence state of SUR-089/090 with an inverse-power benefit, and keeps the two exposure indices. Diagnosis is structural, not a grid issue: the observed tied response DIVERGES as the code share goes to zero, 1.5935 BPB at w=0 against a 0.9451 minimum, and a state bounded in [0,1) cannot produce a divergence at all, which is why its bowl is too shallow at the minimum and why a free damage exponent pinned at its bound without fixing the same-sign residuals. Benefit becomes b_k,i = (c_i E_k,i + eps0)^-gamma with E_k,i = (1-phi_k) w0_i + phi_k w1_i, damage stays max(0, E_tot-1)^tau, and L = b + sum_k sum_f alpha_k,f b_k,f + sum_f eta_f d_f with alpha, eta >= 0. The inverse-power benefit is exactly the incumbent RPL aggregate form, so this is not a new aggregate invention; the novelty is the composition. RPL pairs that backbone with retention plus a late multiplier, which is a ONE-index reweighting and is refuted wholesale by the structural argument in SUR-089: one index cannot beat the best tied policy, and WSD80 measures +0.009594 over the entire tied class. This route keeps the aggregate form that demonstrably fits and replaces the phase channel that demonstrably cannot. phi_slow = phi_fast collapses to a single index exactly.
evidence: The registered reopen condition fired. A divergent inverse-power benefit, the same form the incumbent RPL uses, does NOT fix the tied bowl: tied RMSE 0.006634 (1.43 seed sigma) against 0.006198 (1.34) for the bounded state it replaced, so it is slightly worse, tau pins at the grid maximum again, and the residuals at w=0.30/0.35/0.40 remain +0.0069/+0.0072/+0.0099, still sharing one sign. Two structurally different benefit families, bounded-saturating and divergent inverse-power, each with a free damage exponent, fail the same way. Per the registered condition the aggregate problem is therefore NOT the functional form, and no further aggregate variant is licensed from this panel alone. A separate hypothesis was tested and REFUTED in the process: the SUR-089 gain overshoot is not caused by an inflated tied comparator. The model UNDER-predicts the best tied policy (0.938883 against 0.945062 observed, -0.006179), so correcting the comparator would raise the predicted gain to 0.022183 and make the gate failure worse. The overshoot is optimism at an extrapolated corner: the model under-predicts the two-phase optimum by -0.012589, roughly twice its tied optimism, and places that optimum at (0.030, 0.405) where the surface is sparsely sampled.
reopen_condition: Same boundary stop on every nonlinear parameter. If the tied residuals at the optimum keep a common sign even with a divergent benefit, the aggregate problem is not the functional form and no further aggregate variant is licensed from this panel alone.

title: Cross-scale aggregate form sweep with per-cell parameters
material_novelty: Selects an aggregate functional form using 150 tied coordinates across 10 (N,D) cells rather than the 20 on the WSD80 diagonal, refitting every candidate independently per cell so the form stays fittable from a single swarm at a single scale. Five forms compared against each cell own replicate noise.
evidence: Best form is inverse-power plus damage with per-domain exponents at median 1.60 cell-noise sigma, 3/10 cells within 1.5. Damage is necessary (median 2.26 without). The data-constrained effective-unique-tokens law is far the worst at 5.39 median and 27.78 worst. Per-domain exponents are real, gamma_code 0.05-0.5 versus gamma_broad 0.3-1.0, but worth only 1.69->1.60. Decisive: repaired RPL itself sits at 1.63 sigma on WSD80, so these backbones already match the incumbent and the aggregate response was mis-identified as the blocker. Two further hypotheses refuted: the gain overshoot is not an inflated tied comparator (the model UNDER-predicts it, 0.938883 vs 0.945062, and correcting raises the gain to 0.022183), and it is not phi_fast running to its 1.00 bound (constraining it to the independently measured 0.62-0.84 band worsens RMSE 0.008459->0.014768 and gain 0.015087->0.032212).
reopen_condition: The open defect is that every fitted surface in this family is monotone in early code share down to the support boundary: the interior optimum sits at (0.030, 0.410) under both free and constrained horizons, and 0.030 is the boundary margin. Next candidates in order: an interior penalty on early code share, a non-additive domain interaction, a log-deficit response above a fitted floor, and composition with SUR-073 once its sealed gate resolves.

title: Horizon-consistent damage
material_novelty: Removes an index mismatch that every earlier variant carried. Benefit was read from the horizon-weighted effective exposure while damage was read from raw total epochs, where phase-0 weight carries 21.09 starcoder epochs per unit against phase-1 5.37. Starving the early phase therefore cut damage about four times harder than it cut benefit, a free lunch that drove every fitted optimum to the support boundary. Benefit and damage now read the SAME effective exposure at each horizon, so reducing early weight trades benefit against damage at every horizon and the asymmetry disappears.
evidence: Diagnosis confirmed: the optimum un-pins from the boundary. It moves from (0.030,0.410), where 0.030 IS the boundary margin and was identical under free and constrained horizons, to a genuinely interior (0.130,0.415). Optimum distance 0.1140 -> 0.0901. Interior OOF RMSE 0.008459 -> 0.008184, the closest any candidate has come to repaired RPL 0.007575, 8% worse. Regret@1 0.006290 -> 0.006216. Predicted gain flips from 1.6x overshoot (+0.015087) to 2.5x undershoot (+0.003832), bracketing the observed +0.009594. All three gates still fail but every metric improved simultaneously, which no earlier change achieved. Selected slow=0.45 fast=1.0 gamma_code=0.2 gamma_broad=0.2 offset=0.05 tau=3.0; fast and tau remain at grid bounds.
reopen_condition: Gain now brackets the target between this variant and SUR-089, so the remaining error is amplitude calibration rather than structure. Next: the predicted optimum sits at p1=0.415 against 0.500 observed, so the fast horizon still under-rewards late code. fast and tau at their bounds must be resolved before promotion.

title: Separate damage horizon
material_novelty: Gives repetition damage its own memory horizon, separate from the two benefit horizons. Motivated by a bracket rather than a guess: damage read from raw total epochs gave gain +0.015087 and damage read from the fast benefit horizon gave +0.003832, so the observed +0.009594 lies between them and a free damage horizon spans the bracket. Mechanistically, benefit and repetition harm need not be felt over the same memory.
evidence: HEADLINE WITHDRAWN after independent Codex 5.6 Sol review. The claim that this beats the incumbent on fit does not survive matched evaluation. Shape selection over 17,280 candidates uses the SAME three held-out partitions later reported as out-of-fold, so the seven nonlinear parameters see the test outcomes. A matched 3-by-3 NESTED rerun gives interior RMSE 0.008040 rather than 0.006746, an optimism of 0.001294 or 19.2%. That is 1.061x repaired RPL 0.007575 and misses the 5% core-RMSE gate by 0.000086, so the comparison is inconclusive and NOT a win. The frozen evaluation ladder already required nonlinear selection inside inner folds. Identification is also unresolved, and worse than reported: I checked only tau and fast, but slow=0.45 sits at max(SLOW) and gamma_broad=0.2 at min(GB), two arbitrary bounds I never examined. Adding slow=0.40 or GB=0.15 already lowers the selection objective, so the winner moves under natural grid refinement, and nested folds selected slow horizons 0.45, 0.45 and 0.30. The TAU grid in the repository artifact still stops at 3.0, so the claimed 4x extension check is not reproducible from it. The boundary-location objection stands after all: the reported optimum (0.030,0.470) is CLIPPED by the interior mask, and the raw surface actually minimizes near (0.000,0.495) at distance 0.1001. Support is genuine (six measured points nearby) but location is not, and the gain used the raw minimum while the distance gate used the clipped one. The gain result is exposed-panel development evidence only: coefficients are fitted on all 346 outcomes and compared against an observed gain from those same outcomes, and the damage horizon was introduced after seeing that observed value bracket two prior fits. Using the interior optimum gives 0.007999 and still passes, but it carries no independent validation status. Accepted as correct: the model is a static convex reweighting of the two phase mixtures, effectively a reparameterization of the original coordinates, with no state transition or forgetting law. It escapes the one-index impossibility but is not uniquely minimal (aggregate exposure plus one contrast statistic also suffices) and the charter requires an actual temporal interaction. It is a representability baseline, not a promotable mechanism.
reopen_condition: Closest the project has come, with every structural objection now checked. Two gates pass: core interior OOF RMSE 0.006746 beats repaired RPL 0.007575, and gain error is 0.001501 against a 0.004439 limit. Two fail narrowly: optimum distance 0.0762 vs 0.05, and Regret@1 0.005936 vs 0.004842, over by 0.001094. The boundary objection is defused (six measured points within 0.05, selected region 0.001481 BPB from optimal) and the non-identification objection is defused (tau interior under a 4x wider grid; fast at a physical not arbitrary bound). What remains is a genuine 0.001094 BPB shortfall in selection regret, not an artifact. Next: recover the SUR-093 interior optimum under this calibration, then run the full multi-target harness and the 300M gates before any promotion claim.

title: Acquisition-forgetting state with one shared memory rate
material_novelty: First candidate in this project with an actual state transition rather than a reweighting of cumulative dose. Per bucket the state obeys ds/du = rho_i R_k,i (1 - s) - lambda s over run-fraction u, with delivery rate R_k,i = CTOT_i w_k,i constant inside each phase, solved in closed form phase by phase. SUR-094 was accepted at review as a static convex reweighting, hence an invertible reparameterization of (w0,w1) with no forgetting law; this is not, because s_f is a nonlinear composition of two phase solves and does not factor through any linear index. The SAME lambda discounts repetition damage: X = integral of the over-exposure delivery rate against exp(-lambda (1-u)), closed form via the epoch-crossing time, damage = X^tau. So one memory parameter governs both what was learned and what was overfitted, which removes the benefit/damage index mismatch of SUR-093 structurally instead of by fitting a second horizon. Decisive property: at lambda = 0 the state collapses to s_f = 1 - exp(-rho (g0 + g1)) and X to max(0, e - 1) EXACTLY, so the refuted single-index family is a nested null at an interior grid point, and lambda is precisely the parameter carrying any two-phase advantage.
evidence: PRE-FIT AUDITS ALL PASS and are the strongest part. Closed form matches numerical integration of the ODE to 1.2e-10 and discounted over-exposure matches quadrature to 2.7e-06. lambda = 0 is the refuted single-index null EXACTLY, checked as an identity not a grid: the design row of any two-phase policy equals the tied policy's row at its phase-averaged index to 3.4e-13, so the impossibility argument applies whatever the head is. Drift from the null is linear in lambda over four decades. Shape recovery from simulated data at panel size is EXACT at 0.000, 0.002 and 0.006 BPB noise. HEADLINE WITHDRAWN AND REVERSED WITHIN THE ROUND. This entry first recorded the family as refuted on representability, on a best in-sample interior RMSE of 0.011274 over a 23,040-shape grid against 0.006243 for the two-exposure form, and generalised that into a claim that any genuine dynamical state must lose to a free reparameterization of the phase coordinates. That claim was a GRID ARTIFACT and is false. Under continuous optimisation the same family reaches 0.005362 in-sample against the two-exposure form's 0.004503, a 19 percent gap rather than the 1.8x reported. The grid simply did not cover where the family wanted to sit: the continuous optimum takes rho 0.01, the fast rate 49.8, gamma_broad 0.01 and offset 2.3e-04, every one of them outside the grid's range. The 'mechanism costs fit' generalisation is withdrawn entirely. PROPERLY EVALUATED, nested 3x3 random seed 0 with CONTINUOUS selection inside inner folds: interior OOF RMSE 0.007289, which BEATS repaired RPL 0.007575 and is within 0.000129 of the two-exposure form's 0.007160. Regret@5 is 0.000000, meaning the top five contains the observed optimum outright. The two forgetting rates come out stably separated in every outer fold, (3.17, 46.61), (3.50, 43.50) and (3.21, 55.10), which is a genuine two-timescale identification and the signature the family was registered to predict. STILL FAILS three gates. Regret@1 0.005936 against 0.004842. Raw optimum (0.000, 0.545) is ON the simplex boundary in early code share, distance 0.1097, so the pre-declared free-lunch failure mode did occur and the shared-rate damage discount did NOT prevent it. Predicted gain +0.017665 against observed +0.009594 overshoots by 0.008071, outside the 0.004439 limit. Identification is partial: lambda is well determined but rho 0.0050 and both readout exponents 0.016 and 0.0413 sit at or near their lower bounds, a degenerate ridge where a slow acquisition rate and a flat readout compensate.
reopen_condition: Now the most promising mechanistic route in the project rather than a closed one, and the reason it was nearly closed is worth carrying: a grid search reported a representability ceiling that a continuous search beat by 2x. Do not report a ceiling from a grid again. Next: constrain the rho and exponent ridge, since only lambda is identified; then attack the boundary optimum at early code share zero, which is the pre-declared failure mode and is still present; then the gain overshoot. Nested RMSE and Regret@5 are already at or past incumbent.

title: Two-exposure consolidation form under nested selection with repaired grids
material_novelty: Not a new response surface. This is the SUR-094 form evaluated under the protocol the frozen ladder always required and with every grid bound the review flagged actually extended, which turns out to change the answer rather than merely confirm it. Selection is nested: nonlinear parameters are chosen on inner splits of each outer fold's training rows and never see that fold's outcomes. slow now runs to 0.65 where it stopped at 0.45, tau to 6.0 where it stopped at 3.0, and gamma_broad's lower bound is set by identifiability rather than convenience. The interpretation is narrowed to what the panel can support: the slow horizon is a per-token consolidation ratio, 0.40 meaning a decay-phase token counts 2.62x a stable-phase one, and that reading is labelled interpretation because any horizon in [0.113, 1] is reachable from some forgetting rate under this schedule, so it adds no constraint on this panel.
evidence: Random 3-fold seed 0, 346 rows, 284 interior, primary Programming Languages BPB, shape selected in INNER folds only; independent review confirmed there is no programmatic outer-fold leakage, and that run ids, outcomes, the 284-row interior mask, the seed-0 outer partitions and both metric definitions are identical to the RPL reference, which recomputes to 0.007574658. RESULT ON THE PRE-REGISTERED GRID: nested interior OOF RMSE 0.007160, Regret@1 0.005936, Regret@5 0.000434, raw optimum equal to the interior optimum at (0.0925, 0.4300) at distance 0.0704 against a 0.05 gate. NOT A WIN, corrected after review. 0.007160 against 0.007575 is numerically lower but a paired row bootstrap on the RMSE difference gives a 95 percent interval of about [-0.00195, +0.00114], crossing zero, and foldwise this form wins one fold, ties one and loses one. The earlier 'first nested win in the project' framing is withdrawn: the honest statement is level with the incumbent, not ahead of it. Inner-split sensitivity is material -- RPL uses inner seeds 31000 + outer_fold where this reuses seed 0, and adopting RPL's inner seeds moves the result to RMSE 0.006923 and Regret@1 0.002842. IDENTIFICATION CLAIM WITHDRAWN. It was checked only on the full-panel shape and only for the slow horizon. Across outer folds the selections are slow [0.45, 0.40, 0.40], not identical, and gamma_broad [0.02, 0.10, 0.02], at its lower bound in two of three folds. The reporter printed neither. The gamma_broad = 0.02 exclusion was post-outcome tuning and is reverted; review supplied the decisive argument, that (x^-gamma - 1)/gamma tends to -log x and is a well-conditioned parameterization of the limit, so an amplitude growing like 1/gamma is not evidence of unidentified predictions. The 0.006960 / 0.002842 pair is a sensitivity, not a gate result. BLOCKED-PROTOCOL CLAIM CORRECTED: the registry previously said the incumbent had not been measured under the mixture-blocked protocol. That is FALSE. Repaired RPL's blocked RMSE is checked in at 0.026530 in reference_outputs/repaired_rpl_wsd80_controls_20260731/control_summary.csv, against 0.026371 here, so blocked extrapolation is bad in absolute terms for BOTH and the two are essentially tied. It is not a defect specific to this form. SURVIVING POSITIVE RESULT: the negative controls reproduce independently. Predicted phase gain 0.00012476 on C4 English, 0.00011804 on Falcon RefinedWeb and exactly 0 on Wikipedia English, arxiv physics and BBC news, where the incumbent invents about 0.029, while code positives keep gain at +0.003227 on github_python and +0.004576 on github_cpp. Control gains are computed by the same full-panel selection, head fit and raw-surface minimum as the primary gain. Caveat from review: each target gets an independently selected shape, so this shows form capacity and family separation, not one shared state transferring across metric families.
reopen_condition: Level with the incumbent on fit, better on negative controls, still failing the optimum-distance gate at 0.0704 and Regret@1 at 0.005936. Before promotion: fix the reporter to print every parameter per outer fold and check bounds foldwise; adopt matched inner seeds; and answer the charter's mechanism requirement, which review sharpened decisively -- with one fixed two-phase duration ANY terminal state is observationally a function of (w0, w1) alone, so no analysis of this panel can distinguish genuine dynamics from a static reparameterization. That needs a second schedule or intermediate-trajectory measurements, not another functional form.

title: Tied-calibrated acquisition-forgetting state
material_novelty: Proposed by independent review as the construction that escapes the dichotomy SUR-095 was closed on, that saturating states destroy the power-law aggregate while linear states are exactly single-index. Solve the same acquisition-forgetting ODE for an arbitrary schedule to get the terminal state s_f, then invert the TIED-policy terminal map F(E) = (rho E / (rho E + lambda)) (1 - exp(-(rho E + lambda))) and read the power law off E_eff = F^-1(s_f). By construction E_eff equals total epochs exactly on the tied diagonal for EVERY lambda, so the aggregate response stays an exact power law in dose no matter how strong the forgetting, while off the diagonal E_eff remains a nonlinear order-sensitive state. The saturation is removed from the aggregate without removing the dynamics.
evidence: The calibration identity is exact: max |E_eff - E| over the tied diagonal is 1.1e-13 at lambda 0.5, 1.8e-14 at 4.0 and 1.1e-14 at 40.0, so the construction does what it claims for any forgetting rate. It does not pay off on this panel. Continuous in-sample interior RMSE, all optimised the same way: 0.011363 with one rate component and 6 free parameters, 0.007567 with two rate components and 7 free. Matched references are 0.005362 for the plain two-rate state at 7 free and 0.004503 for the two-exposure reparameterization at 6 free. So pinning the aggregate to an exact power law costs 0.002205 against the unconstrained state, and the ordering across the four forms is monotone in how much each constrains the surface. Fast rate 59.97 sits at its bound and rho 0.0050 at its lower bound, so the ridge SUR-095 found is present here too.
reopen_condition: Superseded as a route by the identification argument rather than by the numbers: with one fixed two-phase duration any terminal state is observationally a function of (w0, w1) alone, so no form tested on THIS panel can be distinguished from a static reparameterization. Reopen only alongside a second schedule or intermediate-trajectory measurements.

title: Per-domain value schedule with a signed late-conflict channel
material_novelty: Registered from experimenter hypotheses rather than from the fitting history, and it changes two structural choices that every prior candidate shared. First, the value of a domain's tokens varies over training PER DOMAIN, so each domain gets its own schedule weight phi_i rather than the pair of shared horizons SUR-094 and SUR-096 use. On a two-domain simplex that still spans both phase coordinates, so it escapes the single-index impossibility, but with one parameter per domain instead of two shared ones and two benefit columns instead of four. It also makes a sharp pre-registered prediction that no previous form could state: phi_broad should come out near the realized phase-1 token share of 0.203, meaning natural language is worth the same throughout, while phi_code should come out well above it, meaning code is worth more late. Second, and this is the part every previous form structurally forbade, gradient conflict is allowed to have a SIGN. Under non-negative amplitudes on (E + offset)^-gamma, more broad text always lowers predicted code BPB. If broad-text gradients are anti-aligned with the code eval gradient late in training then heavy late broad text must RAISE code BPB, so a signed late-conflict channel in the decay-phase off-domain share is added. It is nested exactly at coefficient zero. The two mechanisms in the hypotheses are kept separable by construction: conflict scheduling lives in the phi_i and the conflict channel, epoching harm lives in the damage term, and the predicted two-phase gain can therefore be decomposed into the two by ablating one at a time rather than argued about.
evidence: Continuous optimisation throughout, nested 3x3 random seed 0 with selection inside inner folds. Harness check: the shared-horizon variant reproduces the published SUR-096 continuous baseline at 0.004503 exactly. SIGNED CONFLICT CHANNEL SUPPORTED. Coefficient fits STRICTLY POSITIVE with the predicted sign, meaning heavy decay-phase broad text raises code BPB, and it is stable across outer folds at +0.10582, +0.09229 and +0.10281 with a full-panel value of +0.12460. Nested interior OOF RMSE improves from 0.005252 to 0.004948 with it. The paired row bootstrap on that difference is -0.000304 with a 95 percent interval of [-0.000770, +0.000278], crossing zero, so the RMSE improvement alone is not decisive; the fold-to-fold stability of the coefficient is the stronger evidence. PER-DOMAIN READING REFUTED, and this was pre-declared. Giving each domain its own schedule weights buys almost nothing at matched capacity, 0.004454 against 0.004503 for two extra free parameters. The pre-declared signature fails outright: phi_broad was predicted near the uniform-in-time value 0.203 and comes out at 0.63 to 0.99 in every variant, so the parameters are not reading a per-domain value schedule. GAIN DECOMPOSITION, the round's main measurement. Full predicted gain +0.014036 against observed +0.009594. Setting the conflict coefficient to zero collapses it to +0.000506, so conflict scheduling carries 96.4 percent and is what makes any gain exist at all. Setting the damage amplitude to zero leaves +0.008393, so epoching carries 40.2 percent. The two sum past 100 percent because they interact, and the interaction is the interesting part: without damage the optimum runs to (0.410, 0.855), so repetition harm is not what creates the two-phase advantage but is what bounds how far the schedule should be pushed. Conflict creates the opportunity, epoching limits its exploitation. CAVEAT: an earlier decomposition reported the epoching share as 0.0 percent. That was an artifact of pinning the damage term to uniform-weighted total epochs; freeing the damage horizon, as SUR-096 does, moves it to 40.2 percent. The pinned version is withdrawn.
reopen_condition: The conflict channel should be carried forward into every subsequent candidate. Its sign is a prediction the batch-size sweep can test independently, since gradient conflict should scale with gradient noise while epoching harm should not. The per-domain schedule parameterization should not be retried on this panel.

title: Spacing-aware repetition damage
material_novelty: From the experimenter note that forgetting is characterised by the number of steps between repeat views of an example. Damage accrues at a rate superlinear in the INSTANTANEOUS re-exposure rate rather than in cumulative exposure, so the same total epochs hurt more when packed into a short window. Convex in the rate at any exponent above one, therefore minimised at even spreading, which is the only force any candidate has had that could keep early share off zero.
evidence: Refuted on both counts. Nested interior OOF RMSE 0.007962 without the conflict channel and 0.007959 with it, against 0.006117 and 0.004984 for horizon-weighted damage on identical folds. And it does not do the one thing it was built for: the optimum stays at early share exactly 0.000, distance 0.1129. The reason is visible in the fit. The threshold above which repetition starts to hurt fits at 11.91 epochs per unit run time, so at low early share the phase-0 rate is below it and contributes no damage at all; the convexity that would push toward even spreading never engages. A spacing mechanism with a threshold this high cannot produce a boundary force whatever its exponent.
reopen_condition: Reopen only with the threshold pinned from measured epoch counts rather than fitted, or with spacing entering the benefit term rather than the damage term.

title: Multiplicative early-groundwork complementarity
material_novelty: The first non-additive candidate in the project. Every prior form sums independent exposure channels, so no prior form can represent a penalty that appears only when a domain is entirely absent from the stable phase. Here late exposure is gated by early exposure through late * exp(-kappa * early), which is maximal at exactly zero early share and decays as groundwork accumulates: late data can only be exploited to the extent something was built to exploit it. Motivated by a measured cliff rather than by a hypothesis.
evidence: MEASURED FACT THAT MOTIVATED IT, which falsifies every additive candidate in the project: the panel does sample early share exactly 0.0000, and those rows are distinctly worse than early share 0.0250 at matched late share. At late share 0.45, 0.945904 against 0.938689; at 0.50, 0.941774 against 0.936949; at 0.55, 0.940216 against 0.938095. A penalty of 0.0021 to 0.0072 BPB concentrated at exactly zero. Every model in the registry predicts its optimum AT that point. RESULT: the first candidate to leave the boundary. The optimum moves from (0.000, 0.547) to (0.033, 0.520) and the optimum distance improves from 0.1107 to 0.0704. It costs fit: nested interior OOF RMSE 0.005901 against 0.004941 for the additive form on identical folds. Fitted gate kappa 1.817. Still fails the distance gate at 0.0704 against 0.05, and Regret@1 is unchanged at 0.005936.
reopen_condition: Most promising open route. The gating form was the first one tried and was not searched; the cliff is sharper than exp(-kappa * early) can represent, so a form with a steeper approach to zero should be tested. Combining it with the conflict channel and horizon damage without the fit regression is the specific target.

title: Composite dynamics surrogate: conflict channel, gated absorption, policy-responsive horizon
material_novelty: Assembles the three mechanisms the experimenter hypotheses name, each as its own channel so the head weighs them independently and each nests out at coefficient zero. A SIGNED conflict channel in the decay-phase off-domain share, which every prior form structurally forbade because non-negative amplitudes make broad text always helpful. A GATED absorption channel where late code exposure counts only through a Hill gate on early exposure, early^beta / (early^beta + kappa^beta), which is multiplicative and therefore representable by no additive model; it exists because the panel measures a cliff at exactly zero early share that every additive candidate walks straight into. And a POLICY-RESPONSIVE horizon where the effective recency weight shifts with the domain's own late-minus-early contrast. Two shared benefit horizons and a separate damage horizon are carried over unchanged.
evidence: Nested 3x3, continuous selection inside inner folds, 346 rows, 284 interior, primary Programming Languages BPB. A headline of 4 of 4 gates was reached and is WITHDRAWN as a grid artifact, caught before publication by the robustness run rather than by review. With beta capped at 12 the fit gave interior OOF RMSE 0.004843, Regret@1 0.002842, optimum distance exactly 0.0500 against a 0.05 limit, and gain error 0.000673. Widening the beta bound to 40 flips THE SAME configuration at the same seed to 3 of 4: beta runs to 35.06, still at a bound, and the optimum jumps from (0.050,0.500) to (0.101,0.394) with distance 0.1063. The distance gate had passed only by tying the limit exactly. ROBUSTNESS OVER SIX CONFIGURATIONS, three fold seeds by adaptive horizon on and off, at surface grid 801 and beta to 40. Interior OOF RMSE passes in 6 of 6, ranging 0.004684 to 0.005350, so it beats repaired RPL's 0.007575 by 30 to 38 percent under every setting. Gain error passes 6 of 6, 0.000126 to 0.003846. Regret@1 passes 5 of 6, reaching 0.002842 in three configurations, which EQUALS repaired RPL's regret and selects the same policy (0.050,0.500); Regret@5 reaches 0.000000, the observed optimum inside the top five. Optimum distance passes 1 of 6. The failure is now precisely located and is not a fit failure. The surface RANKS policies well and stably, but its continuous argmin wanders: early share swings 0.033 to 0.109 and late share 0.386 to 0.521 across seeds and beta bounds. Component caveats. The policy-responsive horizon fits at delta about -0.010 in every fold, effectively zero, so its mechanism does nothing and its benefit is as a nuisance parameter that changes the selection landscape; that is not a mechanism claim and should not be reported as one. The conflict coefficient's SIGN is not robustly identified: it fits +0.19477 with the groundwork column present and -0.10524 with the conflict exponent free and groundwork absent, so the earlier 'sign confirmed' statement in SUR-098 is over-strong and is qualified here. kappa is unstable across folds, ranging 2.76 to 17.06.
reopen_condition: Closest the project has come and the first candidate whose SELECTION quality matches the incumbent while fitting 30 percent better. Not promotable: the optimum-distance gate passes in 1 of 6 configurations and beta sits on a bound in most. Before promotion: find a gate form whose sharpness parameter is identified rather than running to whatever bound is offered, since the Hill exponent is standing in for a cliff sharper than the family can express; drop the policy-responsive horizon or replace it with a mechanism that actually moves; and settle the conflict sign, which the batch-size sweep can do independently of the mixture panel.

title: Gated absorption with per-domain groundwork
material_novelty: Adds the one structure that finally moves the optimum: BOTH domains get a multiplicative groundwork gate, not just code. Late exposure counts only through a Hill gate on the same domain's early exposure, so late tokens are worth something only to the extent something was built to absorb them, and the general ability that code capability rides on must be built before the decay phase too. Adding the broad-domain gate is what took the optimum-distance gate from 1 of 6 seeds to 5 of 6. Carried alongside: a pure-early code channel with its own offset, a signed conflict channel, and repetition damage at its own horizon. Nonlinear selection is continuous inside inner folds, five inner per three outer, because selection variance rather than fit was what moved the optimum across seeds.
evidence: Six fold seeds, nested 3 outer by 5 inner, 346 rows, 284 interior, surface grid 801, primary Programming Languages BPB. 20 of 24 gate-passes. Interior OOF RMSE passes 6 of 6 at 0.004696 to 0.005865, beating repaired RPL's 0.007575 by 23 to 38 percent under every seed. Gain error passes 6 of 6 at 0.002396 to 0.003726 against a 0.004439 limit. Optimum distance passes 5 of 6 at 0.038770 to 0.083104, the first time this project has cleared that gate other than by tying it, and the optimum is now stable: early share 0.051 to 0.064 in five of six seeds against an observed 0.100, late share 0.485 to 0.530 against an observed 0.500. Regret@5 reaches 0.000000 in four of six seeds. NOT PROMOTABLE. Regret@1 passes only 3 of 6 and FAILS under the registered seed-0 protocol at 0.005936 against 0.004842, short by 0.001094; the failing seeds all rank (0.050, 0.450) first where the incumbent ranks (0.050, 0.500). There is also a protocol trade rather than a clean win: at three inner folds Regret@1 passes 4 of 6 and distance 4 of 6, at five inner folds distance rises to 5 of 6 and Regret@1 falls to 3 of 6, so the two gates are being traded against each other and no setting passes both robustly. COMPONENT FINDINGS. Phase-split repetition damage puts the stable-phase amplitude at EXACTLY 0.00e+00 in all six runs, which is a direct confirmation of the experimenter claim that early repeats cost little because the data is not yet differentiated; it is recorded but not adopted, because it also costs about 0.002 BPB of fit. The conflict channel's sign is stable across folds at a fixed column set but NOT across column sets, so it is carried for the fit it buys and is not evidence for the conflict hypothesis. CONTROLS RUN, seed 0, all 29 panel metrics, in reference_outputs/gated_absorption_wsd80_20260807/. TOTAL SEPARATION with no overlap: all 26 broad-text metrics predict |phase gain| below 0.001 and all 3 code metrics predict between +0.009 and +0.013. C4 English +0.000032 and Falcon RefinedWeb +0.000008, where repaired RPL invents about 0.029, a roughly 900-fold reduction on the project's sharpest control; Wikipedia English +0.000002, m2d2 wikipedia +0.000001, arxiv computer science -0.000002, arxiv physics -0.000026, BBC news -0.000060. Code positives: Programming Languages +0.012632, github_cpp +0.012700, github_python +0.008993, the last within 0.0006 of the observed two-phase gain of +0.009594 on a metric the model was not tuned against. Interior OOF RMSE across all 29 metrics is 0.003351 to 0.014890, median near 0.005. Caveat: each target gets an independently selected shape, so this shows the form separates the families, not that one shared state transfers across them. THE TWO FAILING GATES ARE IN TENSION AND THIS IS STRUCTURAL. Three settings, and the total never exceeds 20 of 24: three inner folds without ridge gives Regret@1 4/6 and distance 4/6; five inner folds without ridge gives 3/6 and 5/6; five inner folds with a fold-selected ridge on scaled amplitudes gives 5/6 and 2/6. The ridge case is diagnostic. It does reduce out-of-fold prediction variance as intended, lifting Regret@1 from 3/6 to 5/6, and it simultaneously drags the optimum back toward low early share, 0.036 to 0.064, dropping distance from 5/6 to 2/6. So the groundwork gate channels are BOTH the only thing that moves the optimum off the boundary AND the first thing regularization removes: they are the least fit-supported part of the model while being the only part that fixes the optimum's location. Improving the ranking costs the optimum and vice versa. Resolving this by picking the best-looking setting would be post-outcome selection and was not done. SELECTION OBJECTIVE CORRECTED, and it improves nearly everything. The shape was being selected against cross-validated error on ALL rows while the gates are graded on the 284 interior rows, the same mismatch review flagged on an earlier candidate. Selection now scores interior rows only; fitting still uses every row, including the 22 at early share exactly zero and the 30 at or below 0.025 that the interior mask excludes, because those carry the cliff evidence the gate channels rest on. Result 21 of 24, up from 20. Interior OOF RMSE 6/6 and both better and far tighter, 0.004259 to 0.004474 against repaired RPL's 0.007575, a 41 to 44 percent reduction under EVERY seed. Gain error 6/6. Regret@1 rises to 5 of 6 and reaches the incumbent's own 0.002842 in five seeds. Optimum distance 4 of 6. Under the registered seed-0 protocol the model now passes RMSE 0.004362, Regret@1 0.002842 and gain error 0.003290, and fails ONLY optimum distance at 0.065 against 0.05. The remaining failure has a sharper shape than before: the selected optima are BIMODAL. Four seeds land near (0.062, 0.479) at distance 0.041 to 0.044 and two land near (0.035, 0.500) at distance 0.065. The inner-fold objective has two local minima trading early share against late share along the observed valley, and which is found depends on the fold draw. That is more tractable than a wandering optimum: the model is choosing between two specific competing explanations of the same data.
reopen_condition: Best result the project has produced. Documented in reference_outputs/gated_absorption_wsd80_20260807/report.md with a rerunnable artifact and source hashes. Blocking for promotion: Regret@1 under the registered seed, and the structural tension above, which means no protocol setting passes both remaining gates robustly. The gate channels need independent support that the fit criterion does not supply -- the natural source is the simulated-epoching sweep, since this decomposition predicts disabling epoching removes about 40 percent of the gain rather than all of it, and the batch-size sweep for the conflict sign. Still not run on this form: the 300M and Table-9 panel, the multi-target joint fit, and the blocked-protocol comparison.

title: Gated absorption carried to blocked folds and the 300M 39-bucket panel
material_novelty: Runs the three things every candidate in this project has deferred: the mixture-blocked protocol, the 300M 39-bucket panel on both its targets, and the cross-panel consistency test. The 300M panel is the mirror image of WSD80 -- none of its 238 asymmetric policies beats the best tied policy, and it supplies an exact aggregate-matched tied counterpart for each -- so a form that predicts a large gain on WSD80 and a near-zero one here is doing something other than fitting whatever it is shown. The port is family-pooled over 39 buckets in 3 families with per-bucket departures under a fold-selected ridge, on the established correspondence-grouped folds. The signed conflict channel is NOT ported, having no faithful analogue without a single eval domain, and that is the one structural difference.
evidence: BLOCKED PROTOCOL, overturning an earlier reading. Interior OOF RMSE 0.012067, 0.018740, 0.009696 and 0.015421 across four seeds against repaired RPL's checked-in 0.026530, so 29 to 63 percent BETTER under every seed. SUR-096 gave 0.026371 here, essentially tied, and blocked extrapolation was recorded as a weakness of the approach; it was a weakness of that form only. 300M UNCHEATABLE, against HPR all-row RMSE 0.006800 and Regret@1 0.002678 on the column HPR is published on. title: Saturating repetition damage
material_novelty: Every damage term in this project has been max(0, E - 1)^tau, which grows without bound in exposure. That is physically wrong: a bucket can only be overfitted so far, and once its unique content is memorised further passes cannot keep costing more. Unbounded damage therefore over-penalises exactly the heavy-late-code region, and both other structures in SUR-103 already push late share down -- the absorption gate discounts late tokens, and late-weighted damage penalises them. Here damage saturates: D = 1 - exp(-(max(0, E - 1)^tau) / s), which reproduces the old form for small excess and levels off for large. The old unbounded form is the s -> infinity limit, so it is nested.
evidence: PRE-STATED PREDICTION CONFIRMED. Late code share moved from SUR-103's 0.449 to 0.451 up to 0.458 to 0.466, and optimum distance from 0.0489-0.0528 down to 0.0338-0.0430, exactly the direction registered before fitting. In three of four seeds the scale settles at 5965.5, 7328.3 and 8928.9, far from both bounds across four extra orders of magnitude, so the saturation scale IS identified there and the physical argument is supported: damage genuinely levels off, and with the excess term reaching about 16,500 on the heaviest rows a scale near 7000 means the saturation is active in the tail rather than linearised away. In the fourth seed it runs to 1,238,072, about 150 times larger, which is effectively the unbounded limit the argument was meant to replace. A fifth seed CRASHED with scipy nnls hitting its iteration cap, an unresolved numerical robustness defect. And the gates move under the wider bound, which is the decisive point. Seed 0 goes from 4 of 4 to 3 of 4 as interior OOF RMSE rises 0.007816 to 0.008260 and crosses the 0.007954 limit; seed 3 fails distance at 0.050760. So the 12 of 12 does not survive the bound widening, the same failure mode that withdrew a headline earlier in this same session. Of four completed seeds under the honest bound: 4/4, 4/4, 3/4, 3/4. The repetition column is an excess raised to a fitted exponent and spans fourteen orders of magnitude over this panel with the exponent free to 10; the WSD80 head was solving it UNSCALED while the 300M port written later already normalised. Scaling the columns before the sign-constrained solve and unscaling after -- exact, since non-negativity is invariant to positive rescaling -- plus a raised iteration cap. The crash is GONE: the seed that could not run now runs. The runaway is NOT numerical and is real: seed 3's scale comes back as 1,238,072.8 against 1,238,072.5 before the fix, essentially identical, which proves it is a property of the objective on those folds rather than solver noise. Six seeds now give 21 of 24. Four settle at 5963, 7320, 8492 and 8730; two run away to 1,238,073 and 4,484,194. THE CORRESPONDENCE IS EXACT AND IS THE USEFUL RESULT. Every seed where the saturation scale is identified passes the distance gate (0.031250, 0.031350, 0.042957 and, at seed 0, 0.038770), and every seed where it runs away fails it (0.050760, 0.052752). The deciding test compared the two basins on the INNER-FOLD objective with no gate consulted: in both runaway seeds the identified basin scores LOWER, 17.678285 against 17.686885 at seed 3 and 16.457234 against 16.464298 at seed 4. So differential evolution had simply missed the better optimum and multi-start is a pure optimiser improvement, not a modelling change. Implemented by refining from starts spanning the saturation parameter's WHOLE bounded range and keeping the best by inner-fold CV, deliberately not seeded at any value known to work. RESULT 23 OF 24. The saturation scale is now identified in ALL six seeds at 5963, 7333, 8491, 8737, 16180 and 16459, every one far from both bounds across nine orders of magnitude, so the physical argument that repetition harm saturates is supported outright. Optimum distance passes 6 of 6 at 0.031250 to 0.048814, the gate that has blocked this project from the beginning. Regret@1 passes 6 of 6 at 0.000434 to 0.004042. Gain error passes 6 of 6 at 0.000028 to 0.000733, so the predicted two-phase gain is within 0.0008 of the measured 0.009594 in every seed.
