title: Damage and starvation are confounded ON THE TIED DIAGONAL only
material_novelty: A structural check nobody in this project had run, prompted by trying to verify SUR-104's saturation argument against raw data. With two domains on a simplex and constant epoch multipliers the two domains' exposures satisfy broad = C_b - (C_b/C_c) * code exactly, so they are affinely related on EVERY row, not merely on the tied diagonal.
evidence: CLAIM NARROWED after checking it against the columns the model actually uses. What stands: on the TIED DIAGONAL, code and broad exposure are perfectly anti-correlated, corr -1.0000, because with two domains on a simplex and constant epoch multipliers broad = C_b - (C_b/C_c) * code identically. So the marginal-harm diagnostic run on that diagonal IS confounded, and the measured acceleration there -- -0.032794, -0.000660, +0.018307, +0.081680 per epoch over [1,5), [5,10), [10,16), [16,27), with BPB running 1.267761, 1.427923, 1.820322 at 21.2, 23.8, 26.5 epochs -- cannot be attributed to code repetition rather than broad-text starvation. WHAT WAS WRONG: the generalisation that damage is 'the same column up to an affine transform' everywhere. That used uniformly weighted epochs for both domains, which is NOT what the model reads. Damage is taken at its own horizon phi_d with a kink at one epoch and a fitted power, so it is a different and nonlinear functional of (w0, w1) from any benefit column. Regressing the damage column on ALL FOUR benefit columns gives R^2 = 0.589496 with residual standard deviation 64.07 percent of the damage column's own. Pairwise it correlates +0.9299 with broad benefit at the near horizon and +0.7847 at the late horizon, high but far from one. So roughly forty percent of the damage column's variation is unavailable to any benefit column and damage IS partially identified off the diagonal.
reopen_condition: The narrow claim is settled and not reopenable: tied-diagonal exposure comparisons on a two-domain simplex are confounded by construction, so no marginal-harm argument from that slice can establish a repetition mechanism. The broad claim is withdrawn. Damage remains partially identified off the diagonal, which is where the phase structure lives, so damage-versus-starvation on the FULL surface is an open question rather than a closed one.

title: Repeated tokens are worth less than fresh ones
material_novelty: Every benefit term in this project reads TOTAL exposure, so the twentieth pass over a pool counts the same as the second. The experimenters' account is that the two-phase advantage is about using the right data at the right time WITHOUT incurring an overfitting penalty, and specifically that you cannot just repeat on-target data the whole way through. That requires repeats to be worth less than fresh tokens, which no benefit term here expresses. Split exposure into the part that is new content and the part that is repetition and value them differently: effective(phi) = min(1, E(phi)) + eta * max(0, E(phi) - 1), with eta the worth of a repeated token against a fresh one. eta = 1 recovers every previous benefit term EXACTLY, so the whole prior family is a nested null at an interior point of the parameter's range. Note this only bites on code: the broad pool is large enough that its exposure never exceeds one epoch, so max(0, E_broad - 1) is identically zero and eta acts on the small-pool domain alone, which is exactly where the account says it should.
evidence: PRE-REGISTERED REFUTATION, on the failure mode written before fitting: 'eta at or near 1 refutes the account on this panel'. eta fits at EXACTLY 1.0000 on all three seeds checked, its upper bound and the nested null. The panel says a repeated token contributes as much to benefit as a fresh one, and prefers every previous benefit term to any discount on repeats. THIS DOES NOT REFUTE THE OVERFITTING ACCOUNT; it separates two claims that were being run together. 'Repeated tokens teach less', which is what eta measures, is REFUTED at eta = 1. 'Repetition causes harm', which is what the damage channel measures, is SUPPORTED and unchanged: the damage amplitude stays strictly positive at 7.6498e-04, 5.2629e-04 and 4.4840e-04 across the three seeds. So the mechanism is not that repeats fail to teach; it is that repeats teach at full value AND additionally incur a cost, whose net can still turn negative at high repetition. The registered prediction that the damage amplitude would FALL if the two were substitutes is therefore also refuted: they are not substitutes, they are different channels. Benefit amplitudes are stable and strongly code-dominated, code at the near horizon 0.34440 to 0.44931 against broad 0.00646 to 0.00825, and code at the late horizon 0.19402 to 0.25503 against broad 0.00128 to 0.00158. Gates on seeds 0-5 give 23 of 24, but those are the seeds the damage form was selected on, so the number carries no weight either way. RE-CHECKED UNDER UNBOUNDED DAMAGE AND CONFIRMED. The original eta was measured with the saturating damage form that SUR-111 later voided for this panel, so the audit flagged it as suspect. Refitting with unbounded damage, which SUR-111 established is correct for WSD80, gives eta = 1.0000 again on all three seeds. The finding is robust to the damage form. Damage amplitudes stay strictly positive and in fact rise slightly, 8.3398e-04, 7.6741e-04 and 8.8104e-04 against 7.6498e-04, 5.2629e-04 and 4.4840e-04 before, so the separate repetition cost is if anything better supported under the corrected law. Benefit amplitudes are stable and code-dominated as before: code at the near horizon 0.41299 to 0.47235 against broad 0.00623 to 0.00765. Internal consistency check passed: the now-unused saturation parameter wanders meaninglessly across seeds at 631, 5166 and 652900, which is what an inert parameter should do and confirms the unbounded form is actually in force.
reopen_condition: Settled and robust. Repeats are not devalued for benefit purposes on this panel, and repetition carries a separate cost. Both halves now verified under the correct damage law. The remaining open question about the experimenters' account is the timing half, which WSD80 cannot answer for code because late exposure there is almost never first exposure.

title: Three-way token accounting: early-unique, late-fresh, repeated
material_novelty: States the experimenters' account exactly rather than approximating it. Every token a policy delivers to a domain falls into one of three kinds, and the three EXHAUST total exposure with no double counting: early_unique = min(1, e0), content first seen in the stable phase; late_fresh = min(1, e0 + e1) - min(1, e0), content first seen in the DECAY phase; repeated = (e0 + e1) - min(1, e0 + e1), everything past one pass of the pool. They sum to e0 + e1 identically, so this is a partition of the same exposure every prior model read as one number, and giving them one amplitude each recovers those models exactly. 'The right data at the right time' is then a statement about late_fresh being worth more than early_unique, and 'without incurring an overfitting penalty' a statement about repeated being worth least -- both directly readable off the fitted amplitudes instead of inferred from a horizon. It also adjudicates a contradiction the project has not noticed. The absorption gate says late tokens are worth MORE when early exposure was large; a freshness account says they are worth more when early exposure was SMALL, because only then are they new. These are opposite, and the three-way split lets the data choose without either being assumed.
evidence: INCONCLUSIVE, and the fault is in the design rather than in the account being tested. 0 of 24 gate-passes with interior OOF RMSE 0.021464 to 0.024902, roughly three times worse than the working models, so the fitted amplitudes come from a badly misspecified surface and no mechanism can be read off them. TWO ERRORS, both mine. First, the power-law readout was applied to EACH part separately, so early_unique, late_fresh and repeated each saturate on their own. That is a different functional form from the total saturating, and it is why the fit collapsed. Second, the raw amplitudes were never comparable in the first place: early_unique and late_fresh are capped at 1 by construction while repeated ranges to about 25 on this panel, so an amplitude of 2.4 on the small-valued column is not larger than 0.45 on a near-unit one. The apparent findings that repeated dominates at 1.71536 to 3.13402 and that late_fresh sits BELOW early_unique in all four seeds are therefore artefacts of scale, not evidence. Both pre-stated predictions are neither confirmed nor refuted. One observation survives because it needs no cross-column comparison: the BROAD repeated amplitude is exactly 0.00000 on every seed, correct by construction since the broad pool never exceeds one epoch.
reopen_condition: Rerun with the partition weighted INSIDE a single readout rather than split across three: effective = a*early_unique + b*late_fresh + c*repeated, then benefit = (effective + offset)^-gamma, with a, b, c non-negative and columns standardised before comparison. That keeps one power law, makes the three weights directly comparable as token values, and nests the current family at a = b = c. The accounting question is open and worth answering; only this parameterisation is closed.

title: Shape-scale separation in the damage term
material_novelty: Diagnoses and removes the degeneracy behind the only gate this project still fails. In s*log1p(x/s) the parameter s does TWO jobs: it sets the curvature and it multiplies the whole column. For large s the column tends to x scaled arbitrarily, and a free non-negative head amplitude can absorb any rescaling, so s and the amplitude are near-redundant and the objective is flat along that direction. A flat direction is precisely what produces the bimodal landscape observed in SUR-104, where the scale settles near 7000 on some fold draws and runs to 1e+08 on others, with distance passing exactly when it settles. Normalising the column separates the two roles: damage = log1p(x/s) / log1p(x_max/s), with x_max the panel maximum of the excess term. This is 0 at x = 0 and 1 at x = x_max whatever s is, so s controls SHAPE ONLY and the head amplitude controls magnitude alone. The unbounded form is still nested -- as s grows the ratio tends to x / x_max, linear and normalised -- but it is no longer reachable by an arbitrary rescaling, so the flat direction is gone.
evidence: REFUTED BEFORE THE FIT, by a direct check of its own premise, and the run was stopped rather than left to burn compute confirming a proven no-op. The proposal was that s and the head amplitude are degenerate in s*log1p(x/s), and that normalising the column would separate shape from scale. Normalising divides by a constant, correlation is invariant to positive rescaling, and the correlations come out IDENTICAL to eight decimal places at every scale tested: 0.99945391 at s=5e3, 0.99950792 at 1e4, 0.99489609 at 3e4, 0.99061988 at 1e5, 0.98817252 at 1e6 and 0.98786515 at 1e8, the same both ways. The head fits a free non-negative amplitude, so the model sees only the column's DIRECTION, and non-negative least squares with column c against k*c for k > 0 returns amplitude a/k and identical predictions. The normalisation is therefore a provable no-op and could not have changed any gate. WHAT THE CHECK DID ESTABLISH, and it matters more than the failed fix. The column's direction barely moves across FOUR orders of magnitude of s: correlation with the s=7000 column is 0.98787 even at s=1e8, so only about 1.2 percent of the column's variance distinguishes a strongly saturating damage term from an effectively unbounded one. The objective is genuinely near-flat in this parameter. That is why the earlier basin comparison found the good basin better by only 0.05 percent of the CV objective, 17.678285 against 17.686885, and why multi-start reduced the bimodality without removing it. The bimodality is real near-unidentifiability, not a parameterisation artefact.
reopen_condition: Closed. No reparameterisation can help, because the problem is not how the parameter is written but that the panel barely distinguishes its values. The saturation scale needs an EXTERNAL constraint -- the simulated epoching sweep is the natural source, since varying repetition directly is exactly the experiment that would separate a saturating damage term from an unbounded one -- or the distance gate must be accepted as passing about nine times in fourteen with the reason understood and recorded.

title: Token values inside one readout
material_novelty: Second attempt at the token-accounting question, weighting the partition inside a single power-law readout instead of splitting it across three.
evidence: INCONCLUSIVE, my error again. Interior OOF RMSE 0.020439 to 0.031522, three to five times the working model, so nothing can be read off the parameters. The cause is visible in the design: the four horizon benefit columns -- code and broad at the near horizon and at the late horizon -- were REPLACED by a single effective-exposure column per domain, so the structure carrying most of the fit was removed while only token weighting was meant to be added. The parameters confirm the misspecification rather than answering anything. b, the worth of a late-first-seen token, pins at its upper bound of 4.0000 in three seeds and falls to 0.1495 in the fourth. c, the worth of a repeat, ranges 0.2613 to 2.5672 and contradicts SUR-106's eta = 1.0000 measured on a well-fitting model. Two parameters that disagree across seeds and with a better-specified sibling are not evidence. Directionally b reaches its upper bound in three of four seeds, which is what the timing account predicts, but it comes from a surface fitting three to five times worse than the incumbent and is not offered as support. This is the SECOND consecutive design error on this question: SUR-107 applied the power law to each partition element separately, SUR-108 dropped the horizon structure. The question itself remains untested.
reopen_condition: Third attempt must be INCREMENTAL rather than a replacement: keep the working model's four horizon columns untouched and ADD the late-fresh quantity as one further channel. Then the test is whether that channel earns a non-zero amplitude and improves fit, which asks whether content first seen late carries information beyond what the horizons already encode. Compare standardised contributions, amplitude times column standard deviation, never raw amplitudes across columns with different ranges.

title: Import the repetition knee from the 300M panel
material_novelty: Supplies the external constraint SUR-109 concluded was necessary, from data already in hand rather than from a new experiment. WSD80 barely distinguishes a saturating damage term from an unbounded one -- the column's direction moves only 1.2 percent across four orders of magnitude of the scale -- which is why that parameter is bimodal and why the optimum-distance gate passes only about nine times in fourteen. The 300M panel distinguishes them far better: the same sweep moves family 0's column by 17.7 percent, roughly fifteen times more, because 38 of its 39 buckets cross the one-epoch threshold somewhere in the panel and exposure spans 0 to 256 epochs against WSD80's 0 to 26.5 on a single domain. The transfer needs a reparameterisation to be meaningful, which is the substantive part. The current scale s multiplies excess^tau, so it carries units of (excess epochs)^tau and tau is fitted per panel; importing s alone would be dimensionally meaningless. Putting the knee in EPOCHS instead, damage = excess^tau / (1 + (excess/E*)^tau), makes E* the excess-epoch level at which harm stops growing -- the same physical quantity in the same units on both panels, and therefore actually transferable.
evidence: STEP 1 SUCCEEDED. The repetition knee is well identified on 300M and stable: E* = 110.35, 103.81, 102.11 and 109.26 EXCESS EPOCHS across four seeds, about 8 percent spread, with tau also stable at 2.470 to 2.789. The epoch-knee damage form also improves the 300M fit substantially, all-row RMSE 0.005195 to 0.005219 against HPR's 0.006800, a 24 percent reduction and better than the earlier port's 0.006284 to 0.006606. STEP 2 IS UNNECESSARY AND THE REASON IS THE RESULT. E* is about 105 excess epochs; WSD80's maximum excess is 25.46. Imposing the 300M-fitted law on WSD80 leaves the damage column retaining 97.74 to 100.00 percent of its unbounded value everywhere, correlating 0.99998411 with the unbounded column, with a largest single-row reduction of 2.26 percent. WSD80's entire sampled range lies below the knee, so on that panel the physically correct damage law is INDISTINGUISHABLE from an unbounded one. THIS VOIDS SUR-104's GATE IMPROVEMENTS. Its fitted scale of about 7000 in excess-to-the-tau units corresponds, at tau = 3, to a knee at 7000^(1/3) = 19.1 excess epochs -- inside WSD80's 0 to 25.5 range and 5.5 times more aggressive than the 105 measured on independent data. So SUR-104 was fitting a knee that physically is not there, positioned exactly where it could reshape the column, which is how it moved the optimum. That also explains the bimodality, the runaway scales and the failure to replicate on fresh seeds: WSD80 cannot see the knee, so the parameter is free to wander, and any value it lands on inside the range is a fitting artefact.
reopen_condition: The saturation question is settled: repetition harm does level off, at about 105 excess epochs, and no panel in this project other than 300M can see it. WSD80 should use UNBOUNDED damage, which is the original SUR-102 and SUR-103 form. The distance gate therefore stands at 3/11 on fresh seeds with no saturating-damage rescue available, and closing it needs something other than the damage term.

title: Which domain actually needs early groundwork
material_novelty: With saturating damage voided by SUR-111, the absorption gate is the only remaining structure that touches the biased coordinate. The gate multiplies late exposure by early^beta/(early^beta + kappa^beta), which DISCOUNTS late tokens -- exactly the direction that suppresses the predicted late code share, which sits at 0.438 to 0.458 against an observed 0.500 while early share is already right. The model currently gates BOTH domains, but the two were never separated. The history says they should be: the code gate was present from the start while adding the BROAD gate is what moved distance from 1 of 6 seeds to 5 of 6. That points at a mechanistic asymmetry worth testing rather than assuming -- general language ability plausibly must be built during the stable phase before anything can ride on it, whereas code-specific content may be absorbable late without prior code exposure, because it is narrow content rather than a substrate. A three-way ablation of gate placement asks the data which domain needs groundwork.
evidence: CLEAN NULL on fresh seeds 6-11 with unbounded damage as SUR-111 established. All three gate placements are indistinguishable: both gates gives distance 1/6 with range 0.0456-0.0664, late share 0.438-0.455 and RMSE 0.006478-0.007210; broad only gives 1/6, 0.0498-0.0644, 0.439-0.451 and 0.006485-0.007222; code only gives 1/6, 0.0471-0.0660, 0.438-0.454 and 0.006466-0.007021. Each totals 19 of 24. Both pre-stated predictions are refuted. There is no domain asymmetry in which one needs early groundwork, and code-only is not worst. The late-share bias is IDENTICAL under every placement at 0.438 to 0.455, so gate placement is not its source. IT ALSO OVERTURNS AN EARLIER ATTRIBUTION I HAD BEEN REASONING FROM. I recorded that adding the BROAD gate was the single change that moved optimum distance from 1 of 6 seeds to 5 of 6, and treated the gate as the load-bearing structure of the model on that basis. That observation came from the saturating-damage era which SUR-111 has since voided; with unbounded damage on fresh seeds it does not reproduce. GAP IN MY OWN DESIGN, now being closed: the ablation varied WHICH gate and never tested whether ANY gate matters. The neither-gate cell was omitted and is running as SUR-112b.
reopen_condition: If the neither-gate cell also scores 19 of 24, the absorption gate -- described through much of this project as the structure that moved the optimum off the boundary -- is inert under the corrected damage law, and the model should be simplified by removing it. That would be a substantial simplification and should be checked on more than six seeds before it is adopted.

title: Late-fresh CODE is unmeasurable on this panel; the strong novelty claim is withdrawn
material_novelty: Fourth and finally sound attempt at the timing half of the experimenters' account, after two designs I broke myself. The working model is left completely INTACT and the late-fresh quantity -- content of a domain first encountered during the decay phase -- is added as ONE further channel that nests out at amplitude zero. Nothing is replaced, the comparison is paired on identical folds, and contributions are compared standardised as amplitude times column spread rather than as raw amplitudes across columns with incompatible ranges, which was the specific error in SUR-107.
evidence: CLAIM WITHDRAWN AND NARROWED after checking the channel's support, which I should have checked before reporting. The late-fresh amplitude is exactly 0 on all three seeds and adding the channel costs fit -- 0.007632 to 0.007660, 0.006848 to 0.007177, 0.006690 to 0.006952 -- but that is NOT evidence that novelty is inert. The code late-fresh column is non-zero on only 34 of 346 rows and, decisively, on only 5 of the 284 INTERIOR rows the gates are scored on, 1.8 percent. The cause is structural rather than a sampling gap. The code pool is small enough that c0 = 21.089, so one epoch of early exposure is reached at a phase-0 share of 0.0474; any policy with meaningful early code has already exhausted the pool, and late exposure is therefore almost never FIRST exposure. A zero amplitude on a column that is zero on 98 percent of the scored rows shows the panel CANNOT MEASURE code novelty, not that code novelty is absent. WHAT SURVIVES. The paired-fold design and standardised comparison were sound, and the finding that adding an unsupported channel costs fit is a correct negative about THAT channel on THIS panel. Nothing follows about the mechanism. WHAT WAS NOT TESTED. Only the CODE channel was added. The BROAD late-fresh column is non-zero on 284 of 284 interior rows -- full support -- because the broad pool is large enough that one epoch is not reached until a phase-0 share of 1.2546, so late broad exposure genuinely is first exposure throughout. That test is available and has not been run.
reopen_condition: Run the BROAD late-fresh channel, which has full support on the scored rows, before drawing any conclusion about novelty. Code novelty is not answerable on WSD80 at all and would need a panel whose code pool is large relative to the run, so that late code exposure can be first exposure at realistic mixtures.

title: The absorption gate is inert on WSD80 but LOAD-BEARING on 300M
material_novelty: Closes the cell omitted from SUR-112, which varied WHICH domain was gated but never asked whether ANY gate matters. The absorption gate is this model's namesake and was reported through much of this project as the structure that moved the optimum off the support boundary, on a multiplicative-complementarity reading: late tokens count only to the extent early groundwork exists to absorb them.
evidence: INERT. On fresh seeds 6-11 with unbounded damage, removing BOTH gates changes nothing: distance 1/6 with range 0.0454-0.0644 against 0.0456-0.0664 for both gates, late code share 0.439-0.455 against 0.438-0.455, and interior OOF RMSE 0.006458-0.007028 against 0.006478-0.007210, which is if anything slightly BETTER without them. Both total 19 of 24. Combined with SUR-112, all four gate configurations -- both, broad only, code only, neither -- are indistinguishable. THREE CLAIMS ARE WITHDRAWN. The multiplicative-complementarity mechanism is not supported: gating late exposure by early exposure earns nothing. The statement that the gate moved the optimum off the boundary came from the saturating-damage era that SUR-111 voided and does not reproduce. And the model's name is now wrong for what it contains. THE MODEL SIMPLIFIES with no loss: intercept, signed conflict channel, four horizon benefit columns, pure-early code channel, unbounded damage. Two gate columns and their two scale parameters and one sharpness parameter are removed. RECOMMENDATION REVERSED BY THE 300M CHECK, which is the reason to run cross-panel validation before simplifying. On WSD80 removing both gates changes nothing, so the conclusion there was that the model's namesake structure is inert and should be dropped. On 300M it is LOAD-BEARING and dropping it breaks the single most important behaviour the model has. With the gate the predicted mean pair gain over the 238 matched pairs is -0.000458 and -0.000680 against an observed -0.001086, correct in sign and order. Without it the prediction FLIPS to +0.000802 and +0.000622 -- the model starts claiming a two-phase advantage on a panel where NO asymmetric policy beats the best tied one. That is precisely the failure mode this project exists to avoid, the one where the incumbent invents about 0.029 of phase gain on negative controls. All-row RMSE also degrades, 0.006447 to 0.006614 and 0.006606 to 0.006663 on identical folds. The asymmetry is interpretable rather than mysterious. WSD80 has two domains under heavy repetition, 4.79 epochs at its optimum, where the gate has nothing to distinguish; 300M has 39 buckets at a median of 1.01 epochs, where whether late exposure can be absorbed is exactly what separates policies. The gate earns its place on the panel that can see it, like the damage law in SUR-111.
reopen_condition: DO NOT adopt the WSD80 simplification. The gate must stay. This is a worked example of a WSD80-only ablation producing a recommendation that would have broken cross-panel consistency, and every remaining ablation in this project should be checked on 300M before any structure is removed.

title: The optimum-distance gate is at or beyond the panel's resolution
material_novelty: Measures what the failing gate is actually asking for, using the raw panel and no model. Every structural route to the late-share bias is now closed -- saturating damage voided, gate placement irrelevant, the gate itself inert, novelty constructs dead -- so the remaining question is whether the target is resolvable at all. The fixed-aggregate fiber through the observed optimum answers it directly: hold total code epochs at 4.79 and vary only the phase split.
evidence: MEASURED FIBER at total code epochs 4.79, interior rows only, no model. By late share: 0.390 gives 0.941685, 0.420 gives 0.938327, 0.450 gives 0.935902, 0.480 gives 0.936963, 0.500 gives 0.935468, 0.510 gives 0.937989, 0.540 gives 0.938199, 0.570 gives 0.943056. The argmin at 0.500 beats 0.450 by 0.00043. The window from 0.45 to 0.51 spans 0.0025 in total and is NON-MONOTONE, with 0.480 worse than both neighbours. The panel's seed sigma is 0.004633. So across the entire band the gate polices, the measured response varies by LESS THAN ONE SEED SIGMA, and the location of the minimum is not determined to better than about plus or minus 0.05 by the data. The model predicting a late share of 0.438 to 0.455 against an observed argmin at 0.500 is therefore a difference the panel cannot resolve. The fiber does contain real signal further out -- BPB rises steeply to 0.952744 at 0.720 and 0.964577 at 0.780, and to 0.941685 at 0.390 -- so the model is right about the broad shape and is being failed on the unresolvable part of it. QUANTIFIED BY RESAMPLING, which turns the eyeball comparison into a number. Resample every interior outcome with the panel's own seed sigma of 0.004633 and re-take the argmin, 4000 draws. The observed argmin at (0.100, 0.500) moves to a 5th-to-95th percentile range of 0.050 to 0.150 in early share and 0.400 to 0.550 in late share. The MEDIAN distance of the resampled argmin from the observed one is 0.0500 -- exactly the gate threshold -- with the 90th percentile at 0.1118. So a PERFECT model, one that predicts the true expected surface exactly, handed a re-run of this panel would clear the 0.05 distance gate only 47.2 percent of the time. The gate asks a model to hit a target the measurement itself locates only within 0.112 at 90 percent confidence. And the model's predicted optimum at about (0.11, 0.45) sits roughly 0.05 from the observed argmin, which is precisely the typical distance the argmin moves under its own noise. The prediction is inside the noise band of the quantity it is scored against.
reopen_condition: The gate's achievable ceiling on this panel is about 47 percent, not 100. The model's 3 of 11 on fresh seeds is a real shortfall against that ceiling, not against a perfect score, and should be stated that way. This still does not excuse the failure, but it does mean any model passing this gate reliably on WSD80 should be suspected of fitting the argmin's noise -- which is consistent with the variants that DID pass it, SUR-104's 24/24 and the earlier 4/4s, later proving to be artifacts. Promotion criteria for this panel should rest on the three resolvable gates plus cross-panel consistency, with this gate reported as resolution-limited.

title: Conflict channel is load-bearing; pure-early code channel is inert
material_novelty: Ablates the two channels that had never been tested, with the absorption gates RETAINED per the SUR-112b reversal. Fresh WSD80 seeds 6-8, unbounded damage as SUR-111 requires for this panel.
evidence: CONFLICT IS ESSENTIAL. Removing the signed decay-phase off-domain channel moves interior OOF RMSE from 0.006478-0.007213 to 0.009087-0.009501, about 40 percent worse, and the total from 9 of 12 to 1 of 12 -- it stops clearing the RMSE gate at all. This partly resolves the channel's standing ambiguity: its SIGN is not robustly identified across column sets, +0.195 with one set and -0.105 with another, but the column plainly carries real information. Sign interpretation and explanatory value are separate questions and only the first is unsettled. PURE-EARLY CODE IS INERT. Removing it gives 0.006461-0.006706 against the reference 0.006478-0.007213, marginally BETTER, with the same 9 of 12 total. CROSS-PANEL CHECK PASSED WITHOUT A NEW RUN, per the rule adopted after SUR-112b. The 300M port never contained a pure-early channel and still beats HPR outright at 0.00520-0.00522 against 0.006800, so two independent panels agree the channel is unnecessary. Note the same reasoning shows CONFLICT is WSD80-specific: the 300M port has no conflict channel either and works, which is expected since that channel reads late off-domain share against a designated eval domain and 39 buckets have no such designation. Distance is 0 of 3 on seeds 6-8 under every variant, consistent with the known 3-of-11 rate on fresh seeds and with SUR-115's finding that this gate is resolution-limited.
reopen_condition: The pure-early channel can be dropped, removing one column and two nonlinear parameters. That leaves the WSD80 model as: intercept, signed conflict, four horizon benefit columns, two absorption gates, unbounded damage. The conflict channel's SIGN remains unidentified and is the cleanest thing for the batch-size sweep to settle, since gradient conflict should scale with gradient noise while epoching harm should not.

title: Promotion case withdrawn after independent audit
material_novelty: Records the four defects an independent Codex audit found in the promotion case of 2026-08-09, each verified against the artifacts before acceptance.
evidence: ALL FOUR AUDIT FINDINGS VERIFIED AND ACCEPTED. ONE, the headline scorecard mixed estimators. The RMSE 14/14, Regret@1 14/14 and gain-error 14/14 figures are attached in this registry to WSD80-SUR-104, whose own status reads completed_negative_gate_gains_void, while the distance 3/11 came from WSD80-SUR-103. The handoff table combined the voided model's three best numbers with the surviving model's worst one. SUR-103's actual tally is RMSE 11/11, Regret@1 10/11, gain 11/11, distance 3/11. TWO, the 300M knee comparison was not design-matched. The knee fit's blocks are near, late, damage and departures, with NO absorption gate; the port's are near, late, absorbed and damage. Comparing 0.00520 against 0.00628 attributed to the damage law a difference that includes a whole missing block. The claimed 17-21 percent improvement is wrong; the audit puts the matched figure at about 3-8 percent. THREE, optimum and gain are FULL-DATA diagnostics, not out-of-fold. The shape is selected on np.arange(len(response)) and the head fitted on the whole panel. They were presented in the handoff as gates alongside two genuinely out-of-fold metrics. Only RMSE and Regret@1 are validated. FOUR, the 47 percent resolution ceiling is not an oracle pass probability. Noise was added to observations that already contain noise, giving roughly sqrt(2) times the true sampling spread, and the quantity measured -- how far a re-perturbed argmin moves -- is not the quantity claimed, which is how often a fixed correct prediction lands within 0.05 of a fresh argmin. It overstates the difficulty, so the 3-of-11 shortfall is LARGER than reported, not smaller. CORRECTED POSITION: two validated out-of-fold gates on the surviving unbounded shared-shape model, RMSE 11/11 and Regret@1 10/11, with distance failing and gain not independently validated. Not promotable.
reopen_condition: The audit also identifies what survived and it is not nothing: three ingredients are independently load-bearing on WSD80 -- a boundary-localised early-code feature that stops the raw optimum collapsing to zero early code, a separate late-response clock needed for both fit and interior optimum geometry, and a signed late-phase control needed for policy selection. Generic polynomial and tensor-spline baselines fail badly, so this is structured inductive bias rather than added flexibility. It is not confirmed causality: an inverse boundary kernel matches the exponential survival kernel, and the signed coefficient is too unstable to call gradient conflict. Next work should start from the audit's own artifacts at reference_outputs/gated_absorption_independent_audit_20260809/.

title: Bucket-general surrogate: family-pooled, no semantic assignment
material_novelty: Removes every structure that referenced a bucket by semantic identity. The audited WSD80 model assigned three of its five structures by hand using knowledge that one domain is code and the other is off-target text: an early-boundary kernel on code, repetition damage on code, and a signed late-share control on broad. In production the bucket identities are not available that way -- buckets arrive classified by TOPIC, with quality splits inside each topic -- so a surrogate that needs to be told which bucket matches the eval cannot be deployed. Every structure becomes a sum over all buckets with parameters pooled at the FAMILY (topic) level, which is the one grouping production does supply. Quality splits inside a topic share that topic's nonlinear parameters and differ only through shrunk per-bucket amplitude departures, so classified quality is used as a grouping and never as a feature. The signed late control gets the substantive generalisation: instead of the off-target domain's late share, a free-signed late share PER FAMILY. On a two-domain panel that spans the original term exactly, since the shares sum to one; on 39 buckets it becomes three terms with no designated eval domain required. Damage and the early-boundary kernel were already geometric rather than semantic and simply move to sums over buckets. The reason the optimum collapses to zero early share is that early epochs cost about four times more per unit weight than late ones on WSD80, c0 = 21.089 against c1 = 5.369 -- a property of pool size and phase length, not of the bucket being code -- so the correcting feature should be geometric too, and buckets at risk are identifiable in advance from their own c0/c1 asymmetry.
evidence: ELEVEN SEEDS ON WSD80: 42 of 44, against the semantic model's 35 of 44 on the same eleven. RMSE 11/11 at 0.006657-0.007859, Regret@1 10/11 at 0.000155-0.005936, gain error 11/11, and OPTIMUM DISTANCE 10/11 at 0.0270-0.1087 against the semantic model's 3 of 11. The gate that has blocked this project throughout, and that was attacked with saturating damage, gate placement, multi-start and a resolution argument, passes once the hand-crafted semantic assignment is REMOVED. THE CAUSE IS IDENTIFIED AND IT WAS MY ERROR. The early-boundary kernel was hand-assigned to the CODE bucket. Given freedom to place it, the model puts it on BROAD text -- slot 0 scale fits 0.18 to 1.10 against an early-epoch range of 0 to 0.797, fully active -- and switches the code one OFF, slot 1 scale pinned at its upper bound 316.2 in six of eleven seeds where exp(-21.089/316) = 0.935 is near-constant and absorbed by the intercept. Mechanically this is sensible: the failure mode is starving a domain's early phase, broad text is the domain that CAN be starved early and recovered late cheaply, and code at 21.089 epochs per unit weight has its early share pinned by the damage term regardless. Every structural fix attempted earlier was compensating for a misplacement I had introduced. 300M UNCHEATABLE, three seeds: all-row RMSE 0.006306, 0.006484, 0.006214, BEATING HPR's 0.006800 outright, with predicted mean pair gain correctly negative at -0.000397, -0.000854, -0.000473 against observed -0.001086. Regret@1 fails at 0.005816. Two of three family boundary scales are stable across seeds (28.14/32.29/27.43 and 7.47/6.09/6.68), the first time that parameter has held still anywhere. REMAINING INSTABILITY, unchanged: the per-family late-share signs still flip across seeds, so that term is a nuisance control in the general setting too. One boundary scale per panel is unpinned. The single WSD80 distance failure, seed 8, collapses to early share exactly 0.000, the old pathology. MY DIAGNOSTIC WAS ALSO WRONG and is corrected: boundary_risk() returned epochs_early/epochs_late, which equals the phase-fraction ratio and is identical for every bucket by construction, 3.93 on WSD80 and 4.00 on all 39 300M buckets. It now returns total epochs per unit weight, which varies from 4.8 to 1723.9 on 300M.
reopen_condition: Strongest result in the project and it came from REMOVING hand-crafted structure. Before promotion: confirm on 300M that the families receiving active kernels are the ones the corrected boundary-risk metric predicts, since that is a prediction the model makes in advance; settle whether the late-share sign instability matters for selection or is absorbing noise; and address 300M Regret@1, which no variant has moved. The audit's four defects apply to any new scorecard -- keep estimators separate, do not mix OOF and full-data diagnostics, and match designs before attributing a difference to one term.

title: Pool geometry parameters by exposure stratum, taste parameters by topic
material_novelty: GEN-001 pools every nonlinear parameter by topic, because topic is the grouping production supplies. Measurement says that is right for some parameters and wrong for others. The 300M topics span enormous geometric ranges -- family 0 holds 31 buckets from 4.80 to 1723.89 epochs per unit weight, a 359-fold spread -- so forcing one boundary scale onto all of them cannot be right for any. The corrected boundary-risk metric duly FAILS to predict which family gets an active kernel: ranked by pool-exhaustion speed the families run 2 > 1 > 0, ranked by kernel activity they run 1 > 0 > 2. The split proposed here is between TASTE parameters and GEOMETRY parameters. Taste -- the readout exponent and the amplitudes, which say how much a topic helps this particular eval -- stays pooled by topic, because that is what topic membership predicts. Geometry -- the boundary scale, which depends on how fast a bucket exhausts its own pool -- is pooled instead by EXPOSURE STRATUM, buckets binned by total epochs per unit weight. Crucially this introduces no semantics. Pool size is observable from the swarm's own token counts without knowing what any bucket contains, exactly as the epoch multipliers already are. It is the same information the model already uses to build every exposure column.
evidence: PREDICTION CONFIRMED ON 300M. Pooling the boundary scale by EXPOSURE STRATUM instead of by topic stabilises it dramatically. By topic the three scales ran (28.14, 7.47, 29.93), (32.29, 6.09, 87.67) and (27.43, 6.68, 0.73) across seeds -- a worst-case spread of 120-fold, on the topic holding only two buckets. By stratum they run (5.94, 7.87, 24.54), (6.43, 10.13, 26.13) and (16.07, 13.67, 22.49), a worst-case spread of 2.7-fold, and the highest-exposure stratum is the tightest at 22.49 to 26.13 despite spanning the widest epoch range. AT NO FIT COST, which is the right shape for a grouping fix rather than a capacity increase. All-row RMSE is 0.006222-0.006550 against 0.006214-0.006484 by topic, both beating HPR's 0.006800, and the predicted mean pair gain stays correctly negative at -0.000298, -0.001047 and -0.000636 against an observed -0.001086, with seed 1 essentially exact. The strata are cut on the observed log-epoch distribution and land 13/13/13 over the 39 buckets, spanning 4.80-37.02, 41.05-91.63 and 91.83-1723.89 epochs per unit weight. The cross-tab shows why topic pooling failed: topic 0's 31 buckets spread across ALL THREE strata, so one scale was being asked to serve geometry differing 359-fold, while topic 2 had only two buckets to fit a scale from. NOT FIXED. Topic 0's readout exponent still sits pinned at its lower bound of 0.005 on all three seeds, and 300M Regret@1 is unmoved at 0.005816, which no variant in this project has ever shifted. FINAL TALLY, one configuration throughout, stamped NF=2 NS=2 on every result line, multi-start selection, 11 seeds: 40 of 44. Regret@1 11/11, which is the project's original blocker solved on every fold draw. Interior OOF RMSE 10/11. Gain error 10/11. Optimum distance 9/11 at 0.027042 to 0.095688, failing on seeds 3 and 8. Primary-target gain calibration +0.009615 against an observed +0.009594. Note the trajectory as methodology tightened: 42/44 then 43/44 then 40/44, each drop from removing a defect rather than the model worsening. The first two merged selection seeds or configurations; only 40/44 is a single configuration with the optimiser fix applied, and it is the number that should be quoted. NOT PROMOTED. Distance fails 2 of 11; one negative control fails (twitterAAE +0.005783 against 0.005, noise explanation tested and refuted); the 300M Regret@1 gate cannot be evaluated because its reference is unachievable on that row set; seed counts are 11 on WSD80, 3 on 300M, 1 for controls.
reopen_condition: Recommended for continuation, not promotion. The open question is whether seeds 3 and 8 are a specification gap or the distance gate outrunning the data; a matched-budget 14-restart measurement on seed 3 is running. Verdict and rerunnable code: reference_outputs/general_surrogate_round_verdict_20260810.md and fit_general_surrogate_wsd80_20260810.py.

title: The late-share sign instability was an unidentified common mode, not instability
material_novelty: Corrects a claim this project has repeated since SUR-098 and that the independent audit endorsed: that the signed late-phase control's coefficient flips sign across column sets and seeds, making it a nuisance control rather than evidence of anything. The flip is real but it is in a quantity that is not identified.
evidence: On WSD80 the family late shares SUM TO ONE, so only their CONTRAST is identified; the common level is absorbed by the intercept and free to wander. Reading the individual coefficients as unstable was reading an unidentified common mode. The contrast is stable. Across six stratified seeds it is -0.3138, -0.3484, -0.3569, -0.3370, -0.3188 and -0.3206, a spread of 0.043. Across the three topic-pooled seeds it is -0.2021, -0.3547 and -0.3560, spread 0.154. So the quantity was stable even before stratification, and stratification tightened it 3.6-fold. This upgrades what the term can be said to carry. A stable contrast means it holds consistent directional information about which family should be heavy late, which is a stronger statement than nuisance control. It does NOT restore the gradient-conflict interpretation, which needs more than a stable sign. SEPARATE DESIGN FLAW FOUND AND FIXED. WSD80's two buckets fall in strata 0 and 2, leaving stratum 1 EMPTY, so its boundary scale was fitted from no data and wandered across 504.6, 459.6, 0.545, 4.4, 0.322 and 328.6. The stratum count now adapts to the number of distinct exposure rates. The meaningful WSD80 scales are stratum 0 at 0.21-0.72, active on broad text, and stratum 2 at 2133-3162 near its bound, i.e. the code kernel switched off -- consistent with GEN-001.
reopen_condition: Any claim about a coefficient's stability must first establish that the coefficient is identified. On a simplex the shares sum to a constant, so level terms across all families are collinear with the intercept by construction and only contrasts are estimable. Check the other free-sign terms in this project for the same error.

title: The 300M Regret@1 comparison is not reproducible as specified
material_novelty: Explains why 300M Regret@1 has been EXACTLY 0.005816 for every variant this project has ever run -- every model, damage law, gate configuration and pooling scheme -- and finds that the reference it is compared against cannot be reproduced on this row set.
evidence: THE CONSTANCY IS BENIGN AND EXPLAINED. Every model selects row 405, the SECOND-BEST TIED policy, which sits exactly 0.005816 above the observed best. That is sensible behaviour: the models correctly decline the asymmetric policies ranked 2nd and 3rd, since this panel's truth is that no asymmetric policy beats the best tied one, and take the best tied policy they can predict. THE OBSERVED BEST IS AN ISOLATED OUTLIER. Row 480 sits 0.004334 clear of its nearest rival while the 2nd-to-3rd gap is 0.000222 and the 3rd-to-4th is 0.001259 -- roughly twenty times the local spacing. A well-calibrated surrogate arguably should NOT rank it first. THE COMPARISON DEFECT. Only 4 of 520 rows lie within 0.005816 of the best, and only ONE lies within 0.002678, namely row 480 itself. So HPR's published Regret@1 of 0.002678 is NOT ACHIEVABLE on this row set under the definition used here: any model scoring at or below it must have selected row 480 exactly, which would score 0.000000. Either HPR's regret is computed on a different row set, with a different definition, or against a different best row. This project has been comparing against a number whose conditions it cannot reproduce. This is the same class of error the independent audit found in the promotion scorecard -- comparing quantities computed under different estimators -- and it means every 300M Regret@1 FAIL recorded in this registry is uninterpretable rather than a genuine shortfall.
reopen_condition: Do not report 300M Regret@1 against the 0.002678 reference until its provenance is established: which rows, which definition, which best. If HPR's number is computed on the 280 two-phase rows rather than all 520, or on a correspondence-group basis, the comparable figure for these models must be recomputed the same way. Until then the honest statement is that the 300M selection gate has no validated reference, not that the models fail it.

title: GEN-002 negative controls: 25 of 26, with a real trade against the semantic model

title: A 43/44 tally was computed across two model configurations and withdrawn
material_novelty: Records a self-caught repetition of the exact defect the independent audit found in the promotion scorecard, committed within an hour of writing the rule against it into this registry.
evidence: A tally of 43 of 44 over eleven WSD80 seeds was computed for GEN-002, with optimum distance reported as 11 of 11. It combined TWO CONFIGURATIONS. Seeds 0-5 were run before the empty-stratum fix, with a hardcoded three strata of which one is EMPTY on a two-bucket panel, and seeds 6-10 after it, with two strata adapted to the panel's distinct exposure rates. The parameter lines show it directly: five seeds report two boundary scales, six report three. WHAT SURVIVES. Seeds 6-10 under the FIXED configuration give 4/4, 4/4, 4/4, 4/4 and 3/4, so 19 of 20, with distance 5 of 5 in the range 0.027042 to 0.041231 and the single failure being seed 10's gain error at 0.004456 against a 0.004439 limit, over by 0.000017. Seed 8's recovery is real and explicable: it was GEN-001's lone distance failure at optimum (0.000, 0.542) and now gives (0.083, 0.475), which follows from removing a boundary scale that was being fitted from no data at all. WHAT DOES NOT. The 43 of 44 headline and the distance 11 of 11 claim, both withdrawn. Seeds 0-5 are being rerun under the fixed configuration so the eleven seeds describe one model. Note that seeds 0-5 ALSO scored 4/4 each under the pre-fix configuration, so both configurations look strong. That is not a defence: 'both look good' is not a result about either, and a merged tally overstates the evidence for the one actually intended for promotion.
reopen_condition: The rule is easy to state and evidently easy to violate, because the failure does not look like an error when made -- every number is real, they simply do not describe one thing. Any tally in this project should record the configuration hash or parameter count alongside each seed, so that merging incompatible runs is visible rather than silent.

title: Seed 3 is a SPECIFICATION failure; the optimum is determined by the data
material_novelty: Found by rerunning seeds 0-5 after the empty-stratum fix. On WSD80 the two configurations are STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL -- two buckets with two distinct exposure rates give each bucket its own boundary scale either way, and the third stratum's parameter was simply unused -- yet seed 3 moves from 4 of 4 with distance 0.033541 at optimum (0.070, 0.485) to 2 of 4 with distance 0.092500 at (0.013, 0.530). The only thing that changed is the search dimension, 10 parameters against 9.
evidence: The WSD80 objective is MULTI-BASIN and the optimiser's path decides which optimum is found; a change that alters nothing structural flips the result. Seeds 0, 1 and 2 are unaffected at 4 of 4, so the sensitivity is seed-specific rather than uniform. This is the same bimodality diagnosed hours earlier for the saturation scale, where a basin comparison on the inner-fold objective showed differential evolution had simply missed the better optimum, and where multi-start was established as the legitimate remedy because it selects on the CV objective and never on a gate. That remedy was never applied to this model. CONSEQUENCE: every single-run tally for this model is provisional, including the seeds 6-10 result of 19 of 20 that was being treated as solid. Multi-start over each boundary scale's full range is now added, refining from four starts per scale and keeping the best by inner-fold CV. MULTI-START DID NOT RESCUE SEED 3, and the basin comparison explains why in the worst possible way. Under multi-start the seed-3 fit gives 2 of 4 with distance 0.095688 at optimum (0.010, 0.532). A 4-of-4 solution at distance 0.033541 and optimum (0.070, 0.485) demonstrably exists for the same seed. Comparing the two on the INNER-FOLD objective, the only criterion selection may legitimately use: the DE solution scores 14.827697, the better-gating basin 14.845843 after refinement and 15.233310 unrefined. THE GATE-PASSING SOLUTION IS WORSE ON CV. It cannot be chosen without selecting on the gates, which is the post-outcome selection this project has withdrawn from repeatedly. For the saturation scale earlier, the same comparison came out the other way and the better basin was genuinely better on CV, which is what made multi-start legitimate there. Here it does not. THE UNDERLYING PROBLEM IS UNDERDETERMINATION, not optimisation. The two solutions differ by 0.12 percent in CV, so they are predictively near-identical, yet their recommended optima sit 0.077 apart in mixture space, one failing the distance gate at 0.0957 and one passing at 0.0335. A surrogate whose headline output, the mixture it recommends, moves that far between predictively equivalent fits cannot be used to choose a mixture. This was flagged in advance as more serious than any gate failure and is now measured rather than suspected. It also casts doubt on every gate comparison in this project between models whose CV differs by under a percent, including GEN-002 against GEN-001. UNDERDETERMINATION CLAIM WITHDRAWN. It rested on an unverified assumption and proper basin sampling refutes it. Eight independent optimiser restarts on seed 3 give: best CV 14.8116 with optimum (0.005, 0.535) at distance 0.1012; a second at +0.08 percent CV with (0.000, 0.540) at 0.1077; and SIX restarts at +17.86 to +17.97 percent CV, all recommending about (0.070, 0.485) at distance 0.0335 and passing. WITHIN 1 PERCENT OF THE BEST CV the recommended optima span only 0.000 to 0.005 in early share and 0.535 to 0.540 in late, a maximum pairwise spread of 0.0071 against a 0.05 gate tolerance. The optimum is WELL determined among predictively equivalent fits. The gate-passing solutions are 17.9 percent worse on CV, not the 0.12 percent previously reported. THE SOURCE OF MY ERROR. The 0.12 percent figure came from importing the better-gating boundary scales, refining with L-BFGS-B, and reading the resulting CV WITHOUT checking whether the refined point still produced the gate-passing optimum. It had almost certainly relaxed back into the original basin, since 14.8458 is within 0.12 percent of 14.8277, so two solutions from the SAME basin were compared and the difference reported as a conflict between gate performance and the selection criterion. No such conflict exists. CONSEQUENCES. The distance gate measures something real and passing it is not optimiser luck. Seed 3's failure is a SPECIFICATION failure: the best-fitting model recommends (0.005, 0.535), which is wrong, and the models that recommend correctly fit far worse. Comparisons between models differing by under a percent in CV are NOT contaminated as I claimed, so the GEN-002 versus GEN-001 comparison stands. SECOND CORRECTION: the withdrawal was itself too hasty. Sampling seed 0 the same way gives the OPPOSITE picture from seed 3. Seed 3's two restarts within 1 percent of best CV span 0.0071, comfortably inside the 0.05 tolerance. Seed 0's two span 0.0610, EXCEEDING it, with the best-CV solution recommending (0.050, 0.505) at distance 0.0502, a fail, and the next at (0.000, 0.540) at 0.1077. TWO DEFECTS IN MY MEASUREMENT, both fatal to the conclusion in either direction. First, only TWO restarts of eight fall within 1 percent of the best on each seed, so the reported spread is simply the distance between two points and cannot estimate anything. Second, the sampler used popsize 8 and maxiter 40 while the main run uses 12 and 70 plus multi-start refinement, so the sampler's best is not the main run's solution -- which is exactly why seed 0's sampled best fails the distance gate at 0.0502 while the main run records seed 0 as 4 of 4 at 0.042500. The two are different solutions and were compared as though they were not. NET POSITION: I claimed the optimum was underdetermined, withdrew that and claimed it was well determined, and neither claim is supported. Both were drawn from two-point spreads under mismatched optimiser settings. What IS solid is that six of eight restarts on each seed converge to a single gate-passing optimum at about 18 percent worse CV, which is a stable but clearly inferior basin. SETTLED, at matched optimiser budget with fourteen restarts, which fixes both defects of the earlier attempts. Seed 3's distinct recommended optima: (0.005, 0.535) found once at the best CV of 14.8181, distance 0.1012 FAIL; (0.010, 0.530) found once at +0.1 percent, distance 0.0949 FAIL; and (0.070, 0.485) found TWELVE times at +17.8 percent, distance 0.0335 PASS. THE OPTIMUM IS DETERMINED. The two best-fitting solutions recommend optima 0.007 apart, well inside the 0.05 tolerance, so predictively equivalent fits agree with each other. The earlier claim of underdetermination is confirmed refuted, and the later retraction of that refutation was also wrong; this measurement, unlike both, has enough samples and a matched budget. THE FAILURE IS SPECIFICATION. The gate-passing basin fits 17.8 percent worse and attracts 12 of 14 restarts -- a large, easily found attractor that is a decisively worse predictor. It cannot be preferred without selecting on the gate. On this fold draw the likelihood genuinely prefers a near-zero early share, and on ten of eleven draws it does not.
reopen_condition: Concrete next target, no longer a search or identification question: the model is missing a term that ten fold draws' training rows happen to supply and seed 3's do not. Compare seed 3's training rows against the others -- which policies are absent, and does their absence remove the evidence that early share must be positive. The measured cliff at exactly zero early share is the obvious candidate, since only 5 of 284 interior rows carry the code-side version of it.

title: Multi-target frozen gate evaluated for GEN-002: refuted
material_novelty: Closes the frozen WSD80 gate requiring multi-target to improve at least two code-target selection or gain diagnostics beyond paired-bootstrap uncertainty against the SAME form fitted independently per target. SUR-103 measured this on the semantic model; it had not been measured on the bucket-general one, which places its structures differently.
evidence: GATE FAILS: joint improves exactly ONE code-target diagnostic where at least two are required. Programming Languages, the primary: RMSE joint 0.006849 against independent 0.004439; Regret@1 joint 0.000155 against independent 0.005936, a 38-fold improvement and the one diagnostic joint wins; Regret@5 tied at 0.000000. github_cpp: RMSE 0.007437 against 0.004661; Regret@1 0.003738 against 0.001915, independent better; Regret@5 tied. github_python: RMSE 0.007340 against 0.004269; Regret@1 0.002589 against 0.001976 and Regret@5 0.001304 against 0.000000, independent better on both. Paired row bootstrap on the RMSE difference, 4000 draws, gives independent better BEYOND uncertainty on all three targets: +0.002400 with CI [+0.001716, +0.003136], +0.002767 with [+0.002106, +0.003420], and +0.003060 with [+0.002341, +0.003788], every interval entirely positive. CONSISTENT WITH SUR-103 on the semantic model, where independent won on 29 of 29 targets. The multi-target direction is now refuted on BOTH model families, which answers the round's central multi-target question rather than leaving it open. THE ASYMMETRY IS WORTH KEEPING. Sharing theta across 29 metrics acts as a regulariser that sharpens selection on the primary target dramatically while blurring fit everywhere, exactly the pattern SUR-103 found. A joint fit is the better choice if primary Regret@1 is what matters and fit is not; the gate as written weighs breadth across code targets, and on that criterion it loses.
reopen_condition: Do not pursue shared-latent-state multi-target fitting for this problem; two independent families now reject it with bootstrap-backed evidence. The primary-Regret@1 asymmetry is worth understanding on its own terms -- if selection on one designated target is the deployment objective, joint fitting is preferable despite worse fit, and that is a different question from the one the frozen gate asks.
