title: FATAL: the GEN-family solver projected out an arbitrary direction; every GEN result is void
material_novelty: Found by independent Codex 5.6 Sol Max review of GEN-002 and verified here from scratch. The bucket-general design puts the intercept AND one late-share column per family in the free block. Family shares sum to one, so the family-size-weighted sum of those columns reproduces the intercept exactly; the free block is rank deficient by construction. This redundancy was correctly DOCUMENTED in the round's own term specification and then not checked in the solver.
evidence: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, NOT TAKEN ON TRUST. On WSD80 the free block is 346x3 with rank 2 and a third singular value of exactly 0.0; the family-size-weighted sum of late-share columns reproduces the intercept to 0.0 absolute error. THE BUG. fit_head partialled the free block out using np.linalg.qr, whose reduced form returns one basis column per INPUT column. For a rank-deficient input the surplus Q column is an arbitrary direction; measured distance from the column space of free is 1.0000000000000002, i.e. it lies ENTIRELY outside the space being partialled out. The projector therefore deleted real signal from the response and from every constrained column, and which signal it deleted depended on how the families happened to be numbered. MAGNITUDE. Relabelling the two WSD80 families, with readout exponents swapped to match so the model is mathematically identical, moved primary-target predictions by RMS 0.09006 BPB and max 1.66386 BPB over 12 random shapes. The frozen gates are about 0.008 BPB, so the arbitrary component is ten times the quantity being gated. Codex independently measured RMS 0.07054 and max 1.30336 on its own shape draws, the same order. THE FIX. column_space() truncates on the singular values, keeping only directions the free block actually spans. Relabelling invariance is restored to RMS 2.219e-12, max 5.457e-12. BLAST RADIUS IS BOUNDED AND WORTH STATING. The semantic predecessor fit_gated_absorption_wsd80_20260807 has free = [intercept, w1_broad], a single family's late share, which is exactly the identified contrast and is full rank; the 300M port has free = ones(n,1), full rank. Both are UNAFFECTED. The defect was introduced precisely BY the generalisation from one designated late-share column to one per family, which is the change this round was built on. WHAT IS VOID: every GEN-001 through GEN-009 number, including the 40/44 WSD80 tally, the 25/26 controls, the 300M component regressions, and the multi-target refutation in GEN-008.
reopen_condition: Nothing from the GEN series may be cited until regenerated under the corrected solve. Reruns are in flight. Note that GEN-008's multi-target refutation is void as a MEASUREMENT but its conclusion is independently supported by SUR-103 on the semantic model, which is unaffected; do not treat the direction as re-opened without saying which evidence carries it.

title: A large boundary scale LINEARISES the kernel rather than switching it off
material_novelty: Raised by the same independent review and verified here. The round's headline mechanism claim was that, freed of semantic assignment, the model places the early-boundary kernel on the broad family and switches the code one off, evidenced by a fitted code scale of 316.2 giving exp(-21.089/316) = 0.935, read as near-constant and therefore absorbed by the intercept.
evidence: THE INFERENCE IS INVALID. For large k, exp(-E/k) = 1 - E/k + O(k^-2). The constant part is absorbed by the intercept, but the SURVIVING VARIATION is -E/k, and fit_head normalises every residualised column to unit norm before the sign-constrained solve, which cancels the 1/k factor entirely. A large scale therefore does not disable the term; it converts it into a linear early-exposure feature at full amplitude. MEASURED ON WSD80, matching the reviewer's figures to the digit: the residualised code-family column correlates 0.9999600 with negative early exposure at k = 316.2 and 0.9999996 at k = 3162.3. ADDITIONAL FINDING NOT IN THE REVIEW. The term is only genuinely nonlinear at SMALL scale, and only for one family: at k = 1.0 the correlations are 0.9942501 for broad against 0.5399336 for code, and at k = 0.2 they are 0.8806870 against 0.3968361. So the fitted broad scale of 0.18-1.10 sits where the column is nearly linear for broad but strongly nonlinear for code, which is the opposite of how the mechanism was described. CONSEQUENCE: the claim that removing semantic features let the model discover the correct bucket for the kernel is WITHDRAWN. Scale alone cannot establish that a term is inert; only a zero amplitude or a column ablation can. GEN-014 runs that ablation.
reopen_condition: The mechanism story for this round rested on this reading. If the ablation shows the boundary block carries real weight on BOTH families, the honest description is that the term is active everywhere and the fitted scales set how nonlinear it is per family, not which bucket it applies to.

title: The nonlinear form transfers across a 5x change in model scale
material_novelty: Closes the round charter's 'other swarms as transfer checks' requirement, which had no evidence at all. The sharpest available transfer is a change of MODEL SCALE at fixed swarm design: the 60M and 300M panels share the same 39 buckets, the same 3 families and the same epoch geometry, 4.80 to 1723.89 epochs per unit weight, so only the trained model differs. Tests the user's standing requirement that the form fit at any scale. Run under the corrected rank-truncating solve.
evidence: DESIGN. Three arms per scale and target on identical grouped folds: own = theta selected in-fold at this scale; frozen = theta selected at the OTHER scale with only the per-target head refit, nothing else; floor = intercept only. The frozen arm never sees a single row of the target scale, not even through fold selection. Variance recovered = (floor - frozen) / (floor - own). UNCHEATABLE TRANSFERS ROBUSTLY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. 60M with theta from 300M: penalty 1.099, 1.116, 1.120; variance recovered 0.924, 0.922, 0.909. 300M with theta from 60M: penalty 1.208, 1.134, 1.145; recovered 0.874, 0.921, 0.914. TABLE-9 MACRO transfers well downward and unstably upward. 60M with theta from 300M: penalty 1.018, 1.099, 1.056; recovered 0.977, 0.884, 0.923. 300M with theta from 60M: penalty 1.886, 1.158, 1.234; recovered 0.193, 0.874, 0.806. INTERPRETATION. On 11 of 12 cells, nonlinear parameters fitted at one model scale recover 80 to 98 percent of what in-scale selection recovers, which is evidence they describe training dynamics rather than one panel's idiosyncrasies. The single bad cell is Table-9 macro at 300M under seed 0's fold draw, where transferred theta recovers only 19 percent; the same transfer on seeds 1 and 2 recovers 87 and 81 percent, so it is a fold-draw instability rather than a directional failure. SOLVER NOTE. The pre-fix run of this same comparison gave 2.494x penalty and NEGATIVE variance recovered, -0.365, on that cell -- worse than the intercept. The corrected solve improves it to 1.886x and +0.193. The 39-bucket panels are much less affected by the defect than WSD80 because with three families the arbitrary direction is a smaller share of the free block. THREE QUALIFICATIONS FROM THE SECOND REVIEW, ALL VERIFIED, WHICH SHRINK THIS CLAIM. FIRST, THE STATISTIC WAS MISNAMED: it differenced RMSE, which is not a variance share. Recomputed on MSE, the additive quantity, recovery is 0.864 to 0.983 on the eleven good cells and 0.248 on the bad one -- slightly stronger and now correctly named. SECOND, A LEAK IN THE OWN ARM: own-scale theta was selected once on ALL target rows and then scored across the outer folds, while the frozen arm stayed blind, so the two arms were not comparable. The leak flattered own and therefore UNDERSTATED transfer, but it is a defect; selection is now nested inside each outer fold and the comparison rerun. THIRD AND MOST LIMITING, THE PANELS SHARE THEIR POLICY COORDINATES. 60M and 300M share 241 of 242 policies exactly, 300M and delphi_3e18 share ALL 280, and the epoch geometry c0+c1 is IDENTICAL across all three scales. So this measures whether the response shape is stable across model scale AT FIXED SWARM DESIGN; it does NOT show that theta generalises to a new design, which is what this row's original wording implied. The rerun therefore also scores the frozen arm separately on target rows whose exact policy is ABSENT from the source scale, which is the only subset where the source could not have been fitted at the same coordinates.
reopen_condition: The one unstable cell should be diagnosed before this is cited as clean: check whether seed 0's Table-9 fold draw is unusual in support distance or phase TV, and whether the instability survives more seeds. Also worth testing transfer to the delphi_3e18 scale, which load_scale supports and this run did not use.

title: ABLATION: the boundary kernel TRADES gates -- it fixes the late share and breaks the early share
material_novelty: Settles by removal what GEN-016 showed could not be settled by reading the fitted scale. Drops the whole boundary block, both families at once, and reruns the frozen WSD80 gates against identical folds, identical selection and identical heads, on all eleven seeds. Corrected rank-truncating solve. NOTE: this harness's select() omits the multi-start refinement the production driver uses, so both arms are matched to each other but neither is the production estimator.
evidence: FIRST, A CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN EARLIER VERSION. On the first four seeds the tally was full 15/16 against ablated 16/16 and this row claimed a decisive simplification. IT DID NOT HOLD. Over all eleven seeds it is full 42/44 against ablated 41/44 -- indistinguishable, with the full model marginally ahead. The four-seed headline was noise, the same failure mode that killed the 24/24 and 23/24 claims earlier in this project. The extension to eleven seeds was run precisely because four seeds is not enough to promote on, and it paid. THE REAL RESULT IS A TRADE, NOT A WINNER, AND IT IS UNANIMOUS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Ablated is better on GAIN ERROR on 11 of 11 seeds, median 0.000440 against 0.003348, a 7.6-fold improvement, taking that gate from 9/11 to 11/11. Ablated is better on RMSE on 10 of 11 seeds, median 0.006666 against 0.006998. Full is better on DISTANCE, 11/11 against 9/11, better on 7 of 11 seeds, median 0.041231 against 0.047566. THE DECOMPOSITION IS THE POINT. Splitting the optimum into its two coordinates against the true (0.100, 0.500): the FULL model averages early share 0.0693, an error of -0.0307, and late share 0.4854, an error of -0.0146. The ABLATED model averages early share 0.1049, an error of +0.0049, and late share 0.4539, an error of -0.0461. Mean absolute early error is 0.0076 ablated against 0.0307 full, four times better; mean absolute late error is 0.0461 ablated against 0.0146 full, three times worse. So INCLUDING the block shifts the selected optimum toward lower early share, from an almost exact 0.105 down to 0.069, and higher late share, from 0.454 to 0.485. Distance sums the two and therefore hides both effects. UNCERTAINTY, added after the second review asked for it: paired per-seed differences with 20000 bootstrap resamples give |early error| -0.023091 with CI [-0.032818, -0.013091], |late error| +0.031455 with CI [+0.024816, +0.035909], and gain error -0.002777 with CI [-0.003519, -0.001936]. All three exclude zero. Caveat: the eleven seeds are eleven fold-PARTITIONS of one dense surface, so these intervals measure selection variability across partitions, NOT sampling uncertainty on new data. THE TERM-LEVEL MECHANISM CLAIM IS WITHDRAWN, WRONG-SIGN. An earlier version of this row said the kernel breaks the early share. It cannot. The column is exp(-c0*w0/kappa) with a NON-NEGATIVE amplitude, so its derivative in early share is -(alpha*c0/kappa)*exp(...) <= 0: the term makes a HIGHER early share give LOWER predicted loss, and it carries no late-share dependence at all. Verified directly -- the code column falls monotonically from 0.999844 to 0.998439 as early share goes 0.02 to 0.20. The observed shift is therefore a TOTAL REFITTING effect, produced by re-optimising the other nonlinear parameters, the ridge and the heads once the block is removed, not by the term acting on the optimum. THE ESTIMATOR SPLIT. Reporting 42/44 against 41/44 mixes nested-OOF with full-data diagnostics, the same defect this project accepted in SUR-116. Correctly split: nested-OOF full 22/22 against ablated 21/22; full-data full 20/22 against ablated 20/22. CONSISTENT WITH GEN-016. In the seeds where the code family receives amplitude -- 16.48, 13.03, 15.74, 7.32, 12.31, 9.52, 10.00, 8.82, 16.66 -- the fitted scale sits at 1796.7 to 3162.3 against an upper bound of 3162.3, so it is pegged in the fully linearised regime where the column is a linear early-exposure term. A linear early-exposure penalty is exactly what would depress the recommended early share, which is what is measured.
reopen_condition: This localises the specification gap to ONE COORDINATE rather than leaving it as a distance failure: no configuration tested gets both shares right, and the two are controlled by different structures. The next move is a term that raises the late share without touching the early one -- the late-horizon benefit readout is the obvious candidate, since it is currently degenerate with the near readout on the tied diagonal. Do NOT promote either arm on distance alone; report the coordinate decomposition instead, because the aggregate hides a four-fold and a three-fold effect pointing opposite ways.

title: Negative controls on five seeds: 23/26, not the 25/26 one seed suggested
material_novelty: GEN-005 evaluated the frozen broad-text control gate on ONE seed. Selection is reseeded per seed, so a single draw cannot distinguish a model that puts no gain on broad text from one whose broad-text gain happens to land low on the seed that was run. Rerun on five seeds under the corrected rank-truncating solve.
evidence: 23 of 26 negative controls hold on ALL five seeds, against the 25 of 26 that one seed reported. THE THREE FAILURES: gab, 2 of 5 seeds above the 0.005 limit, worst +0.013084, spread 0.008476; twitterAAE_HELM_fixed, 2 of 5, worst +0.009614, spread 0.006451; redpajama, 1 of 5, worst +0.005122, spread 0.003199. GEN-005 recorded only twitterAAE, at +0.005783; on five seeds its worst is +0.009614, nearly double. THE FAILURES ARE NOT INDEPENDENT, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL FINDING, THOUGH THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS ROW OVERSTATED IT. All five threshold breaches fall on seed 1 or seed 2, and the three failing metrics are the three largest seed-1-and-2-versus-rest increases. Quantified after the second review challenged the wording: seeds 1 and 2 average higher on 15 of 26 controls, and both exceed every other seed on 13 of 26 -- not 'almost every metric', which is what this row originally claimed. Note too that every target shares the same selected theta, so correlated motion across metrics is partly STRUCTURAL and is not independent corroboration. Examples of the pattern: 4chan +0.001108 and +0.001559 against +0.000037, +0.000030 and +0.000020 on the other three seeds; dolma-v1_5 +0.000238 and +0.000337 against +0.000002, +0.000001 and +0.000001; ptb +0.000866 and +0.001353 against about +0.000005. So this is not three noisy metrics, it is two of five selections landing in a regime that manufactures phase gain across the board, and the three breaches are simply the metrics with the least headroom. THE PRIMARY IS AFFECTED TOO. Predicted gain on Programming Languages ranges +0.009247 to +0.014412 across the five seeds against an observed +0.009594, so the same two seeds overstate the real gain by roughly 50 percent. GEN-005's headline that primary calibration was near-exact, +0.009615 against +0.009594, was a property of one seed. THE SHARPEST CONTROLS STILL HOLD EVERYWHERE: c4_en worst +0.000046, c4_100_domains +0.000042, falcon-refinedweb +0.000152, dolma_100_subreddits +0.000129, against the incumbent repaired RPL's roughly 0.029 on the first and last. Code positives hold: github_cpp +0.010508 to +0.013933, github_python +0.010007 to +0.011453.
reopen_condition: The correlated inflation is the thing to chase, not the three individual metrics. Identify what distinguishes seeds 1 and 2's selected shape from the other three -- most likely a boundary-scale or damage-horizon regime that adds phase structure globally -- and check whether the GEN-014 ablated form, which removes the boundary block entirely, eliminates the inflation. If it does, the control gate and the ablation point the same way.

title: The 300M phase-sensitive gate, measured with a clustered bootstrap: met on 1 of 3 seeds
material_novelty: The frozen 300M gate asks for one phase-sensitive diagnostic improved beyond clustered-bootstrap uncertainty without regressing the other. It had NEVER been evaluated for any model in this project; earlier rounds reported pooled RMSE and pair gains as point estimates, which cannot answer it. New diagnostic and new uncertainty treatment, run under the corrected rank-truncating solve.
evidence: DIAGNOSTIC. Paired gap error: every asymmetric policy has an exact aggregate-matched tied counterpart inside its correspondence group, so the difference between them removes the aggregate level and leaves only the phase contrast. RMSE of predicted gap against observed gap over 238 groups is therefore phase-sensitive in a way pooled RMSE is not -- a model can score well on pooled RMSE purely by placing the aggregate level correctly while getting every phase contrast wrong. Verified on a synthetic constant offset, which the diagnostic correctly scores at exactly 0.000000. UNCERTAINTY. Bootstrap over correspondence KEYS, not rows: the two members of a pair share a checkpoint, so resampling rows would break the pairing and understate the spread. 2000 resamples. COMPARISON. Shared theta across both targets against theta selected independently per target, identical grouped folds and identical heads, so the only difference is whether the nonlinear parameters must serve both targets at once. RESULT, gate met on ONE of three seeds. Seed 0: uncheatable shared 0.007981 against independent 0.008335, delta -0.000354 with 95 percent CI [-0.000659, -0.000085], entirely negative, so a real IMPROVEMENT; table9 delta +0.000085 with CI [-0.000488, +0.000636], indistinguishable, so no regression. That seed satisfies the gate as written. Seed 1: uncheatable delta +0.000059, CI [-0.000159, +0.000270], indistinguishable; table9 delta -0.001721 with CI [-0.005159, +0.000374], indistinguishable despite the large point estimate -- a good illustration of why the point estimates earlier rounds reported were not evidence. Seed 2: uncheatable delta -0.000004, CI [-0.000273, +0.000248]; table9 delta +0.000087, CI [-0.000414, +0.000535]; both indistinguishable. VERDICT: a gate satisfied on one of three fold draws is not satisfied. The honest reading is that shared theta and independent theta are indistinguishable on the 300M phase contrast, with one seed favouring shared. SECOND-REVIEW QUALIFICATION. Calling this gate NOT MET is correct for promotion purposes, but the stronger reading that shared and independent theta are EQUIVALENT is not established. The bootstrap resamples fixed out-of-fold errors without refitting, so it captures pair-sampling noise while ignoring model-fitting and selection uncertainty inside each outer fold, which understates the spread; and the single significant cell is unadjusted among six examined. The honest scientific status is UNDERPOWERED AND INCONCLUSIVE rather than equivalent.
reopen_condition: Three seeds is thin for a gate this close to zero; run more before treating the negative as settled. If the direction is worth pursuing, the seed-0 improvement is small but real and the mechanism is worth identifying, since GEN-008 found the mirror-image asymmetry on WSD80 -- shared theta sharpens selection on one designated target while blurring fit everywhere.

title: 300M components, corrected solve and matched baseline: 4 regressions, double the earlier count
material_novelty: Closes the frozen 300M requirement to report component regressions with a CHECKED-IN driver, and fixes two defects in GEN-009's attempt that an independent review raised: the sweep lived in an untracked scratch file so nothing in the repository fitted GEN-002 to the 300M panel, and its baseline was mismatched -- the model's OUT-OF-FOLD error was compared against the FULL-DATA standard deviation of the target. Here the baseline is an intercept fitted on the same training folds and scored on the same held-out rows.
evidence: FOUR components are worse than an out-of-fold intercept, against the two GEN-009 reported: sciq 1.568, arc_challenge 1.565, basic_skills_pattern 1.176, csqa 1.020. GEN-009 had sciq at 1.278 and arc_challenge at 1.479, and had basic_skills_pattern at 0.917 and csqa at 0.976, both nominally PASSING. Both flipped. TWO THINGS CHANGED AT ONCE and the flips cannot be attributed to either alone: the solver was corrected, and the baseline was matched. Direction of the baseline effect on its own is known -- an out-of-fold intercept is a WORSE predictor than the in-sample mean, so matching it should make ratios easier to pass, not harder. The ratios went UP anyway, so the corrected solve must have raised the model's error on these components by more than the baseline correction lowered the bar. That is consistent with the buggy projector having removed a direction that happened to flatter these fits. UNCHEATABLE remains clean: all 8 components well below 1, best ao3_english at about 0.20. TABLE-9 spans 0.20 to 1.57; the strong end is minerva_math_* at 0.20 to 0.22 and hellaswag, the weak end is the four regressions plus basic_skills_logical at 0.981. THE GATE EARNS ITS KEEP. GEN-002 beats HPR's published Uncheatable macro RMSE while being actively worse than predicting the mean on four of 47 Table-9 components. Macros alone would have concealed all four. SEED DEPENDENCE, MEASURED AFTER THE FACT AND FATAL TO THE HEADLINE COUNT. Rerunning on seeds 1 and 2 gives ONE regression and FIVE, against seed 0's four. Only csqa and basic_skills_pattern recur across seeds. arc_challenge reads 1.565, then 0.923, then 6586.432 -- the last being a numerical blow-up with an RMSE of 562.684614 BPB, documented in GEN-017. So the statement 'four components are worse than an intercept' is a property of seed 0, not of the model, and the honest summary is that the regression SET is unstable and at least one seed is contaminated by a solver blow-up.
reopen_condition: Do not quote a component regression count from a single seed. Re-measure after GEN-017's range guard is in place, over at least five seeds, and report the components that regress CONSISTENTLY rather than the union or any one draw.

title: theta matters enormously, and bad theta is CATASTROPHIC -- a robustness defect
material_novelty: Control demanded by the second review's logic rather than by the review itself. Once the own-arm selection leak was fixed, transferred theta scored as well as in-scale theta, which admits a deflationary reading: if theta barely matters then ANY theta transfers and the cross-scale claim is vacuous. This scores selected theta, 24 random draws from the search box, and an intercept floor on identical folds.
evidence: THE DEFLATIONARY READING IS REFUTED; SELECTION DOES REAL WORK. 60M Uncheatable: selected 0.008517 to 0.009207 against a random-theta MEDIAN of 0.017219 to 0.017354 and a floor of 0.019282 to 0.019346, so random theta recovers only 0.244 to 0.267 of the explainable MSE while selected recovers essentially all of it. Transferred theta recovering 0.94 to 1.00 is therefore a genuine finding, not an artefact of theta being irrelevant. BUT THE SAME CONTROL EXPOSES A FRAGILITY THAT MATTERS MORE. On 300M, random theta is not merely worse than selected, it is CATASTROPHICALLY WORSE THAN NO MODEL AT ALL: random medians of 0.416839, 0.057051 and 0.103023 against a floor of about 0.0177, which is 23-fold, 3-fold and 6-fold WORSE than predicting the mean. Explainable-MSE recovery is -654.2, -11.3 and -39.6. The design can produce predictions orders of magnitude outside the data range for parameter values inside its own declared search box. THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL -- IT FIRES IN PRODUCTION. The 300M component sweep at seed 2 returns arc_challenge RMSE 562.684614 BPB against a baseline of 0.085431, a ratio of 6586.4. A BPB error of 562 is a numerical blow-up, not a modelling shortfall, and it was produced by the ordinary nested selection procedure with no random draws involved. The same instability explains the 60M Table-9 cell where nested own-scale selection returned 0.039574 against a floor of 0.040194 -- selection essentially failed on that fold -- while TRANSFERRED theta on the same rows gave 0.023547, a penalty of 0.595, i.e. the frozen arm beat the in-scale arm by a wide margin. WHY IT MATTERS. Selection on a noisy inner-CV criterion over a box containing catastrophic regions will occasionally land in one, and nothing in the current model or driver detects it. Every single-seed number this project has reported for this family is exposed to that.
reopen_condition: Before any further gate reporting: bound the design. Either constrain the readout exponents and offset so predictions cannot leave a plausible BPB range, or reject any selected theta whose in-fold predictions exceed the observed target range by more than a small factor, and re-run selection. Then re-measure the component regressions, since GEN-015's set is seed-dependent and one of its three seeds is contaminated by this blow-up.

title: The blow-up has TWO unbounded sources, both now bounded; catastrophic region eliminated
material_novelty: Closes GEN-017's reopen condition, which required bounding the design before any further gate reporting. Diagnoses the mechanism rather than clamping the symptom, and measures the fit cost of each bound.
evidence: TWO SOURCES, FOUND BY DECOMPOSING THE DESIGN BLOCK BY BLOCK over 300 random parameter draws. FIRST, REPETITION DAMAGE reached 6.309e+22 against 3.907e+09 for the next-largest block: max(E-1,0)^tau with tau up to 10 and excess up to 255 epochs caps at 1.177e+24. Because fit_head normalises columns by their TRAINING norm, a test row with slightly larger excess is amplified by the tau-th power -- the extrapolation explosion. FIXED by writing damage in its bounded dimensionless form, (excess/E*)^tau / (1 + (excess/E*)^tau), with E* = 105 excess epochs FIXED at the value measured independently on 300M rather than fitted, since a free saturation scale with a wide bound is exactly what exploded. Max damage entry falls from 6.309e+22 to 0.410. Below the knee it is still a power law, so WSD80, whose excess tops out at 25.46, is essentially unaffected -- measured, seeds 0 and 1 stay 4/4 with distance IMPROVING from 0.045000 to 0.040078 and from 0.045069 to 0.040311. SECOND, AND THIS ONE THE DAMAGE FIX DID NOT TOUCH: the readout (E + offset)^-gamma is regularised only by the offset on buckets with EXACTLY ZERO weight, and the 300M panel has 41 such entries against WSD80's 2. With the offset floor at 1e-5 and gamma up to 2 a single design entry reaches 1e10. THIS IS WHY THE CATASTROPHE WAS 300M-SPECIFIC AND WSD80 WAS IMMUNE: WSD80's smallest real exposure is 0.1 epochs, capping its readout near 100, while 300M's is 4.593e-04. FIXED by raising the offset floor to 1e-2 epochs, capping the readout at 1e4. IT COSTS NOTHING: nested 300M Uncheatable RMSE is 0.005665 at the new floor against 0.005671 at the old one. RESULT, MEASURED WITH THE SAME RANDOM-THETA CONTROL THAT FOUND THE DEFECT. 300M Uncheatable explainable-MSE recovery from random parameters goes from -1559.5 to +0.517, i.e. random theta now BEATS the intercept where it was previously 23-fold worse; random median RMSE 0.013262 against a floor of 0.017782. 60M recovery rises from 0.244-0.267 to 0.440-0.615. The 60M Table-9 seed-0 SELECTION FAILURE is also gone: selected RMSE was 0.039574 against a floor of 0.040194, and is now 0.022925. RESIDUAL CASE, NOT YET CLOSED. arc_challenge at seed 2 still fails, though 355-fold less badly: RMSE falls from 562.68 to 1.583. The cause is now precisely localised -- the fit is FINE on 516 of 520 rows, median absolute error 0.027 and p95 0.110, but ONE row predicts 37.2 against an observed 1.16, and predicted range is 1.030 to 37.217 against an observed 1.108 to 2.041. It is monotone in the offset floor: caps of 1e4, 1e3, 1e2 and 3e1 give RMSE 1.5834, 0.4454, 0.1150 and 0.0859, with the predicted maximum finally matching the observed maximum, 2.033 against 2.041, at the tightest. THE REMAINING TRADE IS IRREDUCIBLE THROUGH THIS KNOB, AND THAT IS THE SEGMENT'S REAL RESULT. Measured on BOTH panels rather than inferred from one. Offset floor 1e-2: WSD80 scores 10/12 over three seeds (3/4, 4/4, 3/4) and arc_challenge sits at 18.534. Offset floor 1e-1, which is what arc_challenge needs -- its RMSE falls to 0.1150, a ratio near 1.35 -- COLLAPSES WSD80: seed 0 gives 2/4 with the optimum at (0.000, 0.535), the zero-early-share failure mode this project has fought since the beginning, and seed 1 gives 1/4 with Regret@1 0.010277 against a 0.004842 limit. So the offset floor that bounds 300M extrapolation destroys WSD80's optimum, and the floor that preserves WSD80 leaves 300M extrapolating. NOTE ALSO that my earlier claim the floor 'costs nothing' was measured on 300M Uncheatable RMSE alone and is WRONG as a general statement: on WSD80's distance gate 1e-2 already costs two cells relative to the 1e-5 baseline with bounded damage, which scored 4/4 on both seeds tested. THE SELECTION GUARD IS A PARTIAL MITIGATION WITH A STRUCTURAL CEILING. Rejecting theta whose held-out inner predictions leave the observed range by more than 3x the spread takes arc_challenge from 18.534 to 10.842, but cannot go further BY CONSTRUCTION: it only sees the rows it evaluates, so a vector can pass every inner fold and still explode on an outer-fold row it never saw. That is exactly what happens here. CONSEQUENCE: the extrapolation defect is NOT fixable by bounding this parameter. The readout needs to be bounded by construction rather than regularised by an additive offset whose floor trades against the WSD80 optimum. THE WSD80 SWEEP IS NOW COMPLETE AND IS WORSE THAN THE PARTIAL VIEW SUGGESTED. Totals over three seeds: floor 1e-2 gives 10/12; floor 1e-1 gives 3/12; floor 1e-0.7 gives 1/12. At 1e-0.7 the model fails outright -- interior OOF RMSE 0.018501, 0.018228 and 0.015255 against a 0.007954 limit, with recommended optima at (0.188,0.240), (0.092,0.338) and (0.030,0.388) against a true (0.100,0.500). So 1e-2 is effectively the MAXIMUM safe floor on WSD80, and the floors that would tame 300M extrapolation are far outside it. This is what makes GEN-021 important: it removes the extrapolation without touching the offset floor at all.
reopen_condition: Stop tuning the offset floor; both directions are now measured and they conflict. CAUTION, AND THIS NEARLY WENT IN AS THE RECOMMENDATION: a reference-normalised readout, ((E + offset)/(E_ref + offset))^-gamma, is a PROVABLE NO-OP. E_ref is constant, so it merely rescales the column, and fit_head normalises every constrained column to unit norm before the solve. Verified numerically -- maximum prediction difference 8.882e-16. That is the same error SUR-109 was killed for. What actually bounds the readout is a SATURATING form, 1/(1 + (E/E0)^gamma), which lies in [0,1] by construction, tends to 1 as exposure vanishes and to 0 as it grows, and keeps the monotone decreasing shape of the power law over the sampled range. Measured on WSD80 its range is 0.163 to 1.000 at gamma 0.5 and 0.001 to 1.000 at gamma 2.0, where the current power law reaches 3.0 and 82.6 and is unbounded as exposure goes to zero. It is the same Hill family already adopted for damage in this row, so the model gains no new machinery. Keep the bounded damage form and the selection guard regardless; both are free or nearly so. Do not quote 300M component numbers for reasoning-family targets until this is resolved -- arc_challenge remains 10x worse than an intercept at the best safe setting.

title: Saturating readout: a real 6.5x improvement, but bounded columns are not sufficient
material_novelty: Tests GEN-018's own recommendation instead of leaving it as advice. Replaces the divergent power-law readout (E + offset)^-gamma with the saturating form 1/(1 + (E/E0)^gamma), which lies in [0,1] by construction and belongs to the same Hill family already adopted for damage. Run on arc_challenge at seed 2, the worst measured failure in this project.
evidence: SUBSTANTIAL AND REAL. RMSE falls from 1.583382 to 0.242334, a 6.5-fold improvement; the regression ratio against a matched out-of-fold intercept falls from 18.534 to 2.837; the predicted maximum falls from 37.217 to 6.359 against an observed maximum of 2.041. This is the largest single improvement any structural change has produced on this failure. NOT SUFFICIENT, AND THE REASON IS INSTRUCTIVE. Every constrained column is now bounded -- the readout in [0,1] by construction, the boundary kernel exp(-early/scale) in (0,1], damage in [0,1) -- and predictions STILL reach 6.359 with a maximum absolute error of 5.199 on 4 rows. Bounded columns do not bound predictions: the departures block carries one column per bucket, 39 of them, and a held-out row can activate more of them simultaneously, or more strongly, than any training row did. The remaining exposure is therefore the WIDTH of the per-bucket departure block against its shrinkage, not the shape of the readout. THIS ALSO CONFIRMS THAT THE POWER LAW WAS NOT THE WHOLE STORY, which the offset-floor sweep had already hinted: tightening the floor to 1e-1 left arc_challenge near ratio 1.35 but destroyed the WSD80 optimum, while the saturating readout reaches ratio 2.837 without touching WSD80's parameterisation at all.
reopen_condition: Two things to try before treating this failure as structural. First, tighten the ridge on the departures block specifically -- it is currently the only shrunk block and its strength is selected in-fold against a criterion that never sees the exploding row. Second, test whether the departures block earns its place at all on the 39-bucket panels; it was introduced for per-bucket resolution and, if ablating it removes the residual extrapolation at acceptable fit cost, that is a simpler model as well as a safer one. Do NOT re-test the reference-normalised readout: it is a provable no-op, verified at 8.882e-16.

title: RESOLVED: saturating readout plus dropping per-bucket departures fixes the worst failure
material_novelty: Tests the second half of GEN-020's reopen condition. GEN-020 showed every constrained column was bounded and predictions still escaped, and localised the remaining exposure to the per-bucket departures block -- 39 columns whose combination on a held-out row can exceed anything seen in training. This removes that block.
evidence: arc_challenge at seed 2, the worst failure this project has measured, is FIXED and the fix REMOVES parameters rather than adding them. RMSE 0.081939 against a matched out-of-fold intercept baseline of 0.085431, a ratio of 0.959 -- the model now BEATS the mean on a component that was 6586 times worse than it. The predicted range is 1.076 to 1.326, entirely INSIDE the observed 1.108 to 2.041, so there is no extrapolation left at all; maximum absolute error is 0.827 against 36.057 originally. THE FULL PROGRESSION ON THIS ONE COMPONENT, each step measured on the same seed and folds: power law with departures 6586.432; plus bounded damage and offset floor 1e-2, 18.534; plus the selection guard, 10.842; saturating readout with departures, 2.837; saturating readout WITHOUT departures, 0.959. THE DIAGNOSIS BEHIND IT. Bounding every column was necessary but not sufficient, because bounded columns do not bound predictions when the design is wide: with 39 departure columns each in [0,1] and non-negative amplitudes, a held-out row can activate more of them, or more strongly, than any training row. Removing the block removes that degree of freedom entirely, which is why the predicted range collapses inside the observed one rather than merely shrinking.
reopen_condition: This is a promising simplification, NOT yet a validated one. Two costs are unmeasured and both must be paid before it is adopted: the per-bucket departures block exists to give quality splits inside a topic their own amplitude, so measure the fit cost on 300M Uncheatable and on WSD80's four frozen gates, and measure it across seeds rather than on the one component that motivated it. If departures turn out to cost nothing on either panel, the honest conclusion is that per-bucket resolution was never earning its place and the model loses a whole block.

title: The GEN-021 fix does NOT pay for itself: dropping departures costs 66 percent on 300M
material_novelty: Closes GEN-021's own reopen condition, which required measuring the cost of the two changes on the panels where the model is supposed to work rather than on the single component that motivated them. Four arms so the two changes are separable rather than confounded: baseline, saturating readout only, departures dropped only, and both.
evidence: 300M UNCHEATABLE, nested out-of-fold RMSE over three seeds. baseline 0.005885; saturating readout only 0.005811; departures dropped only 0.009773; both 0.009849. So DROPPING THE DEPARTURES BLOCK COSTS 66 PERCENT, against a frozen gate that allows 5 percent. That is a decisive rejection: GEN-021 fixed arc_challenge by removing the very structure that carries per-bucket resolution on a 39-bucket panel, and the cost lands squarely on the core metric. THE SATURATING READOUT, BY CONTRAST, IS FREE TO SLIGHTLY BETTER on 300M -- 0.005811 against 0.005885, a 1.3 percent improvement -- while delivering most of the extrapolation benefit: arc_challenge goes 18.534 to 2.837 from the readout change alone, before any departures surgery. WSD80, four frozen gates over three seeds. baseline 11/12; saturating 10/12; departures dropped 11/12; both 10/12. The saturating readout costs ONE cell, seed 2's optimum collapsing to (0.000, 0.490), the zero-early-share failure mode. A STRUCTURAL FACT THAT EXPLAINS THE WSD80 COLUMN AND WAS NOT OBVIOUS: dropping departures is an EXACT NO-OP on WSD80. That panel has two buckets in two families, one bucket each, so family_sums(near) equals near identically -- measured difference 0.000e+00 -- and the departures block is a perfect duplicate of the family-mean block. WSD80 therefore cannot inform this question at all, and the 11/12 for the no-dep arm is the baseline's number rather than independent evidence. NET POSITION: no free fix exists among the remedies tested. Every one trades against either 300M core RMSE or the WSD80 optimum. The saturating readout is the only change that is close to free and it is a trade, not a win.
reopen_condition: Adopt the saturating readout only if the WSD80 cell it costs is judged acceptable against the extrapolation it buys; that is a judgement call and should be made explicitly rather than by accumulating changes. Do NOT drop the departures block. The unexplored direction is between the two: keep per-bucket departures but shrink them far harder, since GEN-020 showed the residual extrapolation comes from that block's WIDTH against its shrinkage and the ridge is currently selected against a criterion that never sees the exploding row. A departures-specific penalty, selected on held-out prediction RANGE rather than on error, is the obvious next probe.

title: Departures shrinkage cannot be tested by a multiplier: the free ridge absorbs it
material_novelty: Tests GEN-022's proposal to keep per-bucket departures but shrink them far harder, by multiplying their penalty. Includes the control that shows why the test as designed cannot work.
evidence: THE SWEEP APPEARED TO SAY SHRINKAGE DOES NOTHING. Multiplying the departures penalty by 1, 10, 100 and 1000 left arc_challenge at ratios 2.821, 2.834, 2.762 and 2.992, with the predicted maximum stuck between 6.2 and 6.7 against an observed 2.041, while 300M Uncheatable RMSE stayed at 0.005811, 0.005805 and 0.005781 before degrading to 0.008414 at 1000. THE REASON IS A CONFOUND, NOT A NULL RESULT. The ridge is itself a fitted parameter, so the inner CV simply lowers it to cancel the multiplier. Measured selected ridges: at multiplier 1, 5.97e-01, 3.35e-01 and 1.17e-01; at multiplier 100, 7.09e-05, 3.21e-05 and 1.18e-05. The EFFECTIVE penalty sqrt(ridge) times multiplier is nearly identical in both cases -- 0.773, 0.579, 0.342 against 0.842, 0.567, 0.343. At multiplier 1000 the ridge pins at its 1e-06 lower bound and can no longer compensate, which is exactly where the 300M fit degrades. The departure amplitudes confirm it: their maximum stays around 5.2, 5.3 and 9.2 across the three multipliers, so they are not being shrunk at all in the fold that matters. THE REAL FINDING, WHICH IS SHARPER THAN THE ONE SOUGHT. The inner-CV criterion selects the same effective shrinkage no matter how the penalty is parameterised, and it will never select one that bounds predictions, because bounding predictions does not reduce inner-fold error. The criterion has to change; the parameterisation cannot be made to do this work.
reopen_condition: Any future sweep over a penalty term in this model must either fix the ridge or report the EFFECTIVE penalty, otherwise it measures the optimiser's compensation rather than the intervention.

title: SOLVED: selecting on predicted RANGE as well as error fixes extrapolation at no cost
material_novelty: Follows GEN-023's conclusion that the selection criterion, not the parameterisation, is what must change. Adds to the inner objective a penalty for predictions running outside the training target range, evaluated over EVERY row's design. Using unlabelled rows' features is not leakage -- a policy's mixture is known without consulting its outcome -- and it is precisely what lets selection see extrapolation that inner-fold error structurally cannot.
evidence: AT RANGE WEIGHT 1 EVERYTHING IMPROVES OR HOLDS, measured against the same folds, heads and arms. 300M Uncheatable nested RMSE 0.005775 against 0.005811 unpenalised and 0.005885 for the committed baseline. WSD80 frozen gates 11/12 over three seeds, equal to the baseline's 11/12 and recovering the cell the saturating readout alone had lost -- seed 2's optimum returns from (0.000,0.490) to (0.062,0.485). arc_challenge at seed 2 gives ratio 0.958 with predictions in 1.066 to 1.648 against an observed 1.108 to 2.041, so the model now BEATS an out-of-fold intercept on the component that was once 6586 times worse than it, and predicts nothing outside the plausible range. AT WEIGHT 10 the 300M fit is better still, 0.005730, and arc_challenge better still at 0.944, but WSD80 falls to 10/12 -- so weight 1 is the balanced setting and weight 10 trades the WSD80 optimum for marginal fit. THE FULL PROGRESSION ON arc_challenge SEED 2: 6586.432 originally; 18.534 after bounding damage and raising the offset floor; 10.842 with the selection guard; 2.821 with the saturating readout; 0.958 with the range criterion. CRUCIALLY, THIS KEEPS THE DEPARTURES BLOCK, so it avoids the 66 percent 300M penalty that deleting the block cost in GEN-022. This is the first remedy in this line of work that is not a trade.
reopen_condition: PROMISING, NOT VALIDATED. Three seeds per panel and a single component drive the extrapolation claim. Before promotion: run the full eleven-seed WSD80 tally, the multi-seed negative controls, and the whole 47-component Table-9 sweep under the range criterion, and confirm the 300M phase diagnostic and cross-scale transfer do not regress. Also check whether the range penalty makes the selection guard redundant, since both now address the same failure and only one should survive.

title: Range-selected surrogate validated at scale: better everywhere except Regret@1
material_novelty: Promotes the range-selected candidate into a checked-in module and runs the validation GEN-025's reopen condition demanded: the full eleven-seed WSD80 tally, five-seed negative controls, and the whole fifty-five-component 300M sweep on seed 2, the seed that previously produced the 562 BPB blow-up.

reopen_condition: TWO CAVEATS BEFORE PROMOTION. First, the 40/44 totals are NOT directly comparable: this candidate selects on the single primary target with no interior restriction, while the committed model selects jointly across 29 targets with one, so two estimator differences ride along with the range criterion. title: 40/44 is invariant across four configurations; the range criterion's WSD80 effect is a wash
material_novelty: Isolates what the range criterion actually contributes on WSD80 by running the committed DESIGN under the candidate's ESTIMATOR, which GEN-027 flagged as an unseparated confound. Adds a fourth arm, the committed power-law design WITH the range penalty.

Committed design under the candidate estimator, single target and no interior restriction: rmse 11/11, Regret@1 10/11, distance 8/11, gain error 11/11. Saturating readout plus range penalty under the candidate estimator: rmse 11/11, Regret@1 8/11, distance 10/11, gain error 11/11. Power-law design plus range penalty under the candidate estimator: IDENTICAL to the previous line, rmse 11/11, Regret@1 8/11, distance 10/11, gain error 11/11. TWO CORRECTIONS TO GEN-027 FOLLOW. GEN-014 found that dropping the boundary kernel raises mean early share from 0.0693 to 0.1049 under the POWER-LAW readout. Under the saturating readout it does the opposite: seed 0 falls to 2/4 with the optimum at (0.015,0.532). The two changes interact and the ablation result cannot be carried across.

title: 40/44 survives a FIFTH configuration; the WSD80 gates appear jointly capped for this family

title: PROMOTABLE: range-penalised selection is strictly better off-WSD80 and free on it
material_novelty: Consolidates the promotion case for the one change that survived every attribution test: penalising predicted-range excess during selection. Establishes what it does and does not buy, separately from the estimator and readout changes it was originally bundled with.
evidence: WHAT IT FIXES, AND THE FIX IS LARGE. The extrapolation defect that made this family unusable is gone. 300M arc_challenge falls from a ratio of 6586.432 against an out-of-fold intercept to 0.926 with the committed power-law design, or 0.958 with the saturating readout, and predictions stop leaving the observed range -- 1.052 to 1.621 against an observed 1.108 to 2.041. Component regressions at seed 2 fall from FIVE, including that blow-up, to THREE marginal ones with the committed design, at 1.063, 1.020 and 1.008, or to ONE at 1.036 with the saturating readout. Negative controls hold on 26 of 26 targets across five seeds against 23 of 26, and the correlated inflation regime that made two of five seeds manufacture phase gain on most metrics is gone. Predicted gain on the primary tightens to +0.008265 to +0.010382 against an observed +0.009594, where the committed model reached +0.014412. 300M Uncheatable nested RMSE improves to 0.005775 from 0.005885. WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY: anything on WSD80, where every configuration scores 40/44 regardless -- see GEN-032. THE SATURATING READOUT IS OPTIONAL AND ITS VALUE IS 300M-ONLY: it is worth one component regression against three, and nothing on WSD80, where the power-law and saturating arms agree gate for gate. THE MINIMAL PROMOTABLE CHANGE IS THEREFORE A ONE-LINE CHANGE TO THE SELECTION CRITERION, with no change to the model at all. That is the strongest form of the result: the model was never wrong, the criterion was -- it selected on fold error alone, which is blind to predictions that explode on rows the fold never scores.
reopen_condition: CORRECTION to this row's first version, which asked for the range weight to be swept inside folds. THAT REQUEST IS INCOHERENT, not merely unrun. The inner objective is error + w * excess^2 * error, so for any candidate w selection returns the theta minimising it; if competing w values are then scored by plain fold error, theta at w=0 minimises plain fold error over the whole space by construction, and w=0 wins always, independently of the data. The weight cannot be selected by predictive error at all. It is not a tunable hyperparameter but a STRUCTURAL COMMITMENT, the same kind of object as a link function or a non-negativity constraint, and it must be justified rather than fitted. The justification for w=1 is that it enforces a safety property the data cannot vote on -- predictions stay inside the observed range -- at no measurable cost on either panel, while w=10 buys marginally better 300M fit and costs a WSD80 gate cell. STILL GENUINELY UNRUN under the criterion: the 300M phase-sensitive diagnostic, cross-scale transfer, and components on seeds 0 and 1.

title: The 40/44 ceiling is a SELECTION limit, not arithmetic: 4/4 is attainable on every seed
material_novelty: Answers GEN-032's question directly rather than by further recombination. Optimises the four WSD80 gates themselves over the parameter vector -- which is exactly the post-outcome selection this project has withdrawn from repeatedly and must NEVER be used to fit a model -- purely to establish whether a gate-passing vector exists at all.
evidence: ALL FOUR GATES ARE JOINTLY SATISFIABLE ON EVERY SEED TESTED. Minimum total violation is exactly 0.000000 on seeds 0 through 4, with comfortable margins rather than knife-edge ones: seed 0 reaches rmse 0.006152 against 0.007954, regret 0.002842 against 0.004842, distance 0.030414 against 0.050000 and gain error 0.002351 against 0.004439. So the model FAMILY can represent solutions that pass everything, and the 40/44 wall that five cross-validated configurations hit is a property of the SELECTION PROCEDURE, not of the panel, the thresholds, or the model's expressive power. BUT NO HONEST CRITERION WILL FIND THEM, and this is the part that matters. The gate-passing vectors fit 343 to 792 percent worse in cross-validation than the CV optimum -- 0.3895 against 0.0437 on seed 0, 0.1662 against 0.0375 on seed 1, 0.1900 against 0.0412 on seed 2. They are not CV-competitive by a small margin that better optimisation might close; they are three to eight times worse. This confirms and sharpens WSD80-SUR-104's old observation that gate-passing basins fit about 18 percent worse, and it means the gap cannot be closed by any criterion built on predictive accuracy alone. A PARAMETER SIGNATURE SEPARATES THE TWO REGIONS. The broad family's readout exponent sits EXACTLY on its 2.000 upper bound in every cross-validated fit examined, three of three, while gate-passing solutions place it at 0.594, 1.310 and 0.566 -- comfortably interior. The boundary scale differs the same way, log_k0 at 2.458, 3.130 and 1.638 under CV against -0.127, 2.066 and 0.051 for gate-passing. A parameter railed against its bound in every fit is a specification defect: the likelihood wants to go further and cannot.
reopen_condition: The pinned exponent is the concrete lead and is being tested by widening its bound. Beyond that, the honest framing of this project's central difficulty is now available: predictive accuracy and gate satisfaction are in genuine conflict on this panel, by a factor of three to eight in CV error, so a surrogate selected to predict well will not recommend the right mixture. Either the gates encode something the loss does not, in which case that something must enter the model as structure rather than be hoped for from selection, or the gates are miscalibrated. Do not resolve this by selecting on the gates.

title: BREAKS 40/44: the readout exponent was railed at its bound; freeing it gives 43/44
material_novelty: Acts on GEN-035's observation that the broad family's readout exponent sits exactly on its 2.0 upper bound in every cross-validated fit while gate-passing solutions place it interior. Sweeps the bound instead of theorising about it.
evidence: Single-target selection with the range penalty, 11 seeds. Bound 2.0: 40/44 with rmse 11/11, Regret@1 8/11, distance 10/11, gain error 11/11, and the exponent PINNED on 7 of 11 seeds. Bound 5.0: 40/44 with Regret@1 recovering to 10/11 but distance falling to 8/11, pinned 0 of 11. Bound 12.0: 43/44 -- rmse 11/11, REGRET@1 11/11, distance 10/11, gain error 11/11, pinned 0 of 11. So the 40/44 total that five structurally different configurations had reproduced was substantially a BOUND ARTEFACT: the likelihood wanted an exponent far above 2 and could not have it, and the resulting compromise cost the Regret@1 gate. This is the best score any configuration in this project has achieved and the first to break the barrier. THE OPTIMUM IS NOT WHAT IMPROVED. Mean recommended optimum is (0.0589, 0.4834) at bound 12.0 against a true (0.100, 0.500), essentially unchanged from bound 2.0's (0.0695, 0.4786), so the early-share underestimate GEN-028 identified survives. What changed is that the gates stopped being forced apart by a constraint the data was fighting.
