Re-measure the 300M side at the wider bound, since every 300M result in this registry was produced under the 2.0 cap and may be similarly constrained.

title: REFUTED: fitting the ordering effect on matched pairs is WORSE than reading it off a joint fit
material_novelty: Tests this project's own strongest standing recommendation, made after the horizon-by-replay panel proposed decomposing loss into an aggregate part A and an ordering part O: that having an aggregate-matched tied control for every untied policy should let us fit O directly, putting the whole statistical budget on the quantity that decides phase selection instead of on the aggregate, which dominates the joint objective by variance.
evidence: TESTED IN THREE PROGRESSIVELY STRONGER FORMS AND REFUTED IN ALL THREE. (1) WSD80 with a modelled A: the two-stage fit gives better pooled RMSE, 0.0048 to 0.0057 against the joint fit's 0.006 to 0.008, but no better gate score and optima drifting further from the truth, means around 0.054 early share against a true 0.100. WSD80 cannot in fairness test this: it has only 20 tied rows in 346, 6 percent, so A -- the harder function, the entire aggregate response -- is identified on 13 rows per training fold while O gets 326. (2) 300M with a modelled A, where tied coverage is 282 of 520 or 54 percent: two-stage is worse on BOTH pooled RMSE, 0.007482 against 0.005959, and the paired-gap diagnostic, 0.009720 against 0.007005. (3) 300M with OBSERVED differences, which is the strongest form and the one the recommendation actually described -- the control is a trained run, so o = L(untied) - L(tied) is data and carries no aggregate-model error at all. Direct-O still loses on gap RMSE on all three seeds: 0.007649 against 0.007031, 0.007428 against 0.006882, 0.007021 against 0.006990. Sign agreement is mixed, 0.866/0.887, 0.887/0.903 and 0.920/0.895, so direct-O wins one of three there. WHY, AND THE REASON GENERALISES. Differencing cancels noise only when the noise is COMMON to both members. Here the two members are independent training runs, so their errors do not cancel and the difference carries roughly sqrt(2) times the measurement noise while discarding the aggregate signal the joint model was using and the tied rows' information about theta. The observed gap has mean +0.001086 against a standard deviation of 0.017957 -- the signal is about 6 percent of its own spread -- so amplifying noise to remove a component that was not a confounder is a bad trade. MATCHED PAIRS ARE STILL THE RIGHT DIAGNOSTIC. GEN-012 uses exactly this differencing to MEASURE the phase contrast free of aggregate contamination, and that remains valid and valuable. The finding is narrow and specific: matched-pair differencing is a good instrument for measuring the ordering effect and a bad objective for fitting it.
reopen_condition: The A + O decomposition remains a correct DESCRIPTION of the loss and should stay in how we explain the model; what does not follow, and is now measured not to hold, is that fitting the two parts separately is better. Do not design the next panel around maximising matched-pair coverage for FITTING reasons -- the pairs earn their place as diagnostics and as the only clean way to state what the two-phase gain is, which is reason enough.

title: The exponent pinning is WSD80-specific; 300M is unconstrained and its numbers stand
material_novelty: Closes GEN-039's reopen condition, which flagged that every 300M result in this registry was produced with the readout exponent capped at 2.0 -- a cap WSD80 had just been shown to be fighting, worth three gate cells.
evidence: 300M IS NOT CONSTRAINED. At bound 2.0 the exponent pins on ONE of nine folds; at bound 12.0 it pins on NONE, and nested Uncheatable RMSE is unchanged -- 0.005909 against 0.005919, a difference of 0.00001 and well inside seed spread. Fitted exponents do reach 8.953 when allowed, so the wider box is used, but using it buys nothing. CONSEQUENCE: every 300M number already in this registry stands as recorded and no re-measurement is required. THE ASYMMETRY WITH WSD80 HAS A STRUCTURAL EXPLANATION, and it is the same fact that made the departures ablation a no-op there. WSD80 has two buckets in two families, one bucket each, so family_sums(near) equals near identically and the per-bucket departures block is an exact duplicate of the family-mean block -- measured difference 0.000e+00. The family-level exponent is therefore the ONLY flexibility that design has, and the likelihood pushes it against the bound: pinned on 7 of 11 seeds, and freeing it recovers three gate cells. On 300M the 39-bucket departures block absorbs that pressure, so the exponent never has to strain and the bound never binds.
reopen_condition: This predicts that the pinning would return on any panel with few buckets per family, which is worth checking before running a new small-support swarm: if a design has one bucket per family the departures block is dead weight and the family exponent carries everything. Consider whether such panels should drop the departures block outright, since on WSD80 it is provably contributing nothing.

title: Two promotable candidates, and the choice is between gate count and the recommended mixture
material_novelty: Isolates the last remaining trade. Both candidates share the committed design, no multi-start, range-penalised selection and the widened exponent bound; they differ in ONE thing, whether theta is selected against the single primary target or jointly across all 29.
evidence: CANDIDATE A -- single-target selection. 43/44 over 11 seeds: rmse 11/11, Regret@1 11/11, distance 10/11, gain error 11/11. Mean recommended optimum (0.0589, 0.4834) against a true (0.100, 0.500), so the EARLY SHARE IS 41 PERCENT TOO LOW. CANDIDATE B -- multi-target selection. Through four seeds at the widened bound it is 16/16 with optima (0.095,0.470), (0.095,0.470), (0.092,0.470) and (0.098,0.470); at the original bound the full eleven-seed tally was 40/44 with mean optimum (0.1041, 0.4620), so the EARLY SHARE IS ESSENTIALLY EXACT and the late share is 8 percent low. The widened bound leaves B unchanged seed for seed, confirming B was never pinned -- consistent with GEN-043, since multi-target selection identifies the exponent from 29 targets and never has to strain it. THE GATE COUNT AND THE DEPLOYED DECISION DISAGREE, and it is worth being precise about why. Distance passes for both but by different routes: A is wrong mainly in early share, 0.041 off, and right in late, 0.017 off; B is right in early, 0.004 off, and wrong in late, 0.038 off. The Euclidean distance gate cannot tell these apart, so it scores both as passing while they recommend materially different mixtures. THE CHARTER SETTLES IT. The stated goal is a surrogate that SELECTS GOOD TWO-PHASE OPTIMA, not one that maximises a gate tally, and the early share is the phase-specific decision the surrogate exists to make. On that criterion B is the model to promote despite the lower total, and A is the better predictor. This is the same asymmetry GEN-008 measured -- sharing theta across targets sharpens selection while blurring fit -- now appearing in the recommended mixture rather than in Regret@1.
reopen_condition: Report both, and report the optimum by COORDINATE rather than as a distance, since the aggregate hides a 10-fold difference in early-share accuracy between two configurations the gate scores as equivalent. If a single model must be chosen, choose B on the charter's own terms. Before that, finish B's eleven-seed tally at the widened bound and re-run the 300M side and the negative controls under B, all of which were measured under A's single-target estimator.

title: CORRECTION: candidate B fixes the optimum and the gates but FAILS the control gate systematically
material_novelty: Completes candidate B's validation at the widened exponent bound, including the negative controls, which GEN-044 recommended B for promotion without having measured.
evidence: B AT THE WIDENED BOUND IS EXCELLENT ON GATES AND OPTIMUM. Through ten seeds it scores 39/40 -- rmse 10/10, Regret@1 10/10, distance 9/10, gain error 10/10 -- with mean recommended optimum (0.1023, 0.4644) against a true (0.100, 0.500). Mean absolute early-share error is 0.0083, essentially exact, against candidate A's 0.041. The widened bound also repaired B's seed-4 distance failure, which at bound 2.0 gave 3/4 at optimum (0.120,0.445) and now gives 4/4 at (0.105,0.463). BUT IT FAILS THE FROZEN NEGATIVE-CONTROL GATE, AND NOT MARGINALLY. Under B, gab predicts phase gain of +0.010068 to +0.013271 and twitterAAE +0.012067 to +0.012916, against a 0.005 limit, ON ALL FIVE SEEDS. That is 24 of 26 controls holding, against candidate A's 26 of 26 and the committed model's 23 of 26. The failures are SYSTEMATIC rather than seed-dependent, so B reliably manufactures roughly 0.012 BPB of phase gain on two broad-text metrics where the truth is essentially zero. THE MECHANISM IS THE SAME SHARING THAT FIXES THE OPTIMUM. B differs from A in one thing only: theta is selected jointly across all 29 targets rather than against the primary alone. That sharing borrows strength and sharpens the recommended mixture -- the effect GEN-008 measured as a 38-fold Regret@1 improvement -- and it also propagates code-driven phase structure onto targets that have none. THE GAP IS NARROWER THAN THE TALLY SUGGESTS. The same two metrics are the marginal ones under A too, at +0.004188 and +0.004954 against the 0.005 limit, so BOTH candidates place substantial phase gain on gab and twitterAAE and A merely squeaks under. The control gate is doing real work and both models are strained on the same two targets, which are the high-variance social-text metrics GEN-005 already flagged.
reopen_condition: NEITHER CANDIDATE IS PROMOTABLE AS IT STANDS and GEN-044's recommendation of B is qualified accordingly: A satisfies every frozen gate but recommends an early share 41 percent below the truth, and B recommends the right mixture while violating a frozen gate by two-and-a-half fold on two targets. Do not resolve this by dropping the offending targets from the selection set after seeing which ones fail -- that is post-hoc and would invalidate the control. The legitimate move is to preregister a selection-target set on deployment grounds, before looking at controls, and re-measure. Note also that 1/std-squared weighting already down-weights these two metrics, so the leak is not that they dominate selection; it is that the shared phase columns are not cleanly separated from the aggregate ones, which returns to the identifiability question.

title: PREREGISTRATION: select theta on the deployment targets (code only), stated before measuring
material_novelty: GEN-046 left two candidates, neither promotable: single-target theta satisfies every frozen gate but recommends an early share 41 percent low, while multi-target theta recommends almost exactly the right mixture and violates the negative-control gate by two-and-a-half fold on two broad-text metrics, on every seed. GEN-046 explicitly ruled out the tempting repair -- dropping the two offending metrics after seeing which failed -- as post-hoc. This registers the legitimate alternative BEFORE any measurement.
evidence: THE DECLARATION. Select theta on the DEPLOYMENT TARGETS: the primary evaluation, Programming Languages BPB, together with its two positive controls, github_python and github_cpp. Three targets. The grounds are stated without reference to which controls failed: a surrogate is built to choose a mixture that minimises the objective a deployment actually optimises, so the parameters shared across targets should be identified from those targets. This is the same principle the round charter already mandates for the 39-bucket panel, where family weighting is required so that Table-9 components cannot swamp Uncheatable; here it is applied to the two-bucket panel. Everything else is held identical to candidates A and B: committed power-law design, no multi-start, range-penalised selection, readout exponent range widened to 12, same folds, same heads. THE MECHANISM THIS PREDICTS, and the reason for expecting it to work. Candidate A selects theta against the primary alone, so theta is code-shaped and the phase columns it produces are ones broad-text heads cannot use; their non-negative amplitudes go to approximately zero and predicted phase gain on broad text is approximately zero -- A holds 26 of 26 controls. Candidate B asks theta to explain 26 broad-text metrics as well, so theta acquires phase structure that improves broad-text FIT, and that structure then yields nonzero predicted gain on exactly those metrics -- B holds 24 of 26 and fails systematically. The leak is therefore caused by theta being asked to explain broad text, not by broad text dominating the sum. EXPECTED SIGNATURES, recorded in advance so the result can falsify them. (1) Controls should hold at or near A's 26 of 26, because theta is never asked to explain a broad-text metric. (2) The recommended early share should improve on A's 0.059 toward B's 0.102, because strength is borrowed across three correlated code targets rather than one. (3) The acceptance tally should land between A's 43/44 and B's 39/40. IF (1) FAILS the mechanism above is wrong and the leak is not about which targets theta explains. IF (2) FAILS then B's optimum advantage comes from the breadth of the 29-target sum rather than from borrowing strength among related targets, and the A/B conflict is irreducible within this family. ||| OUTCOME, measured once against the signatures as registered and not amended. SIGNATURE 1 FALSIFIED, and decisively. Controls hold on 17 of 26, against candidate A's 26 and candidate B's 24. Selecting theta on code targets ONLY -- never asking it to explain a single broad-text metric -- made broad-text control violations MUCH WORSE, which refutes the stated mechanism outright. The leak is not caused by theta being asked to explain broad text. SIGNATURE 2 FALSIFIED. Mean recommended early share is 0.0507 against A's 0.0589 and B's 0.1023, on a true 0.100 -- worse than the one-target candidate rather than better. SIGNATURE 3 FALSIFIED. Acceptance is 38/44, below both A's 43/44 and B's 39/40: rmse 11/11, Regret@1 9/11, distance 9/11, gain error 9/11. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS. On two of eleven seeds the fit COLLAPSES to zero early share, optimum (0.000,0.545) and (0.000,0.542), and those seeds carry the control inflation -- eight of the nine failing controls fail on 1 of 5 seeds and only barely, 0.0051 to 0.0063 against the 0.005 limit, with only wikipedia_english failing 4 of 5. So this is a seed-dependent identification failure, not a systematic bias like B's. THE TARGET COUNT IS NOT MONOTONE, which is the substantive finding: one target gives 26/26 controls and no collapses, three give 17/26 and two collapses, twenty-nine give 24/26 and no collapses. Adding two correlated code targets to the primary makes theta LESS identified, not more; only the full breadth of twenty-nine restores it. THE PREREGISTERED CONCLUSION THEREFORE APPLIES AS WRITTEN: signature 2's failure condition states that B's optimum advantage comes from the breadth of the 29-target sum rather than from borrowing strength among related targets, and that the A/B conflict is IRREDUCIBLE within this family. That is now the recorded position.
reopen_condition: Do not search over further selection sets on this panel -- the preregistration was worth exactly one measurement and it came back negative on all three counts. The finding that target count is non-monotone in identification quality is the part worth following: it predicts that what matters is the DIVERSITY of the targets constraining theta rather than their number or their content, and that is testable by selecting on random subsets of the 29 at matched sizes. If diversity is what identifies theta, the A/B conflict may be resolvable by choosing a diverse subset; if not, it is a property of the family and the honest report is that no configuration both recommends the right mixture and respects the control gate.

title: The 3e18 blocker STANDS: the fantasy optimum is untouched by everything this round promoted
material_novelty: Re-runs the raw-optimum audit that the standing 3e18 guidance is stated in, using the current model, to answer whether this round's improvements make a two-phase validation at 3e18 better founded than before.
evidence: THE FANTASY REPRODUCES EXACTLY. Free optimum on 300M Uncheatable predicts 0.876219, 0.876640 and 0.878766 BPB across three seeds against a best observed 0.951105 -- optimism of +0.0749, +0.0745 and +0.0723 BPB. The standing note recorded this pathology as predicting 0.83 to 0.88 against 0.955, so the current model sits squarely inside the previously documented failure. THE RANGE PENALTY, THIS ROUND'S PROMOTED CHANGE, DOES NOTHING HERE. With it on the same three seeds give 0.876432, 0.876750 and 0.878391 -- differences in the fourth decimal, and phase TV and distance-to-proportional likewise unchanged. The reason is structural and worth stating: range excess is evaluated over the PANEL'S designs, so it constrains predictions at observed policies. The free optimum sits TV 0.57 to 0.68 from proportional, far outside support, where the penalty has no purchase. It is an IN-SUPPORT SAFETY DEVICE, not an anti-optimism device for out-of-support optima. UNDER A TRUST REGION THE TWO-PHASE ARM SIMPLY ROUTES AROUND IT. Constraining the AGGREGATE to TV 0.05 from proportional, the two-phase optimum satisfies that constraint while driving PHASE TV to 0.599, 0.652 and 0.602, and claims 0.9148 against the one-phase arm's 0.9584 -- an asserted two-phase advantage of 0.044 BPB. The panel's own truth is the opposite: best observed tied is 0.951105 and best observed asymmetric is 0.955440, so no asymmetric policy beats the best tied. The model manufactures a large advantage the data says does not exist. BOTH ARMS ARE OPTIMISTIC BEYOND ANYTHING OBSERVED, which is a separate problem. At TV 0.20 the one-phase arm predicts 0.918 against a best observed 0.951. AND THE TRUST REGION IS ANCHORED IN THE WRONG PLACE: the best observed policy itself sits TV 0.503 from proportional and the panel median is 0.504, so budgets of 0.05 to 0.20 around proportional are far MORE restrictive than where the data actually lives, and the model extrapolates optimistically there too.
reopen_condition: The standing guidance is re-confirmed and should not be relaxed: do not validate a two-phase optimum at 3e18. What this round improved is real but orthogonal -- the model no longer produces catastrophic predictions, component regressions fell from five to one or three, and controls went from 23/26 to 26/26 -- so we are markedly more confident it will not BLOW UP, and no more confident about WHERE the two-phase optimum is. If a validation slot is spent, spend it on a one-phase or near-proportional tilt, treat the predicted value as an upper bound rather than an estimate, and anchor any trust region where the panel actually lives, around TV 0.5 from proportional, rather than at proportional itself.

title: The damage term is the one place per-phase materialized epochs are NOT separated
material_novelty: Audits, at the user's prompting, where the design actually distinguishes epochs materialized in the stable phase from epochs materialized in the decay phase, and where it silently blends them.
evidence: WHERE THE DESIGN DOES SEPARATE THE PHASES. The early-boundary kernel reads c0*w0, which is genuinely materialized stable-phase epochs. The benefit pair reads exposure at two horizons, so the phases are weighted differently. The free-signed late-share column reads w1 alone. WHERE IT DOES NOT, AND THIS IS THE GAP. Repetition damage is charged on exposure(phi_damage) = (c0+c1)[(1-phi)w0 + phi w1], a BLEND. Two consequences. First, that quantity is not an epoch count: true materialized exposure is c0*w0 + c1*w1, which the blend equals only at phi = c1/(c0+c1), measured at 0.202937 on WSD80 and 0.200000 on the 39-bucket panel. Since phi_damage is fitted freely, damage is generally charged on a quantity with no physical reading. Second and more important, one penalty on a blend cannot distinguish repetition incurred in the stable phase from repetition incurred in the decay phase, so it cannot express that late re-reading might be more harmful than early re-reading. A ONE-COLUMN PENALTY ON A BLEND ALSO CANNOT REVERSE A PREFERRED ORDERING, which is exactly the effect the horizon-by-replay panel established and which motivated this audit. AN EXACT ORDER-AWARE DECOMPOSITION EXISTS. Phase 0 precedes phase 1 and consumes the first full pass, so with m0 = c0*w0 and m1 = c1*w1: e0 = max(m0 - 1, 0) is repetition within the stable phase and e1 = max(m0 + m1 - 1, 0) - e0 is the part of the decay phase that is re-reading. Both are non-negative and they sum exactly to the total excess, so this is a decomposition rather than an approximation. ONE TEMPTING REPAIR IS A PROVABLE NO-OP, checked before building anything. Replacing the LATE benefit's exposure(1.0) = (c0+c1)w1 with the materialized c1*w1 changes nothing: c1/(c0+c1) is constant across buckets, at 0.202937 on WSD80, so the substitution is a single scalar factor k = 4.9276 and ((k x) + eps)^-gamma = k^-gamma (x + eps/k)^-gamma, absorbed by the free amplitude. This is the same class of error SUR-109 was killed for and GEN-025 nearly repeated. THE REAL CONTENT of separation is giving m0 and m1 SEPARATE AMPLITUDES: a power law does not commute with a linear blend, so two columns with two amplitudes strictly generalise one column with one.
reopen_condition: The fully separable design is under test: every exposure-derived feature rebuilt from m0 and m1, benefit split into two amplitudes, damage split order-aware, boundary unchanged since it already reads m0. It also DROPS two parameters, phi_near and phi_damage, because there is no blend left to place a horizon in. Note it does NOT vanish on the tied diagonal the way the current near/late pair does -- at w0 = w1 the two materialized counts stay in the fixed ratio c0/c1, so the split adds structure to the tied response as well, which is arguably a gain since even a tied policy splits its exposure across phases and the committed model is blind to that.

title: Evaluation was 16x slower than it needed to be, and most of that was my methodology
material_novelty: Prompted by the observation that design iteration had multi-hour turnaround. Profiled rather than guessed, and separates what was a code defect from what was a process defect.
evidence: PROFILE. One inner-objective evaluation cost 0.00961 s, and differential evolution spends 7560 of them per selection at popsize 12 and maxiter 70, so one selection took 1.2 minutes, one seed four selections, and an eleven-seed run 53 minutes. THE CODE DEFECT, worth 2.2x and free. fit_head was called 87 times per evaluation, once per fold per target, but everything in it except the non-negative solve depends only on the DESIGN: the orthonormal basis for the free block, the residualised columns, their norms, and the pseudo-inverse of the free block. None of that varies with the target, so on a 29-target objective it was recomputed 29 times identically. Splitting into a per-design prepare and a per-target solve gives identical results -- maximum prediction difference 8.882e-15 across all 29 targets, objective values agreeing to 1.84e-15 -- at 0.00440 s per evaluation. Batching the range penalty into one matmul over all targets and hoisting the per-fold standard deviations, which never depended on theta, are included. THE OPTIMISER BUDGET IS NOT FREE AND I NEARLY REPORTED THAT IT WAS. Halving to maxiter 35 reproduced the full-budget answer exactly on seeds 0 and 1 -- inner objective 20.8642 against 20.8641, identical recommended optimum -- but on seed 2 it landed in a WORSE basin, 20.9762 against 20.5896, while the QUARTER budget matched full at 20.5894. So the cheaper budget is not reliably equivalent; this is the same multi-basin behaviour this project has repeatedly found in the WSD80 objective. THE PROCESS DEFECT WAS THE LARGER ONE. I had been running eleven-seed full-budget sweeps to answer exploratory design questions. Eleven seeds and full budget are validation settings; a comparison between two designs needs only enough seeds to separate them, and both arms share whatever optimiser weakness a cheaper budget introduces. MEASURED COST MODEL: 53 minutes originally, 12 minutes batched at half budget over eleven seeds, 3 minutes batched at half budget over three seeds. Sixteen-fold on the iteration loop.
reopen_condition: Adopt as standing practice: design COMPARISONS run three seeds at half budget with the batched solver, matched across arms; reported numbers and promotion claims run eleven seeds at full budget. Never mix the two in one tally, which is the defect GEN-006 was withdrawn for. The batched solver should be used everywhere since it is bit-identical; the reduced budget must never appear in a reported result.

title: Per-phase separation of exposure features fails three ways on WSD80, and the panel cannot test it
material_novelty: Tests the user's proposal to make per-phase materialized epochs separable everywhere they enter as features. Three constructions, each fixing a defect found in the previous one, all measured against the committed blended design on matched settings using the fast comparison loop from GEN-052.
evidence: CONSTRUCTION 1, fully separable benefit and damage: interior RMSE 0.0385 against the blended 0.0071, 1/4 gates. CONSTRUCTION 2, benefit left accumulated and only the damage argument split into hill(e0) + hill(e1): 0.0284, 0/4. CONSTRUCTION 3, phase-ATTRIBUTED damage, hill(e_total) partitioned by where the excess was incurred so the two columns sum exactly to the blended damage: 0.0116, 1/4 on the seed measured. Each fix improved matters -- 0.0385, 0.0284, 0.0116 -- and none reached the blended 0.0071. THE PRINCIPLE THE FAILURES TAUGHT, which is general and worth keeping. Exposure ACCUMULATES, so a readout of a phase-weighted total is not a sum of per-phase readouts: f(m0 + m1) differs from a0 f(m0) + a1 f(m1) by 2.8 to 4.4 fold on realistic values, and construction 1 fails for that reason. The same trap recurs one level down in construction 2: the excess itself does decompose additively, e0 + e1 = e_total, but HARM is a nonlinear function of the total, so hill(e0) + hill(e1) is not hill(e_total). Measured in-sample at matched theta, construction 2 fit WORSE on 7 of 8 random draws despite carrying two extra columns, which is only possible if its columns do not span the one they replaced. THE RULE: split the ATTRIBUTION of a nonlinear effect, never the ARGUMENT. Construction 3 obeys it and nests the committed model exactly, verified at 2.776e-17. A SECONDARY FINDING, since it was my first hypothesis and it was wrong: separating the phases does expose the readout singularity far more often -- a single phase weight is exactly zero on 27 or 28 of 692 entries against 2 for the blend, and at gamma 12 with the 1e-2 offset floor that is a column value of 1e24 -- but replacing the power law with the bounded saturating readout did NOT repair construction 1, which is how the accumulation explanation was found instead.
reopen_condition: WSD80 CANNOT TEST THIS IDEA and its failure here is not evidence against it. The mechanism phase-attributed damage exists to capture is the ordering REVERSAL that the horizon-by-replay panel established, and that reversal is a function of horizon and replay state; WSD80 is a single horizon at a single support condition, so there is no reversal present for the extra parameters to earn their keep on. The panel also has two buckets with a globally constant phase ratio, so per-phase materialized epochs carry little beyond the blend. Retest construction 3 on the horizon-by-replay panel, where the effect it targets actually varies, and judge it there.

title: PREREGISTERED: Stage 1 independent atomic fits on the no-replay two-bucket full-pool panel
material_novelty: Foundation reset. Previous rounds identified every mechanism simultaneously on panels that confound repetition, bucket count and objective count. This starts at the simplest identifiable corner: NO forced replay, TWO buckets, ONE atomic objective, fitting each of 23 dataset-level atomic BPB targets and each of 4 horizons independently before anything is shared or pooled.
evidence: DATA, VERIFIED BEFORE REGISTERING. 500 full-pool rows = 4 horizons x 125 coordinates, from the canonical loader load_observations with support_id == 'full'. Horizons 1.00139, 1.91889, 3.92167 and 7.40819 B materialized tokens, 125 coordinates each. 23 dataset-level atomic BPB targets from starcoder_wsd80_atomic_metrics.ATOMIC_METRICS; micro and macro aggregates excluded. ZERO-EXCESS ASSERTION PASSES: total StarCoder epochs span 0.000000 to 0.034207, so no row reaches even 3.5 percent of one pass; starcoder_support_wraps is False everywhere and starcoder_support_fraction is 1.0 everywhere. Repetition mechanisms are therefore not merely inactive but roughly thirtyfold away from activating, which makes this a valid ablation setting rather than an assumed one. A PANEL PROPERTY WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT CHANGES WHAT IS IDENTIFIABLE: the phase-0 share of materialized epochs varies from 0.0000 to 1.0000 across 323 distinct values here, whereas on the older WSD80 panel that share was a GLOBAL CONSTANT of 0.797 fixed by the schedule. GEN-054 found that per-phase separation of exposure features could not be tested on the old panel for exactly that reason; on this panel it can. THE COMPARISON, all on identical folds and optimizer budgets: (a) GEN with repetition damage HARD-DISABLED rather than fitted, since the committed damage feature uses a fitted phase blend and is not a valid no-replay ablation; exact materialized epochs are available here as starcoder_phase_0_epochs and starcoder_phase_1_epochs and will be used in place of any derived exposure; (b) effective-exposure DSP; (c) retained power law; (d) HPR where compatible; (e) a spatial-CV smooth surface as an EXPRESSIVITY REFERENCE ONLY, never a candidate. VALIDATION: spatial or leave-region-out cross-validation, never random-row, because the 125 coordinates form a dense grid and random splits measure interpolation between near neighbours. REPORTED PER TARGET AND HORIZON: RMSE, Spearman, Regret@1 and Regret@5, selected-policy regret, tied and untied optimum coordinates, estimated global two-phase gain, interior versus boundary breakdown, and bootstrap stability. EXPECTED SIGNATURE, recorded so it can fail: if the response mechanism is adequate, independent per-target fits should beat the intercept on the large majority of the 23 targets at every horizon, and the recommended tied and untied optima should be stable under the spatial folds. IF INDEPENDENT FITS FAIL, the state or response mechanism is inadequate and no replay term may be added to conceal it. ||| OUTCOME. THE MECHANISM IS ADEQUATE ON THIS SETTING. A two-bucket exposure model -- a power-law readout of exact materialized StarCoder epochs plus a readout of the COMPLEMENT bucket's exposure, one non-negative amplitude each, both read at one fitted horizon -- beats an intercept on 92 of 92 target-horizons under leave-region-out spatial folds, with median out-of-fold RMSE at 0.457 of the intercept and a worst case of 0.888. It also beats the smooth quadratic EXPRESSIVITY REFERENCE on median, 0.457 against 0.516, and on 58 of 92 individual cells. So the surface is not merely smooth: a mechanism with two free nonlinear parameters captures more of it than a six-term polynomial, and does so while remaining extrapolable. A SELF-INFLICTED GAP THE SWEEP FOUND IMMEDIATELY, worth recording because it was invisible on the code targets. The first candidate built exposure from StarCoder epochs ALONE -- a single-bucket model on a two-bucket panel. On code targets it looked excellent, median 0.186 beating the intercept on 12 of 16, but on the 76 broad-text target-horizons it was INERT: median ratio exactly 1.000, beating the intercept only 5 times, because the non-negative amplitude on a useless column is driven to zero and only the intercept survives. Meanwhile the smooth reference beat the intercept on 72 of those 76, so real structure was present and the mechanism simply could not see it. Adding the complement readout, whose per-phase exposure is recovered from nemotron_max_total_epochs split by the schedule fractions, took broad text from 5/76 to 76/76 at median 0.491 and left code unchanged at 0.186 while lifting it to 16/16. THE COMPLEMENT POOL IS ABOUT 26 TIMES LARGER than StarCoder in epoch terms, so its exposure is small and slowly varying; a readout of it is a genuinely different feature rather than a rescaling of the StarCoder one. PHASE-SPLIT FAILS AGAIN AND THE REPLICATION MATTERS. Giving the two phases separate amplitudes on the StarCoder readout scores median 1.025 and beats the intercept on only 16 of 92, worse than the accumulated single readout at every level. GEN-054 reached the same conclusion on the older panel but could not distinguish the idea from the panel, because there the phase-0 share of materialized epochs was a global constant of 0.797. HERE that share varies across the whole unit interval over 323 distinct values, so the phases are genuinely distinguishable and the split still loses. That is an independent replication of the accumulation principle: exposure adds up, and a readout of a phase-weighted total is not a sum of per-phase readouts. THE SMOOTH REFERENCE FAILS ON CODE, median 1.054 and beating the intercept on only 4 of 16, which is worth stating because it bounds what smoothness alone can do: under leave-region-out folds a quadratic cannot extrapolate the code surface at all.
reopen_condition: Fit every one of the 23 targets and report all of them; selecting favourable metrics after seeing results invalidates the stage. atomic_metric_raw_optima.csv is diagnostic only -- its extrema are one-seed selection-biased grid minima and must not be used as ground truth. The 564 preregistered calibration repeats remain unlaunched, so no calibrated coordinate-dependent likelihood may be claimed at this stage.

title: PREREGISTERED: Stage 2 multiple atomic objectives, and Stage 3 uncertainty treatment
material_novelty: Registers stages 2 and 3 before stage 1 is scored, so that the sharing and uncertainty comparisons cannot be shaped by stage 1 outcomes.
evidence: STAGE 2, on identical folds and optimizer budgets: independent nonlinear geometry per target; fully shared nonlinear geometry with per-target heads; ONE preregistered partially pooled form with strong shrinkage or a small fixed-rank target deviation; and constrained versus sign-unconstrained linear heads as a diagnostic. The question to answer is WHERE a failure originates -- the shared representation, the target head, or the horizon coupling -- and no unconstrained neural representation is to be tried as a shortcut. PRIOR EVIDENCE THIS TESTS: GEN-008 found sharing across targets refuted on the WSD80 gate, GEN-046 found that sharing sharpens the recommended mixture while transferring roughly 0.012 BPB of false phase gain onto two broad-text controls, and GEN-047's preregistered attempt to fix that by restricting the selection set failed all three of its stated signatures. The open question is whether false transfer is a property of sharing itself or of the particular targets shared across. STAGE 3: continue modelling EXPECTED BPB and optimise predicted mean BPB; do NOT substitute a policy-dependent Z-score for the target. Compare unweighted raw-BPB fitting, target-noise-scaled multi-target selection with a preregistered shrunk scale, and robust or heteroskedastic likelihoods only to the extent the repeat data supports. Use a variance floor with Student-t or robust-loss sensitivity. Report decisions in raw BPB and in noise-standardised units SEPARATELY, since a treatment that merely rescales the loss changes neither the argmin nor the selection and must not be credited as if it did. FROZEN BEFORE SCORING: every candidate's equations, folds, hyperparameters and ablations are frozen before being scored on the completed 280-run selected-policy confirmation panel, and nothing is fitted directly to those confirmation outcomes. ||| STAGE 2 OUTCOME, 4 horizons x 23 targets, identical spatial folds and optimiser budgets. NO FALSE PHASE TRANSFER, AND THIS IS THE STAGE'S MAIN RESULT. Sharing the nonlinear geometry across all 23 objectives predicts a maximum two-phase gain of +0.00000 BPB with non-negative heads and +0.00001 with free-sign heads, across every horizon and every target. The panel's truth is that no full-pool selected policy has a positive fresh two-phase gain, so the shared model correctly declines to invent one. This CONTRASTS SHARPLY with GEN-046, where sharing on the older WSD80 panel transferred roughly 0.012 BPB of false phase gain onto two broad-text controls and broke a frozen gate on every seed. The controlled difference between the two settings is REPETITION: that panel sits at 4.79 epochs at its optimum, this one at most 0.034. The natural reading, which stages 3 and 4 can test, is that false transfer is a property of the repetition regime rather than of sharing itself. SHARING IS NOT FREE, AND THE COST IS FAMILY-SPECIFIC. Median out-of-fold RMSE ratios across horizons: independent with non-negative heads gives code 0.163 and broad 0.502; shared with non-negative heads gives code 0.675 and broad 0.490. So sharing costs the CODE family a factor of four while marginally helping broad text, which is what one would expect when 76 of 92 target-horizons are broad-text and the shared geometry is pulled toward them. The cost vanishes at the longest horizon -- at 7.408B, independent gives code 0.122 and broad 0.309 against shared 0.133 and 0.318 -- so the conflict is horizon-dependent and weakest where the signal is strongest. NON-NEGATIVITY ON THE HEADS IS LOAD-BEARING, not a modelling preference. Free-sign heads are catastrophic in two cells: at 3.922B shared free-sign reaches a broad-text ratio of 7.608 and an overall 6.996, and at 7.408B independent free-sign reaches 4.899 on broad text, both far worse than simply predicting the mean. The constraint that makes the terms interpretable is also what keeps the fit stable.
reopen_condition: The confirmation panel is a scoring set, not a fitting set. Any candidate whose form or hyperparameters are adjusted after seeing confirmation scores must be re-registered and re-scored, or reported as exploratory only.

title: CORRECTION: the Stage 1/2 model was SINGLE-INDEX and structurally could not express any two-phase gain
material_novelty: Found by taking seriously the observation that atomic optima are often interior and often untied, then checking whether the model could represent that at all.
evidence: THE DEFECT. Both readouts in the Stage 1/2 two-bucket model use ONE shared horizon, so with f0 and f1 the schedule's phase fractions, StarCoder exposure is C_sc * u and complement exposure is C_c * (K - u) for the single scalar u = (1-phi) f0 p0 + phi f1 p1. Predicted loss therefore depends on the policy ONLY THROUGH u. Measured rank correlation between the two readouts is -1.000000 at every parameter setting tried. Every untied policy shares its u with a tied one, so the model cannot express ANY two-phase advantage, and its predicted gain is identically +0.00000 BY CONSTRUCTION. WHAT THIS WITHDRAWS. ATOM-002 reported that sharing geometry across 23 objectives produced no false phase transfer, maximum predicted gain +0.00001, and read that as the model correctly declining to invent gain where the panel has none. THAT READING IS A TAUTOLOGY and is withdrawn: the model could not have produced a non-zero gain under any circumstances, so the measurement says nothing about transfer. The Stage 2 fit and head findings stand -- sharing costs the code family fourfold, non-negativity is load-bearing -- because those do not depend on phase expressiveness. WHY IT MATTERS HERE RATHER THAN BEING A TECHNICALITY. Measured on the panel's own raw grid minima: 77 of 92 atomic optima are INTERIOR rather than pure corners, and 37 of 92 are UNTIED. Common optima include (0.000, 0.050), (0.000, 0.025) and (0.000, 0.100) -- no code early, a little code late -- which is exactly the two-phase pattern a single-index model cannot represent. A CAUTION ABOUT THE OBVIOUS DIAGNOSTIC. Counting how often a candidate PLACES an untied optimum is misleading: the single-index two-bucket model appears to place one on 45 of 92, purely because many (p0,p1) pairs share the optimal u and the grid argmin resolves the tie arbitrarily. Predicted GAIN is the honest structural measure and it is identically zero. THE FIX AND ITS COST. Reading each bucket at TWO horizons gives two independent linear directions -- rank correlation between the two StarCoder readouts falls from -1.000000 to +0.515601 -- and makes untied optima representable. Measured over all 92 target-horizons: two-horizon locates the empirical optimum better, median distance 0.061 against two-bucket's 0.100 and the smooth quadratic's 0.141, and expresses a non-zero gain, median +0.00005. It FITS WORSE, median out-of-fold ratio 0.517 against 0.457, beating the intercept on 90 of 92 rather than 92 of 92. THE SMOOTH REFERENCE NEVER PLACES AN UNTIED OPTIMUM AT ALL, 0 of 92, despite fitting comparably at 0.516 -- so smoothness buys error but not phase structure.
reopen_condition: This is the accuracy-versus-selection tension again, now isolated in the cleanest possible setting -- no repetition, two buckets, one objective -- and with a structural rather than statistical explanation: the second horizon is exactly what makes untied optima representable, and it is what costs generalisation. Grind this before adding anything else. The immediate questions are whether the second horizon can be regularised or partially pooled so that expressiveness is kept without the fit cost, and whether its benefit concentrates on the 37 untied target-horizons rather than being spread evenly, which would say the extra direction is being used for what it was added for.

title: The second horizon does NOT earn its keep where it was added for; it fixes an argmin degeneracy instead
material_novelty: Tests ATOM-003's own reopen condition. The second horizon was added to make untied optima representable, so if that mechanistic story is right its advantage over the single-index model should CONCENTRATE on the target-horizons whose empirical optimum is untied and be absent where the optimum is tied.
evidence: THE BENEFIT CONCENTRATES ON THE WRONG CELLS, by a factor of twelve. On the 37 target-horizons whose empirical optimum is UNTIED -- the cells the second horizon exists to serve -- median distance to the empirical optimum improves only from 0.0550 to 0.0500, an improvement of 0.0050, and the two-horizon model is closer on just 16 of 37, worse than a coin flip. On the 55 TIED cells the same change improves distance from 0.1414 to 0.0820, an improvement of 0.0594. So the extra direction buys generic flexibility rather than phase structure, and the mechanistic justification given for it is refuted. THE FIT COST IS CONCENTRATED THE SAME WAY, which corroborates the reading: out-of-fold ratio worsens by only 0.0077 on untied cells against 0.0604 on tied cells. THE LIKELY EXPLANATION IS THE TIE-BREAKING ARTIFACT AGAIN, and it also explains a number that otherwise looks backwards. The single-index two-bucket model locates the optimum BETTER on untied cells, 0.0550, than on tied cells, 0.1414, which makes no sense as a modelling fact. It makes sense as a degeneracy: on a single-index surface every policy sharing the optimal scalar u is an equal minimum, so the grid argmin resolves the tie arbitrarily and lands off the diagonal even when the truth is tied. Adding a second horizon removes the degeneracy, so most of its apparent improvement is the disappearance of an arbitrary tie-break rather than the capture of phase structure. WHAT REMAINS OPEN. Neither candidate represents the untied optima convincingly: the best available is a median distance of 0.0500 with the improvement over single-index reaching fewer than half the untied cells. The 37 untied atomic optima, in the simplest possible setting with no repetition, two buckets and one objective at a time, are still not explained by any mechanism tried.
reopen_condition: Do not promote the second horizon as a phase mechanism on this evidence. Two separable questions follow and should not be merged. First, the argmin degeneracy is a reporting hazard independent of any model: single-index candidates should have their recommended optimum reported as the SET of minimising policies, or projected onto the tied diagonal, rather than as an arbitrary grid cell. Second, the untied optima need a mechanism that actually targets them -- the natural candidates are a term that depends on phase ORDER rather than on any weighting of accumulated exposure, since every exposure-weighting scheme tried so far reduces to indices that tie untied policies to tied ones.

title: The accuracy-versus-selection conflict is present at the FOUNDATION, not caused by repetition or complexity
material_novelty: Tests ATOM-004's proposed remedy: a term encoding phase ORDER rather than any weighting of accumulated exposure. Late StarCoder absorption is gated by how much complement was seen early, so the term is a product of a phase-1 quantity with a function of phase-0 quantities and cannot be written as a function of any single weighted sum.
evidence: THE GATE IS NOT A WEIGHTING AND IT WORKS AS INTENDED WHEN USED. At a hand-chosen parameter setting on the primary code target the gated surface places an untied optimum at (0.270, 1.000) against a best tied (0.445, 0.445), an implied two-phase gain of +0.025241 BPB. So the structure needed to express phase behaviour is present, reachable, and produces exactly the kind of recommendation the panel's untied optima would require. THE GATE IS ALSO GENUINELY PREFERRED ON CODE TARGETS. Fitted non-negative amplitudes show the gated column and the plain-exposure column are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE and which one survives depends on the target family: on Programming Languages, GitHub C++ and GitHub Python the plain-exposure amplitude is exactly 0 and the gate carries the signal at 7.18e-03, 9.13e-03 and 8.89e-03; on ArXiv Computer Science and ArXiv Physics the gate is exactly 0 and plain exposure carries it. So the gate is not dead weight -- it wins outright wherever code is the target. BUT CROSS-VALIDATED SELECTION NEVER CHOOSES A PARAMETER SETTING THAT USES IT FOR PHASE. At every selected theta the predicted two-phase gain is +0.00000, on tied and untied cells alike. On the 23 untied cells the gate improves the recommended optimum not at all, 0.0500 against the single-index model's 0.0500, and is closer on only 3 of 23. Its distance improvement instead lands on the tied cells, 0.1760 to 0.1011, which is the same tie-breaking artifact ATOM-004 identified rather than phase structure. ONE HONEST QUALIFICATION: on the specific target inspected the empirical optimum is (1.000, 1.000), TIED, so declining the gate is correct there and the +0.025241 gain at the hand-chosen setting is a fantasy. The failure is not that selection declines the gate everywhere; it is that selection declines it on the untied cells too. THE PATTERN NOW HOLDS ACROSS EVERY CANDIDATE THIS ROUND AND IS THE POINT. Two horizons, phase-split readouts and an order gate are all expressible, all capable of untied optima, and all left unused by a criterion that scores held-out error. Expressing phase structure does not reduce fold error, so nothing that selects on fold error will choose it. This reproduces, in the SIMPLEST SETTING THAT EXISTS -- no forced replay at 0.034 epochs, two buckets, one atomic objective at a time -- the accuracy-versus-selection conflict previously measured on the repetition panel, where gate-satisfying parameter vectors existed but fitted 343 to 792 percent worse. THE CONFLICT IS THEREFORE NOT AN ARTEFACT of repetition, of many buckets, or of many objectives. It is a property of selecting a mixture surrogate on predictive error.
reopen_condition: The foundation reset has answered its own question, and the answer forecloses a family of fixes rather than suggesting one. No amount of mechanism design will help while the criterion is held-out error, because the mechanisms are already expressible and already declined. The next move is on the CRITERION, and it must be preregistered before being scored: candidates include selecting on the accuracy of the aggregate-matched CONTRAST rather than on level error, which is the only quantity phase structure actually affects, and which the 280-run confirmation panel can score without being fitted to. Note that ATOM-004's separate reporting hazard stands independently -- single-index candidates must report the SET of minimising policies rather than an arbitrary grid cell.

title: PREREGISTERED: select theta on aggregate-matched CONTRAST accuracy instead of level error
material_novelty: ATOM-005 established that every phase mechanism tried is expressible and capable of untied optima, and that a criterion scoring held-out LEVEL error declines all of them, because expressing phase structure does not reduce level error. That forecloses further mechanism design and points at the criterion. This registers the change before any fitting.
evidence: THE CHANGE. Keep fitting the head on levels; change only what THETA is selected on. Instead of minimising held-out level error, minimise held-out error on the AGGREGATE-MATCHED CONTRAST, c = y - A(aggregate), where A is the tied response interpolated from the panel's tied rows. The contrast is the only quantity phase structure affects: two policies with the same aggregate differ only in ordering, so a criterion built on it cannot be satisfied by getting the aggregate level right. PANEL SUPPORT, CHECKED BEFORE REGISTERING. 26 of 125 rows per horizon are tied, spanning aggregates 0.000 to 1.000 in 26 distinct values, against 6 percent on the older WSD80 panel and 54 percent on the 39-bucket panel. Median nearest-tied aggregate mismatch for untied rows is 0.00000 -- exact matches exist -- with 78 of 99 untied rows matched within 0.01. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM GEN-042, WHICH FAILED AND MUST NOT BE REPEATED BLINDLY. There the ordering effect was made the FITTING TARGET, so the model was trained on differences of independent runs; differencing amplified noise by about root two while discarding the aggregate signal, and the observed gap was only about 6 percent of its own spread, so it lost on all three tests. Here the fitting target remains the level and only the SELECTION criterion changes, so the head still sees the full signal and no target is replaced by a difference. That distinction is the whole basis for expecting a different outcome and should be stated plainly in any report. EXPECTED SIGNATURES, recorded in advance so the result can falsify them. (1) Contrast-selected theta should produce a NON-ZERO predicted two-phase gain, where every level-selected theta in ATOM-003 through ATOM-005 produced exactly +0.00000. (2) The improvement should land on the 23 UNTIED cells, where level selection improved the recommended optimum not at all, 0.0500 against 0.0500. (3) It should COST held-out level accuracy; if level error does not worsen, the criterion is not doing what it claims and the result is suspect rather than good. IF (1) FAILS the criterion is not the binding constraint and the obstruction is deeper than selection. IF (1) HOLDS BUT (2) FAILS the model expresses phase structure in the wrong place, which would implicate the mechanism after all. ||| OUTCOME, measured once against the registered signatures. A FIRST IMPLEMENTATION WAS WRONG AND THE RESULT EXPOSED IT IMMEDIATELY: subtracting a common reference from both prediction and observation cancels, so the contrast criterion reduced algebraically to the level criterion and reproduced the level numbers to the last decimal. The corrected form makes the model reproduce the contrast against ITS OWN tied baseline. SIGNATURE 3 CONFIRMED, so the criterion does bite: held-out level fit worsens from 0.1692 to 0.2141 for two-horizon and from 0.2103 to 0.3591 for gated. SIGNATURE 2 FAILED DECISIVELY and it was the one that mattered: median distance on the 23 untied cells RISES from 0.0500 to 0.0850 for two-horizon and from 0.0743 to 0.1450 for gated, with tied cells also worsening, so this is a loss everywhere rather than a trade. SIGNATURE 1 RESTED ON A PREMISE OF MINE THAT WAS PARTLY WRONG, which matters for interpretation: I registered that every level-selected theta gave exactly +0.00000 gain. True for GATED -- median +0.00000, maximum +0.00023, non-zero on 8 of 46 -- but NOT for two-horizon, which under ordinary level selection already gives non-zero gains on 32 of 46 with a maximum of +0.01086. Level selection was never uniformly blind to phase. THE REGISTERED FALSIFICATION LOGIC APPLIES: signature 1 holding while signature 2 fails implicates the MECHANISM rather than the criterion.
reopen_condition: Do not try further criterion variants on this panel; one preregistered criterion was measured once and it lost on every axis. The corrected reading of the whole ATOM sequence is narrower and more useful than the one ATOM-005 recorded: the two-horizon model DOES express phase gain under ordinary level selection, on 32 of 46 cells, so the obstruction is not that selection is blind to phase. What no candidate does is place those untied optima in the RIGHT PLACE -- the best median distance on untied cells is 0.0500, achieved by the single-index model whose untied placements are an argmin artifact. The open problem is therefore accuracy of the untied optimum's LOCATION, not the ability to express one, and ATOM-005's framing should be read with that correction.

title: PREREGISTERED: fit for the DECISION, and report the optimum as a region rather than a point
material_novelty: ATOM-006 narrowed the open problem: every candidate can express an untied optimum -- the two-horizon model does so on 32 of 46 cells under ordinary level selection -- but none PLACES it accurately, best median distance 0.0500 on untied cells, and that best is itself an argmin artifact of a single-index surface. Two changes follow that are about the decision rather than the surface, and neither has been tried in this project.
evidence: ROUTE A, TRUST-REGION REFITTING. Every fit so far minimises error over the WHOLE mixture square, but the quantity wanted is the location of one minimum. Fit globally, find the predicted optimum, reweight rows by a Gaussian kernel in policy space centred on it, refit, and iterate three times with a fixed bandwidth. This is deliberately NOT weighting by observed BPB, which would be circular and would chase a one-seed selection-biased grid minimum; the weights depend only on the model's own current recommendation and on policy coordinates, both of which are known without consulting held-out outcomes. ROUTE B, THE OPTIMUM AS A DISTRIBUTION. Report a REGION rather than a point by bootstrapping rows, refitting, and taking the argmin of each replicate. This addresses two things at once. It is the uncertainty treatment the round has not yet delivered, and it dissolves ATOM-004's reporting hazard, since a single-index surface has many equal minima and a distribution represents that tie set honestly where an arbitrary grid cell does not. EXPECTED SIGNATURES, recorded so they can fail. (1) Trust-region refitting should reduce median distance to the empirical optimum on the untied cells below 0.0500, the current best; if it does not, local accuracy near the optimum is not what is missing. (2) The bootstrap region should CONTAIN the empirical optimum at close to its nominal rate; systematic under-coverage would mean the surrogate is confidently wrong rather than merely imprecise, which is a different and worse failure. (3) Region WIDTH should be larger on untied cells than tied ones, because a surface with a genuine interior asymmetric minimum is harder to localise than one whose minimum sits on the diagonal; if width is flat across the two, the uncertainty is not tracking the thing it should. IF (1) FAILS AND (2) HOLDS the honest deliverable from this setting is a calibrated region rather than a point estimate, which is still a usable decision object and should be reported as the result rather than treated as a partial failure.
reopen_condition: Both routes are scored on the same spatial folds and matched optimiser budget as ATOM-004 through ATOM-006. The 564 calibration repeats remain unlaunched, so the bootstrap here resamples ROWS and captures fit uncertainty only; it does not and must not be described as capturing measurement noise in the underlying BPB values. Coverage is therefore a statement about the fit, not about the experiment.
